Some of The Evil Within's many positives:
- Perhaps the game's most fun aspect is its sublime combat system.
- Aesthetically pleasing and terrifying, through and through.
- The game is not at all easy, even with check points.
- Collectibles are not just meant to keep you busy; you are actually rewarded for finding them.
- New Game + offers new weapons and secrets that encourage replay.
- Having Debussy's Clair de Lune as the game's iconic musical track is icing on the cake.
My only three issues with the game:
- The protagonist lacks personality. It is as though he isn't even there. It could be possible they made him intentionally "blank" to make it easier for the player to imprint themselves onto him and be in his shoes, but I like my protagonists relatable and Sebastian Castellanos is definitely not so.
- Many questions are left unanswered. This is a real shame because the plot is quite intriguing. The player deserves at least some of their questions answered after going through so much trouble, even if the developer says they deliberately left much of the story hidden or vague to encourage player theories.
- The game explores one too many horror subgenres, to the point that it all feels a bit "experimental." A couple of chapters were almost entirely unnecessary.
Statistics: First try, finished the game on Survival (Normal) difficulty in
and
I owe at least half of these deaths to a certain boss. You know the one I mean.
Technical issues: The game has actually been quite stable for me. I only had one rather funny glitch (a boss followed me into a room where it wasn't supposed to and then disappeared) and only one occurrence of low frame-rate while opening a door transitioning from one part of a chapter to another. I'm guessing I have not experienced any of the technical difficulties others had been complaining about because I played it so many months after release, when most issues got patched, presumably.
Options: I recommend removing letterboxes from graphics>hardware options. Also, if your device can handle it, raise the framerate lock to 60 fps; the game will look considerably smoother.

I have nearly no complaints.
To start, the later previews of the game showed me that it probably wouldn't be the fantastic return of classic survival horror I'd been waiting for, and I was right (I'm a classic Resident Evil veteran; some I've beaten about twenty times).  But it can be scary.  What it does better than that I find, is tension.  It is one of the most tense games I've ever played.
The aiming system is clunky enough to feel more realistic than Resident Evil 4, though it (the game overall, and the aiming system) is in many ways similar to RE4.  Ammunition is limited but not finite the way it is in classic RE.
The game is not easy.  It is a challenge and almost never in a cheap way.
The boss fights are inventive.
Psychological horror has generally not felt threatening to me.  Silent Hill would add weird sounds and disturbing images and then no-thing would happen (and conversely actual danger would come without warning).  Evil Within however, has something to back up every threat it makes.
I've read some weird complaints about the level design and why would certain things be here or there.  The answer is simply that it's psychological horror.  Everything's gone mad.  The game establishes new rules of reality and then follows them, only breaking or bending them when a specific effect is desired.
Lastly, a couple of objective flaws:  the game ran like a slideshow on my PC initially, even with the lowest settings, and my PC has no trouble with any other game on the highest settings.  Following the patch I had no trouble whatever, so there's a good chance any complaints you've read regarding that, are outdated (or my experience would indicate so).  The other flaw is that the mechanics can at times be messy, which will cause you occasional frustration, and with this I'll lump in the worst sprinting system I've seen in a game to date.  When he runs out of stamina from running he just stands there catching his breath for ages.  Slowing down I understand, but if there's a fella with a chainsaw behind me, I can't think of any thing that'd keep me from moving.
8 or 9 of 10 I suppose?  Never done a review before.  Great game, I recommend it to most people.

If you are a true Deus Ex fan you should play this game. It has its faults certainly and I shall get the negative parts out of the way first before stating why I believe this game should be played. For starters it is clearly a port from a phone. The controls feel a bit off and it doesn't look any where near as good as a game relelased on PC in 2014 should look. There are jarring glitches such as when you do a melee takedown on someone whilst you are in cover and suddenly you are two metres from the corner to perform the cinematic takedown. The uncertainity of whether the AI will spot you, sometines you walk right in front without them noticing yet other times you are across the room with them facing in the other direction and they swing around shooting at you. There are optional micro transactions but they are certainly not required to play at all (I built my character exactly as I wanted to no problem) so I don't see them as an issue.
Now to list the redeeming qualities: it feels like a Deus Ex game. What I mean is the story, setting and protaganist all certainly feel like they are part of that universe. It's dialogue and the story itself are well written, the characters are engaging. *Slight spoiler alert* I wanted to know what happens next when the game finished to see where the story went next as well as as the next location was being heavily hinted at being Australia, a place I haven't explored in video game form (even though it would be a futuristic one of course).
All in all I believe you should play this game if you enjoy the world of Deus Ex and want to explore another part of it. Just make sure you get it when it's on sale.

Pros:
- Absolutely brilliant level design
Perfect setting for the exploratory nature of this game. Ambiance created with the sound and lighting made for suspense throughout. The changing and evolving environment beckoned for exploration.
- Amazing camera and point-of-view event queuing
Something could be evolving/changing just outside of your POV, so when you look back it could be completely different. The ques for changing the environment could be so simple as lingering too long, looking away for a fraction of a second, looking at something more than once, and of course the usual proximity.
- Phenomenal story
You play as a haunted artist with schizophrenic paranoia living with torturing delusions from his past. This probably represents the worst of schizophrenia and it’s terrifying. The art décor found around the house is inspired by famous artists which were thought to have suffer from some form of mental disorder (such as Francisco de Goya y Lucientes).
- Replay value
The player is sometimes presented multiple paths. I am too curious about all the paths I didn’t take and what could be found in those rooms.
- Creative and original
The developers did their research. The only jump scares are when you sort of die.
Cons:
- NONE, although I didn't want it to end!

Short version:
Fun game, bullet hell, play at your own pace, always challenging
In its current state, 7.5/10, but there are constant updates improving the game.
Worth buying for the price if you wnat straight action.
Long version:
This game has a lot of mechanical similarities to games like Realm of the Mad God, and gives you a lot of room to play the way you want with an impressive variety of classes that each have multiple unique mechanics and take time to master.
You cannot play each class the same way at all, giving you the opportunity to play the game an entirely new way whenever you feel like mixing it up.
The things that this game does really well are:
- Instant chllenging action
- Boss battles every minute or so depending on how quickly you progress through each stage
- A class to suit absolutely any playstyle
- It's hard to snowball into a game breaking monster, keeping the game engaging and challenging
- Gear upgrades drop as you progress, which combines with gold drops to make killing mobs very satisfying
- Random large elite mobs in stages, making for intense moments
The things this game doesn't do so well are:
- Repetitive bosses, that all seem to follow you around the same way
- Mobs seem to all follow the same design, and you just need to back up and shoot
- Character upgrades do not make a large difference to your character, and you end up paying a lot for very little gain
- Some classes are very slow to play, which goes against the theme of the game in my opinion
Some suggestions I have for the devs are:
- Give bosses more variety. Punish the player for not playing to the weaknesses of each individual boss and give the bosses phases in which they can bevery hard to kill, or very vulnerable. The key here is making each boss difficult and unique.
- Bring more variety to the regular grind in stages. This doesn't man you have to overhaul each minion, but elite mobs may be a good focal point in improving this area. Maybe try bringing in more elite mobs that are weaker, or making it so that elite mobs always drop something, giving players an incentive to seek out this chalenge.
Class balance is something that will come with time, and looking at the patch notes I can tell that the devs are putting a lot of effort into it, and I'd like to commend them for that.
This game has a bright future, and for its low price I would definitely recommend it.

Overture distills RPG and Roguelike elements to it's core and pulls an addictive little game out of the mix. It's fast pace and though the mechanics are simple enough, it still manage to offer a fairly high skill ceiling experience.
You'll be entering a procedurally generated map where you'll be hacking, shooting, and casting against hordes of enemies. The bosses are often tough and offer a fair degree of variety in strategy. You'll also be collecting money and loot as you travel. Though your loot get reset with every play, the cash you collect carry on, allowing you to purchase new classes and upgrades.
The game is mechanically sound. It's addictive, it's tough, and it mixes it up enough that each play through will offer it's own set of challenges. Where the game lacks a tiny bit is in the visuals. It's by no means ugly, and certainly has it's charm in it's pixel art, it it does look pretty standard issue. I didn't find the art direction to be very memorable. This is one of those games where it's "mechanics over graphics".
Overall Overture is a pretty enjoyable little romp, with some addictive qualities to it. It's not asking for very much either, and I think it's well worth the asking price if this interest you at all.
Pros:
- Simple mechanics, but high skill ceiling
- Does a good job at distilling core RPG and Roguelike elements
- Addictive
- Fair asking price
Cons:
- Uninspired visuals

Super Monday Night Combat is best described as a free-to-play 3rd-person shooter/MOBA hybrid with an oddball cast and a dedicated development team. The setting is the distant future, when fighting to the death for money is not only an accepted form of entertainment, but fully televised and marketed to no end. These deathmatches are fought between The Hotshots and The Icemen, whose teams are each made up of genetically engineered clones designed to wage a weekly war for the cameras.
Gameplay-wise, it's like many other f2p MOBAs: rotating free "pros," a small selection of upgradable moves, and waves of robots pouring out to destroy the turrets that guard each team's prize; the difference is the 3rd-person playstyle (instead of the traditional typical top-down, click-to-move style), which feels great and lends itself to a more immersive experience. Lastly, bugs are fixed in mere days, if not hours, and purchased items are purely cosmetic- no "pay-to-win" problems here. Try it!

Super Monday Night Combat is, simply put, the most unique Multiplayer Online Battle Arena game out there.  For those who don't know what a MOBA is, it's a highly-competitive online skill-based objective game that pits small teams of varied characters against each other.  SMNC ditches the usual isometric-perspective fantasy style and instead is a third-person shooter in a goofy dystopian game show.
It's free-to-play.  The only things you can't buy with earned in-game credits are cosmetic items, and you can still trade for them (and they have a chance to drop after a game, but that's very, very rare).  The only problem it has is the community; your fellow players can be quite aggressive.
Okay, there's another problem.  The tutorial doesn't tell you too much.  If you play, here's some key things.
1. Play the training stage to get a feel for the characters
2. Kill bots
3. Don't die, since this "feeds" enemy players (usually means stick with your team)
4. Defend the Annihilator

Meh. It feels like a very watered-down version of Human Revolution. The mechanics are actually decent for a mobile game port and the shooting mechanics feel alright. The stealth can get a bit wonky as the AI is not the best (and sometimes even below mediocre). The story is just okay; I was intrigued by the mysterious Tyrants and the backstory behind the main character, but only after about and hour of being exasperated by the at-first cheesy story. You can easily avoid microtransactions of any sort (by which I mean AT ALL) simply by picking up ammo and credits and not blowing all of your in-game money on things you don't need, so I'm not sure why people are complaining about this. Overall, a pretty solid title. It plays like a compact version of Human Revolution. If it goes on sale or you see it in a Humble Bundle, like I did, then I suggest you pick it up if you are interested. Avoid it as long as the price tag is above $5.00 USD though - that's the most I'd recommend spending on this game.

I just completed the early access version.
This game is a fine example of what Early Access should be about.
The game, while incomplete, has a stable base, is not an asset flip, features which are included work and look polished and most of all this game makes you feel like the developers have a clear vision where they want this game to go which is what most Early Access games lack and is extremely important in my humble opinion.
To the developers I can only say, well done and thank you for not coming on to Early Access to early with a game in a terrible state like so many others do.
Last but not least it is not the type of Horror Game which gives you a flashlight in darkness and thinks that is all we need for a Horror Game!
In this game you find yourself in control of a man, a painter and without trying to spoil anything, he has issues. He seems to be on a mission to complete a "unique" painting from "unique" ingredients in a House which is changing every time you go between rooms.
Throughout the game you will find clues as to what might have happened in this house but what ever it is something is not happy with the person you control and the fear of something looming in the next room is always present.
This game has an amazing atmosphere and the audio of dialog, footsteps, doors, objects, etc,,, is superbly done and adds to it in every way.
The jump-scares are well thought out. Not ones did I feel a jump-scare was just done for the sake of it but instead had some meaning to it that showed progress to the story or hinted at something, wanting you to find out more about it.
The things that happen in rooms with objects or the changing of rooms while you search for clues is just amazingly well done.
Rooms change seamlessly and the game is so well designed that it has you somehow look into the opposite direction when things change, resulting in the "WTF" moments more often than not when you turn back around.
The story so far has been deeply intriguing, making you continuously wanting to find out more and questioning your own thoughts on what happened more than just a few times.
I don't know what it is but the developers have the mixture of things down to such a fine art that everything just flows together so well it is hard to believe this game is only in Early Access.
What ever it is you are doing guys, keep on doing it :)
This Game ticked all the right boxes for me and I can't wait to play it again ones it is completed.

This game is right up there with the horror masterpieces like Amnesia, Outlast, Clive Barker's Undying, etc. with just a slight step below quality of a polished triple-a product. It is already excellent and still being worked on by the developers.
The controls are as simple as it gets: move, look, slight zoom, and examine/take. No map, objectives, inventory (of note), or handholding. The goals are still easy to figure out, even without any guidance, and that is a testement to the devs skill in this, and among many other areas, including the pacing, and graphics.
PROS:
-great atmosphere and setting
-excellent pacing
-very inventive scares, if one doesnt get to you, another one will later
-great graphics with some of THE BEST PAINT EVER DONE IN A GAME!
-genuinely creepy and offputting
-Story is gradually discovered through papers and notes, but done very well
CONS
-Some of the voicework is a bit of the indie variety (not on Amnesia level)
-the icons are very large and cartoony, making them easy to see, but breaking  much immersion.
-A bit linear, but this might not be a con really, since it flows really nice.
If you want an actual quality horror game that is great for the price, and if you like spookier, more supernatural games as opposed to Outlast's type scares, then this is a must get.

TL;DR -- Although showing its age, this work of art is the best atmospheric point-and-click game all-time. No apologies.
This is a 3rd-person perspective point-and-click horror game, where you play as Nigel Danvers. There are unusual goings-on at your workplace (hinted at in the introduction) causing you to be on the run. But where you end up is even more bizzare and haunting. The setting is modern-era coastal England, and the backgrounds are based on the game designer's photography of local areas. (it was a thrill to find out that the locations are based on real towns and locations).
Not everyone will like the black-and-white film noir style (with the occasional color bit). It's an acquired taste, but when you look at this as not just a game but really an artistic work, then it all fits into place. The pacing of the game is also reminicent of film noir, with Nigel jumping into the middle of things with minimal exposition at the beginning.
There are maybe 20 hours of gameplay and many characters to interact with. The puzzles are moderately hard (I had to look up one of them and another I did a brute-force approach) and there is at least one audio puzzle. Most of the voice acting is very good. However, you might not be thrilled with Nigel's delivery style ("Large...black...crows.") The music and haunting sound effects are top notch.
The graphics are from 2008, and the character models are starting to look dated (this may be a reason the sequels are taking so very long in development hell, to update graphics made quite a bit ago).
The story is immersive, and it makes the scary bits all the more effective.
True story: When I first played this and was getting used to the film noir effects, a small red orb in one scene caught my attention. The rest of the scene was in b/w, but I had already seen the occasional color effects to stress points (an I had seen the orbs before). As Nigel investigated a wall, this small red orb floated and meandered across the scene...and kept going right off my screen and onto the frame of my laptop. After I recovered my shock, I realized it was, of course, a small red mite that was crawling on my laptop screen.
Definitely get it on discount if you can. This is one every point-and-click gamer should have.

Your personal enjoyment of this game is directly correlated to how much you are into Star Trek.
If you are casually into Star Trek, you will probably enjoy the epic space battles, starship customization, team-play, and episodic content (called "seasons", haha). Although you may be put off by the grind in order to rank up and aquire the really awesome ships and weapons (most of which become available when you achieve the rank of Admiral; end game content).
However, if you really, really like Star Trek, this game might just be for you (considering it's pretty much the only Star Trek game on the market right now that is continually supported, updated, and added to by a team of extremely dedicated developers, not to mention backed by CBS and staying very true to cannon... mostly).
Go anywhere in the galaxy. Join the United Federation of Planets, the Klingon Defence Force, or the New Romulan Republic. Play as almost any species featured in the Star Trek universe, or create your own in the EXTENSIVE character editor. A hallmark of Cryptic Studios, customization is very, very detailed and varied (and maybe just a bit overwhelming) - everything from your species, face, body dimensions, uniform, comm-badge, stance, starship, registry number, shuttle, and even individual bridge officers can be customized so that your crew is exactly the way you want. The amount of creative freedom this game allows you without you having to pay a single dime is laudable indeed (I have played this game for nearly 3 years before installing it on Steam without spending any money on it whatsoever - it is NOT a "Pay 2 Win" game... but if you are paying to win, then why are you doing this to yourself?).
Such a thorough customization system allows you to craft your own truly unique character, ship, and story within the Star Trek universe - the only thing you are bound to is your career choice of either a science, engineering, or tactical officer. Even then, everything is available to you - nothing is restricted. The amount of freedom and choice this game allows you is, often times, mind blowing for a free-2-play title. Unfortunately, the graphics are beginning to show their age - although it's nothing a little bloom, dynamic lighting, and post-processing can't fix (it is a very system-friendly game). Here's hoping they implement a visual overhaul in the future.
Truly diehard Trek fans (and I mean diehard to the point where it's detrimental) might be disappointed at the overall mission structures. If you go into this game expecting every mission to be like a TNG episode, you will be dismayed that the missions are more like VOY episodes, or regular MMO missions, but with a Star Trek flavour (that is to say, not all the missions are bad - they're just not all TNG episodes... although some are). Unique diplomatic missions of peace and exploration are few and far-between (if not abundant and repetitive), with most missions ending at the tip of a phaser. Although the overall "Star Trek feel" is never lost or muddied, you may find yourself going "oh yeah, it's an MMO" to explain why you just sent a fleet of Hirogen vessels screaming into a black hole, or why you went back in time to the 22nd century and vaporized a handful of redshirts with no consequence. You simply need to replace your TV logic with Videogame logic.
Overall, if Star Trek is your jam, you may end up really, really enjoying the hell out of this game. I know I did.

So when I first started playing,  I was not enjoying and I really disliked the game. However after playing the game for an hour or so and getting past the horrible intro to the game, I started to have fun. While it is not tthe best game out there, it is certainly not the worst. I wasn't sure why they were charging for a f2p game but I realised that in game, you get 100 IRL currency and a "bond" that can be cashed in for some basic gear. Now a lot of people ask if this is pay to win, not at all. you can buy in game items with IRL money, but they only last a limited time. But this is the nice part, you can earn these items and weapons by simply playing and finding/looting the items in game, and they will last forever.
SUMMED UP-
Pay To Win?
A- No, you can buy items that last a limited time. However you may earn them in game and stay forever.
Why Pay For A Free Game?
You get in game currency that you would otherwise have to pay for IRL anyways, this way you pay less than usual and get to support the dev's. It is early access as well.
Is This Even Fun?
In the beggining, not at all. But I dragged on about an hour, and it suddenly became fun! After completing the horrible intro, you are free to explore and do quests, level up, and earn skills. Just like any other MMORPG. But this is in the S.T.A.L.K.E.R world and has a great community.
Is the world PVP?

Overall it's only barely a MMORPG in the traditional sense, and that's something i'm happy about. It may not feel very open world due to the game being composed of several (large!) different maps, but in effect you're absolutely free to go where you want. Knowledge of the game, maps, anomalies and etc is more important than hours put into the game, in many situations.
Skill and/or luck also plays a big role; Where in a traditional MMORPG a lvl 10 does not stand a chance against a lvl 20, this does not apply here. Especially in PvE it's more dependant on how you handle the situation. However, as you progress, you are able to get better gear and this too, plays a big role.
While in essence most quests are well made and interesting, considering they are mostly relatively simple/traditional kill and fetch quests, they are unable to immerse you properly, one of the biggest things keeping you from being very immersed is sloppy and missing translations.
Overall the combat IS good, but just doesn't feel very good due to eternal lag/latency issues.
It sometimes feels like the russian player dominancy ruins the community aspect for non russian players, and hackers can ruin any session at any time.
Still.. I do recommend the game. It's a special game. It's one of a kind... We should be happy it exists in it's current form.
We all know a true franchise S.T.A.L.K.E.R. MMORPG would be a traditional grindfest that would probably not feel anything like S.T.A.L.K.E.R. except the world it takes place in. This MMORPG, sZone, tries hard to avoid the traditional MMORPG feel while still attempting to maintain some degree of balance and still stay true to some of the original S.T.A.L.K.E.R. concepts. If you're more anal about knowing the ups and downs before even trying the free demo out, I'll go ahead and compile a list of Pros and Cons.
[Cons]
1. The game isn't the best in terms of customizable interface. At the present time, there is no such thing as an audio slider, so the player cannot choose how heavy SFX is over the Music.
2. Resolution is an issue. You currently only have a few options. 700xSomethingElseIDoNotKnowWhat, or Fullscreen.

[Pros]
1. The Soundtrack
2. The Soundtrack
3. Did I say the Soundtrack?

Let me just preface this with a caveat:  I would NOT recommend this game if you're not a fan of Wolfenstein 3D, or novelty games in general.  I am only giving it a recommendation if you have a predisposition toward early FPS games.
As an early FPS game, one of the Wolfenstein 3D engine games, this is actually overall quite solid.  The level design has some weaknesses in it, but as a whole the difficulty ramps up quite nicely, and other then giving no concern for actually making sense as far as being on an ark is concerned, they are mostly entertaining and easy enough to navigate.
The graphics are fine, even if I found areas that overused the "yellow curtain" theme to be somewhat headache inducing.  The theme is quite novel, and doesn't entirely work, but there's no reason for that alone to turn you away.  There are even some nice touches, such as all the episodes can be run as one single game, and the early episodes are shorter than the later ones.
The game is certainly not flawless.  Like Wolfenstein 3D itself, nearly every enemy is a hitscanning enemy, meaning they will instantly deal damage to you no matter how far away they are.  Sure, further away, more likely to miss, but one major issue is just how much damage they can do when they're right on top of you.  They deal progressively more damage each spit - how they 'shoot' - the closer they are to you.  Which leads, particularly in later levels, to an abundance of traps.  Enemies around corners that you can't hit until they get a free shot off you, enemies standing right behind doors, etc.  So in later episodes, there will be several instances of "Open door, DIE!"  There's some maze areas as well with very tight corridors and enemies that just keep filtering in from all sides, making it a real death trap as well.  One of the weapons, a rapid-firing slingshots, takes up gigantic portions of the screen, obscuring vision dramatically.  The new weapons, coconut and watermelon launchers, cannot fire over obstacles like the regular slingshots can, but can do some splash damage and sometimes can breeze past animals and still put them to sleep (this game's non-violent approach).  They are not very consistent, and have a tendency to hit walls, corners, objects, and 'explode' too early.  On later levels, you will STRUGGLE for ammo.
If you DO like Wolfenstein 3D games, this one's perfectly fine.  If you like novelty games, this one also qualifies.  On those points, absolutely, pick the game up and give it a try.  But if you are annoyed by some of the worst issues these Wolfenstein 3D games can have, this game certainly shares them.  Be warned.

The Evil Within is good. The combat is satisfying. There's a lot of variety to not just the locations, but the game play itself. This game took me around 20 hours to finish and the variety helped keep things fresh through the end. Ironically, I kept having deja vu all the time. This game really has no original ideas at all.  It's a patchwork of so many other games and even some movies, but they gel well together. There's a picture of the antagonist as a child during some loading screens and he looks a lot like the puppet from Saw. That cracked me up. Everywhere reminded me of something else. Even that kind of  fits in with the theme of story. The developers did a fantastic job making it feel like playing a dream. The narrative of the story and the structure of the progression of the levels are very much like a dream. Disjointed  and incoherent. That's not a dig at the story. I'm not sure I really understood the ending or if there is really anything concrete to get. The art style and some of the visual effects are really well utilized in selling the dream-like nature of the experience. This is a really sharp looking game too. The character models of the enemies look fantastic and suitably grotesque. Most of the bosses look straight out of Resident Evil and they are the scariest part of the game. Creepy! This game isn't so much scary, though, as it is really gory. This game is all about showing you some sick messed up stuff. It does have a spooky atmosphere and its always tense. This game takes a good step towards putting the 'survival' back into horror. I was always concerned about my ammo supply. Sometimes I'd just punch enemies to death  because I didn't have the ammo to spare or shoot them once in the leg hoping they'd drop to the ground so I could throw a match on them and burn them to death for the quick KO. Death is lurking behind every corner. Even easy enemies can kill you you're not paying attention and there are booby traps lying around that aren't always easy to spot. They can be disarmed but you have to stop this spinning needle at exactly the right spot or the trap will go off. This game is tough. Checkpoints are plentiful so it's also a fair game. I was pleasantly surprised by how much I liked The Evil Within. It was a blast to play through and I definitely recommend it.

Daggerdale was presented as a hack-n-slash action-RPG in the vein of the "Baldurs Gate Dark Alliance" games that appeared on the XBox and Playstation 2. Those were fairly uninventive RPGs (no party, no significant role-playing or dialogue) but still enjoyable for all that. I was looking forward to more of the same.
But Daggerdale doesn't even reach the unimpressive standards of a console RPG. It is a dull and dreary game. The level design is exceedingly linear, and every foot of it looks the same. The music is perhaps the most uninspired I have heard in any recent game, and the "Simlish" speech (doubtlessly used to save on localization costs; why pay for voice-actors when you can just use random grunting in place of speech?) is terrible. The controls are sluggish, the auto-targeting is terrible and the action is poorly paced. Nor is there any redeeming quality in the loot; none of the weapons are in anyway impressive. Story and setting are equally under-whelming. And the savepoints are poorly placed.
To top everything else off, the game is buggy; textures didn't show up, the game crashed randomly and too often my on-screen avatar just stopped responding to my controls (my favorite bug is how, in the climatic quicktime event -yes, the game resorts to those, too- my character wasn't even visible on the screen! The only possible saving graces to this game was the inclusion of co-op play... but then, I'm not sure I'd want to subject a friend to this game anyway. The four-hour gameplay, normally a disadvantage, was a god-send since I'm not sure I could have stomached more of this game anyway.
Daggerdale sucks. Even at sale it isn't worth the price. Avoid at all costs.

I have just completed this game, the story is brilliant and you could not possibly predict it, you will not recognize its brilliance until you finish it and piece everything together, for this reason I highly recommend this game.
Great game if you can live with the awfully slow movement (you can double click most areas so you dont watch Nigel amble around) and if you dont mind the game being almost black and white. Great story, atmospheric sound and music.
Get used to hearing "Thats not right!"
NEGATIVES
My first instincts after 5 minutes of playing was to turn it off and burn my computer including the building it resides in.
The reason for this is the first negative for the game.
The movement is painfully slow, you can speed this up in most places (not all but most) by double clicking the exits.
This is by far the biggest downside of this game and to be fair is due to a limitation of the game engine I am guessing.
The other negative for me was the voice overs, the people who do the voices are clearly amateurs and it shows in places, some of the dialogue sounds wooden and doesnt show enough emotion in places, on the whole its more a small niggle as you can tell that the people were passionate about this game at least which for me made up for it and for the most part the voice overs are fine, some are clearly better than others and its only here and there you can tell that the people doing the voices arent proffesionals, it didnt bother me much but I have read lots of comments about this so thought I would mention it.
It reminded me of an amatuer dramatic society reading through a script if that makes sense.
They are the only two negatives for me personally.
POSITIVES
This is not a game for impatient people, it is a game to play lesuirely and absorb yourself within the village of Saxton.
I found myself hooked on the story after the obvious glaring bad points of the game
It is a point and click game, you cannot use the keyboard at all, it is a supernatural mystery set in a fictional town in the south west of England and has a lot of text based information building a history of the town and the surrounding areas.
It does not hold you hand, I had to use a walkthrough guide two or three times but some people will struggle less/more depending on your patience.
It is a slow paced game at first but does start to smoothly progress after the in game day one which I urge you to perservere with as it does get better and the game world does open up to more locations
The story itself is very well written and thought out with seemingly fragmented stories all slowly evolving to make sense.
The sound and the music is exceptionally used, it is not over used and totally fits the game.
The graphics really is just a lot of stills that have very good monochrome detail and seem to basically be converted real photos for the most part.
I whole heartedly recommend this game to people with patience and want a story driven game to make you think, I cant really define this into a genre but the world needs more games like this,
(if anyone behind the game reads this, I would like to be involved in any projects you guys work on, I will not state why or what i could do here, just message me if you are seeking help at all)
Do not be discouraged by the general look of the game, although if you have played point and click games then it wont be a total shock to you, it is not a hidden object or puzzle game at all, you will not find silly puzzles for the sake of it, every aspect of the game is logical and relevent.
If you are interested in this game based on this review then I encourage you to not read anything more about the game but to simply dive in, it is after all a mystery at its heart, there are a few definite horror moments but its more of a mystery than a horror game
RELATING TO PREVIOUS GAMES
Having played and completed the two dark fall games I can state that the order of play for the three games doesnt much matter, there are small snippets that long the games but they are subtle and you will not have any spoilers for other games if playing them out of order, the lost crown is smoother and easier to play too, the team seem to have relaxed the difficulty a little compared to the dark fall games which in places could be very frustrating.
Thats all from me, go buy and play this little gem!

Even after I found their dead cats for them and fixed their stupid elevator.

If you're interested in pre-christian British history and culture and you don't hate point and click adventures, stop reading and buy this game. There are so few examples of games treating this subject with any seriousness or artistry that The Lost Crown is worth playing for that alone.
Aside from that, it has plenty of flaws, well documented elsewhere, and I needed a walkthrough for a couple of obscure puzzles, but it is all pretty tolerable. The ghost hunting aspects are not central to the game, but the theme of historical and supernatural investigation is, and gives this game a unique atmosphere. I found the art style to be a little strange at first, but grew on me a lot during my playthrough, to end up one of my favourite aspects of the game.
People who are interested in the specific subjects and themes of the game will get the most from it.

This review is based on a stealth/no kills only run of Deus Ex: The Fall.
I like Deus Ex: The Fall but there is also a lot of things it does wrong. The game isn't much of a graphics powerhouse and is based on an iOS/Android version of the game, it is plagued with low resolution textures, bad object geometry and terrible character models. The options are fairly limited and you only have the ability to change resolution and anti-aliasing and none of the various options you would expect to find in Deus Ex: Human Revolution. You only have 1 save slot and if you have auto saving on it is possible to ruin your game if you run into the many glitches this game has. One such example was I missed out on a side quest but was unable to load to an earlier state.
Being based on a mobile port leads to other issues in which I will go on with. The game has a store menu which has being lifted from mobile version without the real money transactions where you can buy Praxis kits, weapons, ammo and health any time you want as long has you have the credits. I don't like this system as I feel it's lazy and all this should of being available from NPC vendors within the game or found via the world of Deus Ex: The Fall.
There is no jump button in this game which creates frustration at times when wanting to go over simple obstacles. Another legacy of The Fall's humble mobile origins is disappearing bodies are in the PC version, whether you knock out or kill an enemy their body just disappears a few seconds later right before your eyes. Ignoring everything else negative I have mentioned about this game so far my biggest pet peeve is the terrible A.I. You can literally perform take downs on enemies from 100° angles and they easily give up on you after getting bored hunting you down and go back to their regular patrol routes as if nothing happened. What weapons I did use in the game had barely any recoil, bad animations and explosions from grenades and mines where terrible.
After getting all the negatives out of the way Deus Ex: The Fall does have redeeming qualities as hard as it is to believe. It plays similar to Deus Ex: Human Revolution with hidden areas, hacking, the ability to take stealth or guns blazing approach to situations, the ability to upgrade your augmentations/weapons, it has a HUB area and even some side quests with a multi branching dialogue system. The story is actually interesting, Ben Saxon was a better protagonist than I was expecting, the level design is ok and the voice acting outside Anna was pretty decent. The game ends of a cliff-hanger so it’s unclear if we will ever actually get a conclusion to this story via an Episode 2. To 100% the game it will take players around 6 hours.
If you are thirsty for more Deus Ex go ahead and play it. As a mobile game it might be the best on the platform but as a PC title, it is hard to indorse.

While it's not the worst game out there, it's still not very good and here's why.
Anyone who has any knowledge of the Bible know Noah and his Ark. For those who don't know. Noah builds an Ark tor the great flood and puts two of each animal inside the ark.
The game is set inside the ark and your goal is to go around the multiple floors of the ark and find the animals and put them to sleep so they stop causing trouble.
The game has a rich back story of being one of the most infamous SNES games of all time. Originally Hellraiser the video game it was reworked into this game, with the bible theme around it and was brought into the mainstream by AVGN who made a video on this game.
The game is nothing more than a Wolfenstein clone and nothing more. You go around a maze like environment, look for keys and go to the next floor. The gameplay is also identical.
The game is a first person shooter, where you use a slingshot to shoot food into the animals to make them fall asleep.
Later on you can pick up different types of slingshots, but all that changes is the fire rate. Also you can pick up melon launchers, but those are incredibly useless and you will only use them in dire situations.
The graphics are alright for the most part. Everything looks crisp as it is updated from the original graphics which is nice, but the level layouts almost always look the same which brings me to my next point.
The level design is atrocious. Now don't get me wrong Wolfenstein had a lot of this as well, but the way this game does this maze like environment is atrocious. The map doesn't help at all and is pretty much useless in the end. The graphics make everything look the same making it hard to figure out where you've been and where you haven't been.
The soundtrack is atrocious and it's just best to mute the entire game and to listen to something else while playing.
The game counter told me it took me 2 hours to finish and that with a lot of trial and error. A lot of the later stages have massive difficulty spikes which make you be as careful as possible.
Final Thoughts:
Super 3D Noah's Ark is a mediocre Wolfenstein rip off. It's been called the worst clone out there, but after playing it, I have to disagree. While the game is not good, it's definitely not the worst clone out there when stuff like Nerves of Steel exist.
Pros:
+ Fun Gameplay
+ Vibrant and Colorful graphics
Cons:
- Terrible Level design
- Terrible Audio
- Map system doesn't work
- Massive difficulty spikes
5/10

THE GOOD:
This is a fairly mixed review. I really, REALLY liked the lore and atmosphere, it kept me coming back to this game. Whatever coherence is lacking in the overall plot, it is made up for with interesting characters that had me genuinely interested in all 6 or so different storylines. The writing is thoughtful and does much more than simply galvanizing the story. I have issues with the level design of many of the chapters, but the controls are still fluid and responsive. Avoiding spoilers as much as I can, I was especially impressed with Apocalypse. It was gorgeous, funny, terrifying, and surprisingly poignant.
THE BAD:
The fatal flaw of the game is the pointlessly long corridors that pair with a mostly unpredictable AI, making levels like Stronghold and Take Over (The second floor of Take Over is arguably the most difficult in the game) feel like an exercise in repetition until RNG turns favorable. The frustration of having the only remaining enemy be a gunman you've never seen in a hall you thought you cleared, or a dog in a dark room, makes it hard to push through to get to the meat of the game. Also, huge pet peeve of mine, I hate getting caught on random obstacles in games where movement is key, and that happens frequently with much of the environment having ambiguous function. As for the story, like I said, *I* really liked the story, and I understand if this is not unanimous. Without spoiling too much, the very last piece of story felt clumsy with very little foreshadowing until you go back and find the subtle clues hidden amongst the levels.
THE UGLY:
The acid trip-esque visuals and the pixel art are beautiful pairings with the hyperactive stimulation of the brutal gameplay. They lend themselves well to the grossly indulgent violence and the pixel art especially brilliantly juxtaposes the incredibly dark and somber nature of the game. The caveat being that it is a challenge with vague graphics to discern what certain objects are and how they are interacted with, if they block movement, bullets, or both.
VERDICT:
I think the reviews for this game are in the right place, I give it a 7/10. I am aware Dennaton denied that a sequel would ever be developed, which is a serious bummer. I would love an HM3 as the artwork and writing put this series well above it's clones in my eyes.
~~~~~~~
EDIT: After getting more into the speedrunning of the game, I found it actually has fantastic replayability as a typical arcade style action game. I went from 30 hours which was mostly the campaign to almost 80 in a matter of weeks trying to get all the achievements. I think the game peaks at this late stage where the player has developed strategies for every room in the game and the execution becomes incredibly satisfying. With that said, I also found myself wishing moreso than in my first playthrough that there were more characters and different loadouts in the game, going from the many masks of the previous game to a tight rotation of characters, several of which do not have extra abilities, is a bit of a let down. The abilities they include are great though. The direction they took with Evan Wright was especially awesome, although not necessarily an ability as much as a deviation. I would revise my score to a 9/10. Just give it time.

I have seen many negative reviews on this game and decided to put my own in answer to them.
Yes this game has grinding, no doubt about that.
What people need to understand is that this game makes grinding not so bad. Sure you want tanks, planes, snipers, etc. But this game plays just fine on a default character. Once used to this game, you will even find yourself going back to the default gun (semi-automatic rifle) for some of your builds, as it has the best versatility.
This game is also fun for people who are normaly mediocre in a FPS.
Positioning (even if someone has their super moded SMG, that wont do them much good when getting shot in the back), coordination (granted many teamates lack the required IQ for this, but this is true for the entire Internet), combined arms (no, dont attack with only tanks, dont attack with only planes, have a mixed team) all make this game fun.
What im trying to get to is this:
Yes you want that tank real bad. Once you get that tank (if you have the patience for that), you will only want the next tier. You will be annoyed at getting killed all the time because of the lack of infantry support.
Yet, when you were a little noob, were you supporting allied tanks? Probably not.
So instead of whishing you could have something better right away (which you can if you pay money), enjoy the equaly competitive build you already have.
Once you play with the default build properly, you will have fun. Once you are having fun: you wont be grinding anymore because you will be unlocking things without waiting for them.
P2W?!? NO! Buying weapons, etc. is far from pay to win. Most guns are balanced if used properly. Of course an SMG will beat the Semi-Auto of yours at close range. Of course a 1 hit BA will kill you at long range. So stay at medium range at first. You might think the you never have enough credits at first. But after a while, you will find yourself with over 500k credits with no way to spend them.
Getting sniped in spawn? Use a vehicule, dont rambo. Or even better, sneak up on the sniper, kill him, start sniping yourself :) .
Getting killed by tanks? Get a RPG and dont stay in the open.
Getting killed by planes? Thats just bad luck, planes aren't all that good.
Getting killed by that OP gun in the other team? Stay where your gun is good. Dont go in close when the enemy has an SMG, dont stay in the open when they have a BA.
No able to pay for the weapon upkeep (or new ones)? Dont go for unlocking every weapon at once, chose your play style (long range, close range, medium range) then pick something according to that.

I know games in Early Access have a certain stigma,some questionable devs have been slapping an "Early Access" label on complete POS games and selling them for insane amounts of money and not updating or completing their games. . . .THAT IS NOT THE CASE WITH THIS GAME !! So far there have been several updates and I've only had the game for 6 days,I'm really pleased so far with these devs and this game !! The devs are active in the games forums and really seem to be wanting to give us a quality game !!
When I saw this game,I waited a few days and read through the reviews,I trust what my fellow gamers have to say a whole lot more than those that get paid to write reviews. . .It looked like a really good game,so I took the chance and so far so awesome !!
*SPOILERS AHEAD* BE WARNED *SPOILERS COMING* !!
I love the way the entire game is nothing but a glorious mind f*ck !! It's everything a horror experience should be !!
I love the way the enviroment changes as I look around in a 360 degree circle. . .this game got the insanity feeling that I was hoping for in Hektor,spot on !!
Some fellow gamers have alluded to how this game reminds them of PT,but to be honest,I have no clue what PT is/was so,for me,that aspect dosen't matter . . .
I also want to touch on the things that make it a good game,in my opinion,the atmosphere is so twisted that I get jumpy all the time. . .A rat skitters across the floor making it's "squeaky" rat noise and I threw my controller,swear to the Gods,I threw it and my dog just looked at me as if I were crazy !!
I love the way there are various "warnings" on the walls or in the enviroment !! Listen to what those warnings say !! It could be the difference between life and death !!
I've loved getting snippets of the story via various notes,letters,diary pages,writing on the walls and so on. . .

I think if you like horror,you need to buy this game. . .If you like story-rich games,you need to buy this game. . .if you like exploration,you need to buy this game. . . .I recommend this game,whole-heartedly !!

Where would i start....
Probably by saying that this is an early access game review.
Right, i think it's both fantastic and horrendous the way this game makes you feel. Honestly, i'm at the loss for words here.
The game itself looks brilliant, the atmosphere build up is absolutely gorgeous. It makes your jaw drop, and i find it interesting how much it makes enjoyable to feel fear and how much it plays with false sense of security. The story is intriguing, not many modern horror games can say that. I'm not going to compare this to any other game for a simple reason: This game is on a whole new level. It amazingly portrays the insanity, the mayhem in a deluded person's head. One must be open to interpretation. So far, i liked what i saw, this has a potential to become so much more, a trailblazer for modern horror games. Now, there are some elements that you might find it familiar, but i think, they were scrapped and unused in other projects, wasted potential, thus used in THIS game to it's full extent. I'm not gonna lie, i didn't know the weight of my decisions that i made, let me tell you one word - explore. Layers of Fear is one of the best horror games i played and it's still in early access. I want to commend the developers for such a game, you fellas have absolutely no shame, brilliant geniuses. At first i thought i'd list all the phobias that i encountered in the game, but honestly, the list would be too long. If you don't believe me, by all means, try this game out, and experience for yourself. I will update the review as the game develops.

I really can't heap more praise on this game than has already been given... it is by far my favorite Point-and-Click Adventure game out there. And that is really the only caveat that I can give... This is a classic P&C game with all of the classic P&C "problems." You will spend a lot of time running around looking for something to do, only to find out that you stupidly missed something simple... or you missed a hotspot on your first pass. I can guarantee that you will likely be frustrated with this if you are not someone who plays a lot of these type of games. But this is the one P&C game that has stayed with me for many, many years. I first played this game on disc when it first came out (and many times since). I truly can't wait for the sequel, I love the atmosphere of the game, and the characters are just as charming as they can be annoying. I'll also point out that this is the first game that ever managed to successfully catch me off guard with a jump scare. I also love that the majority of the logic in this game isn't absolutely ridiculous as it is in many P&C games. If you find yourself stuck, or are not really up to wandering for hours, find one of the many free walkthroughs out there and take a tour of Saxton... for the price, it's worth the atmosphere alone.

Scrap Mechanic set you along your way to becoming a master builder in this wonderful world that allows you the player to be in charge of how your world takes shape. Build vehicles, race tracks, amusement parks, and much more, all with your own unique style and flare. Automate your roller-coaster's and cars. Connect them to switches and bearings and sit back and enjoy the ride.
Pros:
-	The ability to easily connect blocks to working controls allowing them to become automated and timed to work in perfect concert with everything around them.
-	The beautiful graphics of the game make it a joy to see and be a part of as your creations take shape around you.
-	Multiplayer allows you to invite your friends to join you or to join them on their world and see their creations first hand.
-	The devs are very good about adding new things into the game and fixing bugs that exist in the game at this time, one of the new things that make the game quite a bit more enjoyable recently has been the spray paint.
Cons:
-	Multiplayer is extremely laggy for the joining party, although the better the connection you have the less there is but even with a great internet you will still find the lag to be very annoying. (keep in mind this game is still in early access and will most likely fix this problem as time goes on)
-	The spray paint tool has a fairly small size of colors to pick from; it’s only my personal taste but would love to see a color wheel added into the tool to give the full range of color shades to the player.
In conclusion Scrape Mechanic is an amazingly fun game that will let you build in ways most others of the genre have yet to tap into. You will spend hours messing with controllers and timers but in the end you will create something amazing to behold. 3.5 out of 5.

-was the tag line this game was advertised with. That puts a heavy shadow over this game as a result and I believe it works against it. It's not a tagline that would get me to buy a copy as I'm not a big fan of where the Resident Evil series has evolved into, however I am a fan of the classic RE series.
As you play The Evil Within it becomes obvious they haven't gone far from their previous projects as "the makers of Resident Evil" and The Evil Within is like the new kid that has a big brother looming over him called Resident Evil, that it tries to emulate and copy from while awkwardly doing it's own thing.
This doesn't mean it lacks in originality, but it's hard to call this game original at all since it borrows from so many sources and horror clichés and it's hard not to roll your eyes while playing it if you play a lot of horror games or if you watch horror movies. This might be because the current horror gaming genre is over saturated by pretty bad games but what The Evil Within does try very hard to is scare you which is something it's big brother Resident Evil stopped trying to do years ago.
It plays like a generic third person shooter with massive influences taken from another third person horror shooter: The Last Of Us, down to collecting random scrap to create ammo and trying to sneak up on the monsters for instant kills. Monsters in this game are durable and gameplay is a mix between sneaking and "aim for the head and hope it dies".
Most monsters are identical in how they fight you with minor differences in their patterns, as such the gameplay can get boring quite quickly. You go into a stage, scavenge for ammo, waste it instantly (even perfect headshots won't be enough) on a few monsters, then struggle with stealth to survive if the stage allows it and repeat that all over in the next stage.
You can upgrade your characters attributes with the "green goo" you get from random monsters or find around stages by injecting it into your brain. Upgrade types are straight out of Resident Evil from shorter reload times to 10% critical increase for kills on headshots etc. and it does allow you to customize your gameplay a little, but mainly it becomes obvious it doesn't matter a hell of a lot since you cannot buy ammo at all and that shotgun you upgraded might not get any ammo drops on the next stage making all those points spent upgrading it moot. The only weapon worth upgrading is the crossbow and it's bolts as it's the only one that you can make ammo for.
The only unique twist to the combat is the use of matches as "finishers" that are limited but sadly it becomes an awkward mechanic as most if not all monsters get up too quickly for you to utilize it. However matches are limited and I liked the added pressure for the player to have to choose which bodies he felt were worthy of burning. Cool idea but feels wasted.
Boss fights in this game are also very cookie cutter "find the pattern" or "weak point" and shoot it. The monster designs are of another matter and I'll get to that a bit later. Most boss fights either waste all your ammunition or leave way too obvious ways for you to kill them like brightly coloured red barrels.
The last thing I'll mention in gameplay are the cheap instant deaths. There are a lot of them such as trip wires hidden under water you can't see, spike traps that you couldn't notice, monsters instant killing you while off screen etc. there are a lot of "well that was cheap" moments and as far as the controls go they don't help. The PC version of this game lacks good localization and moving around feels very clunky at best. Menus are a pain to move in and the inventory system seems hastily made for the PC version. Expect to be frustrated with the controls if you don't own a controller.
This game is pretty. It has all the luxuries of a "next gen" game in terms of lens flares, texture animation, physics and screen filters. It is a pretty looking console game and the PC version does offer 60 FPS and anti aliasing. The god awful top and lower bars are gone from the console version since you can just toggle them off and overall it's a nice looking game. The only minor thing that will only a few is the texture pop in. It's a half a second blurriness every time the camera changes scenes during cut scenes and can take you out of it but shouldn't bother most.
The game has some pretty awesome looking monster designs and segments that feel very like mini Micheal Bay movies. "Destruction porn" is the closest thing I can describe it as. It has some really interesting environments and visuals apart from a few areas at the end of the game that feel shoehorned in for a few fights but over all this game had some good visual artists working on it.
It copies from Inception heavily and adds in typical Japanese fantasy type villains and the main protagonist feels empty and void of any character. His favourite catch phrase is &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; and that should tell you a lot. The very few other characters are also very bland and uninteresting, and most if not all plot elements are pretty much explained in tapes and cut scenes in very bland ways leaving nothing for player interpretation, and the twists in story are very easy predict.
The voice acting has a lot to be desired and many lines are delivered with no passion and it takes you right out of the moment. It is comparable to anime dubbing where most of the "acting" is just grunts and sighs and heavy breathing then as dry as you can be line deliveries.
The main characters whole background is littered in journals around the games "save points" and it plays no role in the actual cut scenes or arch of the main story, which leaves a bitter taste for anyone who actually searches horror games for interesting stories.
The whole story is fixated on the subject of psychology and horrors, but it is just a bad attempt at putting those two elements together and thinking this is what makes a good psychological horror game. It does not. Most horrors in this game are just cheap jump scares, loud noises and gore, gore, gore and gore. Nothing is really scary for a veteran of horror games and the game does very little in terms of advancing the genre but then again I don't think that's what it's trying.
It IS trying to scare you WITH a horror story about psychology but this does not make it a psychological horror. The makers of this game fill in as many cliché horror elements as they can and it feels like canned horror much as everything else in the industry and I think this is what they wanted, to sell it.
The fact that it's third person doesn't help it either plus the main character is void of any real life human reactions to the terrors he sees and all you'll ever him say is "what the ♥♥♥♥" or &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; while he runs away. The only moments it feels like the main character is scared is in his breathing, which will take you aback as he's pretty much sold as a bad♥♥♥♥♥in cut scenes and then suddenly he's breathing like a sissy in another.
Scary the game isn't, an interesting story it doesn't have but it really does try. I get this feeling there must've been some limitations while making this game. It is far more a horror game than Resident Evil series is, which stopped trying to scare the player. The Evil Within tries and it might actually scare some of your squeamish friends.
For sure! It's not a bad game by any stretch and has some interesting visuals. It isn't a genre reformer and I don't think it tries to be. It's a horror game for the masses that dips its' head into the jar of ideas and copies a lot from other sources and then slams together a sandwich of a game with a bit of everything. It lacks heavily in originality, story, gameplay and horror but it's all in all a very... mediocre game. Not bad, not good, just bland.
I just don't know, so to say. And I think I can say that; I do not get the choices anyone makes. And I mean it, anyone.

So far, i liked what i saw, this has a potential to become so much more, a trailblazer for modern horror games. At first i thought i'd list all the phobias that i encountered in the game, but honestly, the list would be too long. For readers who have innevidably read that this game feels like a L4D game, you have heard correct, and I have to say that saying that is a deserved complient.
Upon begining Vermintide you are introduced to the 5 playable characters via a short video, and then have the option of selection one (you can change at any time while not in a mission). Each character has a unique weapon and playstyle unique only to them as they carve their way through an endless sea of Scaven rat creatures.
Gameplay is a lot of fun, however can get annoying if you keep losing. All in all, very fun and fast paced game with interesting story missions (ideas such as collecting food for the resistance in a market district populated by rats, or convincing a wizard to cast a ward on your home base) that kept me interested. Only problem is I think the charge attacks take a bit too long to charge (esspecially when cornered) and the lack of available teammates at midnight.

It's been a long time since left for dead, we needed something to expand off of the same sort of genre with different stories
*edit*
well, my original review was pretty short, so i feel that it's time to, after a long time playing this game, expand on it. First off, I'm going to talk about the combat. there are multiple weapon types, each of which fits into 2 categories. these categories are ranged weapons, and melee weapons. ranged weapons, of course, use ammo to fire (excluding the staffs used by the wizard). This ammo can be found in one use pick-ups around the map, and far more rarely, in crates with unlimited supplies of ammo. IF YOU ARE PLAYING AS A MELEE FOCUSED CHARACTER, LET YOUR TEAM MATES PICK UP AMMO FIRST.
The melee weapons all have different stats, with their different weapon classes having vastly different stats. For example, both 2 handed hammers and 2 handed swords can do a sweeping attack, but hammers have far more knockback, and will stun enemies and push them back far better than swords ever could.
All of these weapons, excluding white quality weapons, have some sort of buff on them that can be unlocked at the forge for a small amount of materials (basically money). The higher the rarity of the weapon, not only does it do more damage, but also has more slots for these buffs. Weapons come with buffs already on them, but if you want to change them, you can do that at the altar, but keep in mind that you may hate your new buffs worse than the old ones.
The combat itself -actually swinging your weapon- feels very good, each swing feels unique, and you can cut off enemy limbs, which usually puts them into pre-made death animations. The enemies are quite varied, and will be familiar to Left For Dead players.
I don't really feel like adding more at this time, but i may make some more edits at a later time.

Easy point n click game with scary tones.  The Lost Crown gains bragging rights for being a game that is not big on graphics, but it has sustances.  You play as Nigel Danvers, on the run from Hadden Corporation after witnessing some of their technological hardware, which apparently is illegal by their standards.  Danvers then enters a train that takes him to the Sedgemarsh Station which leads to the shady harbor town of Saxton.  Thankfully, Nigel discovers the town is riddled in mystery of the paranormal and is even helped by Hadden using ghost hunting equipment to discover the towns ancient treasure The Saxton Crown.  So, as the player you control Nigel to explore the town, talk to people and solve puzzles.  What I like is that the game will give you a chime once the puzzle is met.  Also, certain actions and cutscense will play unless you solve certain puzzles, like before Nigel goes to bed, he must place the camera on the window sill before going to sleep in order to continue.  This is good idea and little things like these help with the games creepy atmosphere.  Yes, creepy is a great word to put in this perspective.  I am also glad that there are no jump scares, unlike FNAF, the presence of scary looms over you and watches you from shadows, until it scares you.
Using the tools are great as well.  You have many things to work with such as tape recorders to here EVP, a camera to take pictures for both scenery and the paranormal, a E.M.F. Meter to find powerful forces, and a Night Vision Camcorder to see in the dark and record movement.  The harbor town of Saxton is like a small dream come true and I do enjoy the ambience this game has.  It has calm quiet moments that enjoy the scenery, and there are times on where it will scare you.  I recommend to anyone if their are interested into ghost hunting and reading a huge story.  As always if you don't like it, you don't, but if you want to explore the curious side of things, I highly recommend you pick this one up.

[Update 2-15-15] - Many issues have been addressed by the developer and he is very active in the forum. There are constant updates, sometimes multiple per week it seems. I've changed my recommendation from not recommended to recommended. Enough has been fixed with the game and there has been enough support by the developer(s) that it's worth a purchase for anyone interested in this type of game.
I want to get some negatives/gripes I have with the game off my chest first. Don't mind the description, it's misleading imo. It has little to nothing to do with Zelda or Binding of Isaac and the only thing in common with Diablo is the way loot/money explodes out of monsters and chests. The game plays like a mix of Hero Siege mixed with Realm of the Mad God. The "vast" dungeons are just square levels, decently sized but still just square levels.
- There is a big lack of options currently.
- The game runs in something like a 700x400 window. You can't resize it but you can fullscreen if you want.
- The window constantly gets centered in the middle of your monitor after you die and start again even if you move it to somewhere else on your screen.
-
- There is now an option to disable screenshake.
- The game is fairly difficult and punishing but doesn't feel as rewarding as some others in the genre for the amount of effort it takes to progress. Items are mostly bland and boring (have only gotten to level 3 but things don't seem to change). Need far more effects on items, right now it seems like there are only a small handful of them. x% chance to cast poison cloud, some dagger skill, potions on kill, exp, and that's about all I've seen. Boring overall.
- I believe this has been fixed or mostly fixed. You can now walk through walls (as can enemies sometimes) based on certain conditions(?). I assume if an item lands on it it becomes passable. I have no idea how exactly it works but at least you can grab your loot.
With all that said, it's still not necessarily a bad game. The soundtrack is absolutely amazing and I hope they add more to it. The game can get very very repetitive with all the dying so you need more variety. The gameplay overall IS still fun, there is plenty of variety with the characters and you can unlock all of them within a few hours of gameplay.
My absolute biggest problem with the game currently is the camera. Second is resolution. If at least the camera is changed so it pans only when you hold down a key I'd consider recommending the game to others. If resolution and how far around you you can see is increased I would definitely recommend it. Hero Siege is the only other game I can think of that has come out recently in this style and right now, I feel like that is much more polished and fun. Overture feels like a beta rather than a fully complete game, there is a lot more to add to really make it fun and rewarding but if the devs support the game it can definitely get there.

So I played the game through, and just when it was about to get interesting, there was a TO BE CONTINUED.  Bear in mind that it took 5.8 hours to get interesting (I'm pretty sure at least one of those hours was preparing a soup from scratch and then eating it).  I expect the TO BE CONTINUED will be another equal waste of cash.
So the gameplay is largely the same as Deus Ex, except you start with the Icarus Wings falling system.  Not that there are any heights to fall from, so that's useless.  There's no jump button, so anything you're looking for -- such air vents (!) -- is at floor level.  The "numerous" side-quests the overview boasts is about 5.  The levels are claustrophobic and tiny, which I understand to be a hold-over from being a mobile game.  You get just enough cash through the game to buy maybe one of the "bundles" (!), or one of the advanced weapons, just before the game is over.  There don't appear to be many meaningful decisions to make with dialogs, in-game choices, in the way that other games in the series have.  The story *could* be interesting, but it isn't yet.
In short, this game is a Deus Ex game, but with far less Deus Ex than a Deus Ex game should have.  It's a thorough "meh."  As such, even though it provided a vaguely entertaining Sunday afternoon, I can't really recommend it.

I have to clean up this review. The review before was a list of pros and cons, and since is this is my most popular review, I will fix it just before Mankind Divided's launch.
Before the review starts, I need to mention this is an iOS port.
When many people think Deus Ex, they think of either the original or Human Revolution. The original is considered one of the best videogames of all-time and was ambitious for the time. Human Revolution took the license back after 7 years of hibernation to revive it and did a great job. Now, this intermission between Human Revolution and Mankind Divided steps in, is it good?
It's mediocre. The maps, controls, and microtansactions (still left in the port, even though you can't buy anything with real money besides the base game) feel like an iOS game. The maps were shrunken down so that mobile phones could play the game. The controls also aren't the best and can feel awkward. The augments and mechanics are similar to Human Revolution's, so if you liked those, then you'll feel at home (with the exception of the controls). It will take about 2-4 hours to finish the game (4 if you are like me and do side missions etc). Also, expect an occasional bug, but nothing gamebreaking.
Deus Ex games are known for their story, so does this game have a good story?
Not really. It is very forgetable and writing this over a year after playing it, the only thing I really remember about the story is the cliffhanger ending, like the developers were planning future DLC but then decided to call it quits after the average reviews came out.
Rating:
4.10-Mediocre
Rating for Deus Ex Fans:
5/10-Average

Steam reviews really need a neutral recommend option, but I'll make do with what I have. So let me clarify, I would only recommend this game to people who have finished Deus Ex: Human Revolution and The Missing Link DLC (or DE:HR - The Director's Cut), and really want more. Having played through DE:HR multiple times a year or so ago, it was enjoyable to get more content in that world. Granted, it's extremely neutered and simplified content, but it scratched the itch I had to go back to DE:HR.
The other reviews seem almost unanimously negative and I really don't think Deus Ex: The Fall warrants that harsh of criticism. You definitely need to know and expect that you are playing a port of a mobile game, and it's not going to live up to complexity or visual fidelity of a full PC title. But that being said, I was really surprised that this was a mobile game first and I think I would have been pretty impressed if I saw it running on a tablet. It's certainly an extremely simplified version of DE:HR, but that doesn't mean there isn't anything to enjoy.
Things it does well:
-Borrows enough assets (visual and audio) that it's immediately recognizable as the world of DE:HR.
-Has mandatory Deus Ex freedom of approach. You can burst through the front door on a murderous rampage or sneak through side tunnels reaching your objective with only the occasional thug knocked unconscious.
-Very stable from my experience. I expected a mobile port to be much more buggy.
-It's a good length and the pacing is decent. At 5-7 hours to complete it doesn't overstay it's welcome and I never felt like there was filler content for the sake of stretching out the game.
Things it does poorly:
-Graphic fidelity is low, both in 3D models and animations. But hey, it was a mobile game, so you shouldn't be expecting the Crysis engine.
-It's easy. My playthrough was based on stealth and no-kills, and was completed without much difficulty.
-All of the systems from DE:HR are VERY simplified. Some to the point of making them less interesting (ie: being able to buy any item from the inventory menu instead of having to find an arms dealer in game).
-The voice acting is pretty sub-par. It's fully voiced, which is nice, but the acting is all pretty bland and npc voices seem disconnected.
-The controls can be wonky in some situations. I can't imagine playing this on a touch screen as there are some problematic controls even with a k/m.
-The interface buttons are really unresponsive. This is actually the thing that probably bothers me the most. Clicking a large button that your cursor easily fits inside almost always takes at least 2 clicks to get it to work.
As I said earlier, I'm recommending this ONLY for people who have played all of the other Deus Ex: Human Revolution content and want more. It is absolutely skippable if you don't feel the need for another story in the same world and should definitely be avoided if you haven't played DE:HR. It certainly pales in comparison to the game it's based on, but with a cheap price, I personally enjoyed jumping back into that world for a few hours (although I'd wait for a sale if you haven't bought it yet, there's seriously no rush).
The dialogues feel horribly forced, the plot is boring and the graphics are bad. Also, the game's got none of the charm other Deus Ex games have.
