I played 388 hours at the time of this post in about a month. So It speaks for itself. I was going to postpone this review until i got my character closer to max but the problem is, It's incredibly grindy, even with the power level support of a guild you will spend 10s of hours doing the same dungeon over and over and over again just to gain a few levels. I actually had to level by myself most of the time from 0-125 and got a few levels with the help of people here and there.
But it was mostly solo and as I grew this became increasingly more frustrating and when i tried to find people to group with even in my own guild they were either to low or 160+. I thought it would be more fun leveling with others while we strive for the same goal and even if I did find one or two people theres no telling what there hours are if I wanted to do a hardcore 8-10 hour session there unreliable.
My point is you cant do it solo. Even if you spend money on the game it will take an eternity and be very frustrating and mentally taxing and at lower to mid levels it's incredibly difficult to find a group so your grind to like 180+ Is going to be absolute hell and it begs the question ''Why am I even doing this? I'm not even having fun.''
Maybe because once you get to a point where you can consistently group it would actually be joyous. But is the reward really worth the journey? Especially considering how repeatitive it is? Well In my opinion no. Would the game pass expectationsif you could find a group and hard level with them for 5+ hours? Yes.
I realize by this point it seems like I do not recommend the game. There isn't anything wrong with the game at all. It's the playerbase, It needs to grow and stop being nothing but wakfu veterans with 20+ near max or fully maxed characters.
There are solutions IF you have money but this is not how wakfu was intended to be played It is not a pay to win game by any means. However, if you get the hero pack which allows you to add two characters from your own account to your party and you buy sufficent items from there store to in turn sell for in game currency you can buy top tier gear for your three characters and should have no problem soloing content that is for leveling. Atleast up until a certain point.
But this in my opinion is unreasonable. Simply being able to find a group of OTHER players would more than suffice, you shouldn't have spend money just to level at a reasonable pace and you wouldn't if the playerbase wasn't dramatically low.
I know the reviews long, I just want you to have sufficent knowledge of what your getting yourself into because if you install and start playing you'll be addicted within the first hour especially if turn based strategy game is your gamer turn on and you will be very dissappointed that you cannot continue due to lack of funds or because you don't want to spend 5+ months ( depending on your schedule ) maxing a character.
QUICKER REVIEW :
It's a very entertaining game in a somewhat dying genre of the turnbased strategy games, which in some way makes it a gem since it is also an Mo. Character diversity is definately a Huge plus. No one character feels similar to any other. Visuals are very nostalic to those that played older mmorpgs/games with a short of polished feel in comparison. Animations are sort of back and fourth, some are overwhelming while others are quite underwhelming 7-10.
The music can get old relatively quickly but there aren't many games that don't also suffer this way to some degree.
Mechanics are definately a plus. Very complex and alot of playstyles and strategies that can be formulated. Characters don't really NEED a cookie cutter build to perform. Although, if you don't understand how each character works and how each stat works I would look up a guide because if you just wing it you can mess up your character dramatically.
AI's arent super intelligent but they get some pretty dramatic abilities to compensate for this. Basically if you don't do things correctly in the provided situation your dead. Which for some of you hardcore gamers is a wetdream. Have to love the chance of failure and when you succeed it's that much more rewarding. Quests are fairly standard.
There is a learning curve for players new to the genre but it wont take the average human being very long to figure out the basics. The tutorial is lacking theres a broader spectrum in comparison to what the tutorial suggests.
The haven bag system is fairly cool. It's basically a house you carry with you and can expand upon to a certain degree and decorate with trophy's you've aquired or furniture you built through the crafting system, you can even set up workstations for the various crafting systems. You can also enter your haven bag and put items up for sale and if you log out while inside of it, the haven bag stays online and other players can purchase your items.
There are alot of other things I could list about this game but I have a bad habit with writing books instead of reviews so i'll leave it here for now. I'm going to give this game a 10/10 with a big fat needs a playerbase banner right above it.
Good luck and have fun

Funny thing is, I ended up enjoying the game in and of itself. Story was adequate, but nothing special. Hayden's face annoys me when he talks, and his eyebrows are a little frightening.
Mechanics are what made up for everything. Glaive mechanics are really satisfying, and designed well. The gun upgrade system was lackluster, but then again, you don't really ever need to use a gun (except for in the very beginning).
Boss battltes felt larger-than-life, like they ought to, and the moodiness in some of the darker areas (cemetery, morgue, hospital, cathedral) was really well done. The cemetery in particular gave off a lot of excellent spooky vibes, and I enjoyed it.
The end of the game was satisfying, and the last boss battle in particular. The fights were hard, but not frustratingly so. Whenever I died, I felt like it was my fault, instead of bad game design.
All in all, good game. Spooky, you learn more about the origins of Warframe, and it's got a multiplayer feature too (which I haven't really tried out, but seems promising).

Having played a couple of the artistic horror-themed genre of games, i have to say that i'm quite impressed with "Layers of Fear". I will start off with the cons (i have to be honest sorry), followed by the pros.
CONS:
- Linear gameplay, you're constantly forced to open the door in front of you.
There are rooms, where you can choose to either enter or bypass a scary-looking scene , but i feel that the player deserves more than one option in his direction through this horrific game.
it appears to me that the player DOES have choice in choosing some doors to open, so please let there be some more consequences that creates that "OH GOD WHAT HAVE I DONE" moment of terror.
- The fear you experience during the game has a potential of being crippling, but isn't. It needs to be more than simple jumpscares. Rooms that were completely dark and threatening scared the crap out of me. Other rooms were merely disturbing (but in the best way possible, kudos to creating the unique atmosphere in each room)

- Puzzles are few, and extremely easy. If you're gonna have puzzles, they need to be challenging. Don't underestimate the players ability to solve a puzzle.
PROS:
- EXTREMELY INSANELY GODLIKE ARTISTIC DISPLAY AN DESIGN.
- Intriguing and very interesting story. Very enjoyable.
- Amazing sound
- Becomes more scary as the game progresses.
- Anyone with a phobia of anything will probably faint from this experience. The game contains a wide selection of horror elements.
- The game feels autentic to the time-period
- The amount of artistic varity is great.
In conclusion i think the developers should focus more on the "game" part of this "video game".
Otherwise you're looking at a top tier horror game to enjoy.
-End notes-
For players:
- The game is worth more than its price.
For developers:
Consider that you can divide players into:
- Scaredy-cats wanting to complete the game for the sake of bravery
- Intellectuals that wish to uncover and analyze the amazing story and the artistic details
- Classic fearless gamer that plays the game for the sake of gaming
It might be impossible to satisfy all, but adding some sort of OPTIONAL challenge to the classic gamer would be very interesting.

I was anxiously awaiting the release of The Evil Within. When I saw that the game was being directed by Shinji Mikami, I was expecting to play a game that was going to be the spiritual successor to Resident Evil 4. The Evil Within bares many similarities to this game. It attempts to create a suspenseful and gritty gaming experience  by combining horror, tension, and action. Unfortunately, the game simply does not equate to the sum of its parts. The Evil Within, while enjoyable, feels generic, forgettable, and repetitive at times.
The Evil Within is designed and performs like a standard third person shooter. The controls might take a little getting used to, but they are manageable. The game begins as a survival horror. The player starts off with limited resources and must rely on stealth to dispatch enemies.  However, as the game progresses, the player begins to find more ammunition, and The Evil Within begins to focus more on action. The game's arsenal is limited, but still provides the player with enough satisfying options to destroy enemies. Weapons and player attributes are upgradeable through a skill-point system, though health and ammunition cannot be purchased.
The game's plot is intriguing but heavily convoluted and  hard to follow. It's told through a series of cinematic and in-game files. The player will assume control of Sebastian, a detective tasked to investigate an emergency at a mental asylum.  Shortly after arriving, Sebastian is knocked unconscious and separated from his compatriots. He escapes only to find himself in an ever-changing city and stalked by an enigmatic figure. Sebastian has hallucinations and flashbacks, as the game plays on a psychological thriller vibe. There are also several documents the player can find that detail the characters' background and the backstory behind the plot.
Unfortunately, the game keeps jumping between areas and the player is unable to determine what is really happening and what is a hallucination. I understand that this is a story-telling element, but it's overused to the point where players might feel lost and with several questions. Another major fault is the acting and character growth of almost all the characters. Sebastian has the personality of a dead moth and does not appeal or relate to the player.  His demeanor remains unchained throughout the game.  Meanwhile, the game's antagonist, 'Ruvic',  fits almost all the stereotypes for a malevolent genius seeking revenge on society.
So what does the Evil Within get right? The first few hours of the game are set in a dreary rural village. Layers of fog and darkness comb over the nightscape, which is only illuminated by scattered funeral pyres. As soon as I stumbled upon this setting, I felt a gut-wrenching sensation of impending doom and malice.  This theme fits perfectly with the scarcity of ammunition, and will force the player to sneak around the map rather than engaging enemies head-on.  These moments were very tense and pretty much embody the essence of a survival horror genre.  The Evil Within slowly picks up pace, and as aforementioned, becomes more focused on action. Sadly, these segments at times feel mundane and dated, and have the player engaging wave after wave of enemy in a systematic manner.
The Evil Within is not a bad game by any means, but it does not live up to the standards set by Mikami's other titles. The single player campaign will take players  at least a hearty 15 hours to complete.  Many players seem to lose interest in the game mid-way through the game because of the detached  plot  or frustration from the sometimes unforgiving difficulty. I purchased the game when it went on a massive dsicount and enjoyed playing it on a cold winter's weekend. While it's not the spiritual successor to Resident Evil 4 that many Mikami fanatics were waiting for, The Evil Within is still an enjoyable game that features both action-driven and survival horror style gameplay.

This is actually a really fun game. I'm having more fun with it than I originally thought I would be.
Super 3-D Noah's Ark is a labyrinth FPS from the DOS era which used and upgraded Wolfenstein 3D's engine. It added a few cool things like MIDI support and texture-mapped floors and ceilings. This version on Steam has been repolished and ported over to modern operating systems, so now there's no need to use DOSBoX to emulate it!
The quality of this port is really good. The sound quality has been bumped up significantly, it can play in 1080p with true 16:9 aspect ratio (no stretching), the mouselook feels natural and it supports mods. This release also has achievements and trading cards, which is more than what most re-releases or remakes get.
In many ways I think this game is actually better than Wolfenstein 3D. The music is better for sure and there's more enemies scattered about, which leads to more action. The level design is smart. While the levels are maze-like, I have an easier time finding my way around and not being completely lost, like I did a lot with Wolfenstein's lack of color and texture variety. So nevermind the somewhat religious theme, as the game barely even touches upon the story.
The developer of this port is a core developer of ZDoom and ECWolf, and has some involvement with the development of Zandronum. If you play Doom, you likely have already used this guy's work before. The money spent on this game supports the development of the ECWolf engine (the engine this game uses) which will be receiving updates, like online multiplayer. If you take a peak in the forums, you'll understand why this developer is so cool and why he deserves your money. After all, it's just 5 bucks! Which is the same price as Wolfenstein 3D on Steam but without all the fancy upgrades.
If you were into Wolf3D or Ken's Labyrinth, you're gonna love this. Recommended.

News Tycoon puts you in charge of a newspaper company in the golden age of the printed periodical, 2016...  Let me start off by saying this game is not BAD, and I would probably give it a neutral if that was allowed in Steam reviews, but I did refund it and I didn't have fun with it for more than a few moments.  The gameplay basically consists of you picking articles from a repeating list of topics, there is no input during article writing, there is no decisions for you to make outside of which articles you write, what offices go where, and what the layout of your paper looks like.  It's impossible to tell if any of this actually affects anything else because there is far too little feedback given to the player in the game.  No columns are labeled, few values are put into context and there is no tutorial to speak of.  Not to mention the game feels static because you're always in the same view for the most part and doing the same things over and over.  There are some decent automation options it seems, but I was not compelled to use them because the game felt unbalanced, unimpactful, and unrefined.
I would let this one cook for a half year or so and see if it offers more, then bite if so!

As far as I can tell, gameplay revolves around assigning a story - selected from a revolving pool of headlines - to one of your journalists. A progress bar will fill up twice, once for "writing" and once for "proofreading." A number next to “ready to publish” increments by one each time. You choose how often your paper is published (weekly, daily, etc), and every time it is published, “ready to publish” resets to 0 and you get some money based on the quality and relevance of your articles. The relevance is determined by a random number next to each headline – and you know it's random, because nothing exists in the game world besides your office building and the menus you use to put out your paper. Headlines with higher numbers are better. If comparing two numbers to see which is higher is too much for you, there is an “autosearch” button you can use to automate the entire process.
If there is more to it than that, it is well hidden. There is no tutorial or help menu, and there are no tooltips. You can upgrade your building so it holds more offices, or do research for passive buffs for things like increased speed or decreased rent. Leave the game on autosearch and fast-forward for a while to get enough money to do this. You can also hire more journalists to help you. They have various statistics (celebrities, science, politics, etc). I assume this matters behind the scenes, but the pool of “relevant” articles is so small it hardly seems worth fussing over. I took out a loan to get to the end of the game to try out things like “investigations,” but nothing shakes up the core gameplay of watching progress bars fill up (granted, many games focus on that, but there's usually some window dressing or decision making).
While half of the game is patronizingly obvious, another half of the features are just plain baffling. You can choose to have your journalists do “notes,” “articles” or “interviews,” for instance. None of these options are explained, and as someone who works as a newspaper reporter, I can confidently state that this lack of information is not helped with real-world experience. There are also random events. For example, you might lose $42 because people are upset over your paper's article on abortion, even though you didn't write about abortion. Or your article about tennis might cause some scientists to lose a grant. This also subtracts money from your account. The negative events are balanced out by positive events that are just as arbitrary and disconnected, so they don't add a gameplay challenge, they're just odd.
And while this won't matter to many, and I don't want to be mean about this because I'm certain the developers are not native English speakers, grammar and spelling are awful throughout. Given that it's a game about journalism (and even features proofreaders), I had higher expectations for the language localization than I would have for, say, a game about spaceships or pirates.
In summary, the gameplay is too generic and uninvolving to simulate anything, and attempts at making the game about running a newspaper are poorly executed. The developers say Early Access won't last more than 1-2 months, and while that might be enough time to fix existing issues, it's not enough to add the features that are needed to make this game unique or enjoyable.

Clowns... creepy, evil clowns. They're terrorizing the United States, and they've recently made their way in to Canada. Attempting to scare passerby's by standing around in rural areas and places around town, doing... nothing, essentially. So what better time to check out Clown House, a free horror game from 2015. It's also a mobile port.
There's not much to say about Clown House. The game has one moderately sized room, three clowns, and a key that has about 3-5 spawn points at best. The basic rundown is that you're locked in the room with these clowns, and two out of the three of them are murderous; if you kill the innocent one, you lose. In order to kill the evil clowns, you must right click once to bring your gun up, and then right click again to actually shoot. You can't move while you have your gun out.
It's a no brainer to be able to tell which clowns will be the evil ones, they're always the ones closest to the key. Two of them don't even bother to stand up or look at you until you collect the key, anyway. Also, the key is always in plain sight. In short, the title can be won in as little as ten seconds and it offers zero replayability factor. As well, I have no idea why this game has the multiplayer tag on the store page since it's only a single player experience.
There's nothing particularly good or awful about Clown House... but there's no actual reason to play it. Even in game one of the screens says that you're in this house for "no meaningful reason". Whoever reviewed this game for CGMagazine should stick to their unicorns and rainbows, because if this scared them then they don't stand a chance in hell against a real horror title. If you really want to live the experience, spend the minute on Clown House; it actually takes longer to download than it does to beat. Otherwise, your time really can be spent better elsewhere.

Okay so, sarcastic reviews aside, this game is actually pretty fun. If you enjoy Wolfenstein 3D, then you’ll be satisfied with this. The game uses the same modification as the ECWolf mod for Wolfenstein, if you’re familiar with ECWolf it’s exactly the same.
For my review I wanted to compare Super 3D Noah’s Ark to Wolfenstein and what areas are better or worse.
-Theme-
If it wasn’t obvious, this game is a very family-friendly game. Rather than killing enemies you are feeding them to put them to sleep. This is in stark contrast to Wolf3D which was about dropping as many dudes as you encountered. So if the rather light-hearted and, let’s face it, silly nature of the game doesn’t hold a certain charm for you then you probably won’t enjoy it that much.
-Weapons-
Super 3D Noah’s Ark and Wolfenstein 3D are pretty similar in terms of weapons and how they function.  Hand feeding is the knife (that is, melee), the small feed launcher is the pistol, the large feed launcher is the machine gun, and the Super Feeder 5000 is the chaingun. What sets this game apart from Wolf3D is that it has two additional weapons: the cantaloupe feeder and the watermelon feeder. Both of these weapons use alternate ammo from the other weapons and actually deal some splash damage. The cantaloupe feeder fires two rounds in sequence which makes it a decent strafing weapon and the watermelon feeder is great for quickly taking down tough enemies.
-Music-
It loops quite a bit and isn’t very impressive. It maintains the light-hearted theme of the game and the boss level theme isn’t too bad. Not much else to say about it otherwise.
-Levels/Difficulty-
Since this game is geared more towards kids, it is understandably easier than Wolfenstein. Secrets are also more identifiable (at least for me they were) and the game generally leaves more pickups laying around for both ammo and health. The game even features scrolls which pose a trivia question about Noah’s ark and reward the player with health. As far as the level design goes, I think the game does a very good job. Some of the earlier levels feel longer than the early Wolf3D levels but the game is considerably shorter than Wolf3D. What really impressed me are the boss fights. At the start of each chapter you are told what animal you will need to put to sleep. The fights themselves have very well designed stages around them. They have plenty of room to fight, spots to hide when things get dicey, additional enemies to distract you/add more challenge, and side rooms to run away from the boss. These fights are surprisingly robust in comparison to Wolf3D’s bosses. So even though most enemies don’t take too much to dispatch, they can sneak up on you and take you out very quick if you are not careful.
-Final Conclusion-
The game is good. Get it if you enjoy Wolfenstein 3D and want to see better bosses and more weapons. Don’t get if you don’t like the light-hearted theme or dislike the looping music.

After finishing the game on survival nightmare and akumu it was easy to see what the game did right and wrong.
Despite some gameplay flaws I find myself returning to it again and again to see if I can find another way of surviving an area with a new tactic that may conserve more ammo or make the confrontation a lot easier.
There may be some linear moments but more often then not there is a suprising amount of variety in how a given situation can be handled.
The Evil Within's gmeplay is very similar to Resident Evil 4 with slightly more freedom in movement. Despite this improvement the game is a lot harder overall with the absence of the ability to quick attack stunned enemies, use a knife at any time from a still position(punches move the player forward), or easily stun enemies with headshots. The hareder difficulty unfortuantley makes issues that existed in RE 4's gameplay become much more apparent in TEW.
For instance, monsters that compelety missed a grab or punch will sometimes register as a hit. If an enemies grab animation starts just as a freeze bolt hits the enemy it will not register as a hit on the enemy and they will continue to deal damage on the player.
As stated previously these issues did exist in RE 4 but they become more apparent in the harder difficulty of TEWparticularly when playing on Akumu mode where one hit will kill.
TEW is a much darker game then the later resident evil entries. It is also less action focused. It still has a lot more action then the earlier resident evil games that focused a lot more on exploration, puzzles and backtracking diffrent areas.
The game could have benifited a lot more with areas that allowed more exploration and suspense before moving so quickly in to the action sequences but overall it is a very well balanced game.
The PC version initially had a lot of issues but recent patches have done a lot to improve the overall stability and experience for the PC version of the game.
Overall I'd give the game a 8.7 out of 10.
I personally I enjoyed this game more then other game in past year or so. Mostly due to the lack of games that are like this (and the poor execution of recent RE titles). But it definitely has a lot of room for improvement and considering this is a new IP that means there could be a lot to look forward to in the future DLC and possible sequals.

So, I finally beat the game after going at it one chapter per night with some rest days between. It was a hell of a ride and in my opinion it would have been THE horror game had the last five chapters been as amazing as chapters 3-10. When the final tally was spinning I was terrified that I'd entered into three digit death territory after my 21 hour playthrough. I would have been legit ashamed, but thankfully (somewhat) I only died 88 times on survivor difficulty.
The bosses in this game can be the worst if you aren't observant. I tried to kill Laura for a good while at first because I wasn't paying full attention to my environment and her weaknesses. Really, this game is all about watching the bosses, watching the environments and moving constantly. Fire is your best friend in this game. If you are fighting a sub-boss or a boss and you are staying still it won't be pretty. The agony bolt REALLY showed it's stuff in the later boss battles with the capabilities of the flash, lighting and freeze bolts. If an enemy couldn't be flashed then it probably means you can freeze it or paralyze it for a few seconds to reload your weapons and make some spare explosive bolts. I probably died forty times to regular bosses and 3/4ths of it happened before chapter 10 because I moved, but didn't observe and I shot, but I didn't think to use anything more than explosive bolts+regular weapons. The bosses are creative/tough, but very beatable once you realize how useful the other bolts really are.
That said, up untl chapter 10 TEW was amazing and chapters 13-14 got sort of close to that feeling again. Chapter 15 was okay, but the highlight really was the final boss fight because until the finale stone face Seb just couldn't react to any of the crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥in the final chapter until Ruvik went all Kaiju on his♥♥♥♥♥ Ruvik really managed to get a reaction out of Sebastian with that. Clearly the game is begging for a sequel because neither of the major two stories (Sebastian's and Ruvik) had a satisfying conclusion. Kidman's role in the story is also still shrouded in mystery.
The lighting, sound, enemy variety and resource management were tuned to literal perfection. I feel like these were the things Tango did best. Every chapter had gorgeous lighting with blacks that weren't crushed, appropriately revealing lighting and beautiful lighting effects on water, foliage and architecture (especially humid indoor environments). The sound design was particularly on the dot. Chapter 13 was particularly good about it (the hallways full of haunted and fake R****). Did anyone else notice that killing the first fake R**** and moving forward a bit caused more haunted to appear behind you? Very very few games actually do a good job of giving enemies proper sound direction and placement. The Evil Within on the other hand passed that test with flying colors and probably saved me quite a few times since the amazing sound reproduction warned me when someone was coming from 3 o clock,  9 o clock or 12 o clock. My only complaint was the tiny sound produced by the magnum which sounds tinier than the pistol. The enemy variety complimented the scarcity of resources perfectly too. My only complaint was the low number of invisible haunted. I'd have liked for the total number in the game to be more like 10-12 instead of the 4-5 we got. This game was chocked full of regular haunted, but it never got tiring thanks to regular appearances by slightly higher level opponents and challenging environments (multilevel, trap laced, open and tight spaces were all available). Every chapter started with a handful (or two at best) of bullets for your pistol and a handful for the rest along with a bolt or two of each type and I played very conservatively with lots of headshots and group burnings via matches. By the end of chapter 6 anyone playing on survival difficulty should be an ammo saving pro at any game.
The real weaknesses for me were the characters (or lack of), the gigantic bars, chapters 11-12, minimal movement abilities, the weak story and storytelling devices. Sebastian just didn't react at all even though things around him were going all Dead Space by chapter 14 and it can really take you out of the mood when someone doesn't react to this craziness. Kidman is another one. We heard almost nothing from her. I think all her lines could be written on a standard notebook page in extra large font. Joseph was sort of mundane, but I can sort of see from his personality that it's what they were going for. Unfortunately the game rarely (if ever) took a chance to move the story along with storytelling devices. Resident Evils 3 and below all did wonderful jobs with the creepy journal entries/lab notes (Metroid Prime also managed to instill a slight feeling of dread with the scanning storytelling ability), but Ruvik kept details a bit too vague in the audio logs. Now, the more technical gameplay weaknesses to me were on full display in chapters 11-12 (except 11's mannequin scene) and after experiencing them chapters 13-14 lost a bit of their luster. Somehow I was completely in love and I had almost forgotten the black bars until chapter 11 in the city. These stupid bars are downright fatiguing and I finally began to understand the complaints when I found my head hurting after a lot of squinting up/down to get a full look at the gradual destruction of Krimson city. Thankfully the headaches never came back for chapters 13 and over. The uncomfortable feeling I and a lot of other people have gotten from the camera would probably be helped by regaining that huge 30(+) percent of screen real estate taken up by those bars. Reducing the bar size and increasing the FOV will be the first order of business when I finally start my NG+ run. The movement in the game was also way too stilted for my taste. A simple roll like the one in Demon's Souls and Dark Souls combined with a basic manual cover system would make this game's combat scenarios almost perfect if they came with better (i.e. less exaggerated) melee animations. Some of the boss fights and all the group battles in this game would be immensely more fun and fluid if Sebastian could dance around them a bit and dodge dramatically when a boss is about to crush him or drag him to his death.
Based on the demo I'd have never expected anything less than an 8/10, but the version I played sits at the best 7/10 a game can get. I expect FOV and bar fixes will push it up to a solid 8, but all the modding in the world isn't going to improve the admittedly great (but not perfect) combat and weak story/characters. If ANY game needs a sequel it's TEW. I really hope this holiday season was great for Bethesda and Tango because a little more heat and pressure is going to give us a real diamond if they decide to follow up and polish what needs polishing. I got the game for $16 thanks to GMG so I should probably buy a season pass for the DLC (never bought a season pass for a game before) in order to show my support for the IP and Tango.
Even my modest i5 2500k setup held a solid 30FPS with everything maxed at 1080p with SMAA. Anyone with a GTX 580/660 and above should be able to play TEW at 30FPS even without overclocking. Those lucky 4GB card owners should have no problem downsampling the game too. The PC version is the way to go with this game, people.

I enjoy wakfu's visuals and the music a lot.
I can write thousands of pages of text just complementing the beutiful music. Each Nation has its own pleasent theme ... and if you joined Brakmar looking forward to the music ... just make another character and next time don't join Brakmar. I love Amakna's pleasent music while grinding crops and monsters. Each track is unique and colorfull, unless your in Brakmar, which is themed with more depressing music.
The visuals are also very pleasant, I enjoy the color scheme a lot and the animations too.
Though, gameplay is a different thing. Sometimes it might take a while to try to click something that is behind an object or something that is too close to another object that can be interacted with. I enjoy the different classes, but sometimes it takes too long to fight to a higher level with characters other than your main one. Though fighting relies heavily on grinding.
Wakfu doesn't just have fighting though, the way the environment works is really cool and really fun to play with. If you chop down all the trees in one area, new ones won't grow back by defalt, or when they do only a small amount grows back. And the area's owner (NPC) also has a satisfaction thing where, if you toy with things and change the quantity of something lower than the satisfaction minimum or maximum, you will start loosing nation citizenship points. If those points go lower than zero, you will be considered an outlaw to your nation. There are consequences for destroying too many things or planting too many things (this also applies to monsters). But don't worry, since this restriction isn't on every monster/ plant in the area, just some of them. You also have easy access to the gauge that will show you each of the populations of the monster/ plant group and it's easy to see where the 'satisfaction area' is.
Wakfu also has crafting but some things just have too many materials that are hard to get that isn't worth the item you're making. There are a lot of items that you can mass craft with only a few materials and are worth crafting.
My favorite part of Wakfu though, is the player market. Most of my enjoyment has been from using the player market and checking Haven bags for good stuff. When I mass craft items, I can also mass sell them and get a lot of in-game money for it. Then I can save up for expensive items that players sell. Sometimes I'm able to get something that was bought from the greater shop (The shop where you can buy costumes and pets and more with in- game money that you have to get by paying real money). Wakfu is really fun with it's market, and if you play for long enough, you can get compansation tokens from the bugs that have happened (they're to apologize for the bugs), and then trade them in for A LOT of kamas (the name of the in- game money). I got 200,000 (A lot of money, a lower level item is about 50 - 100 kamas in a fair sale) kamas just from compansation money. It's really fun and easy to earn kamas from mass selling items, and you earn enough to make yourself happy even if you didn't earn a whole ton of money, and you won't earn too much money that would make you satisfied and stop selling items.
There is a bit of a problem with the inventory space, so conserving is vital and you will probably spend a while thinking "should I drop this or this?."

I decided to recommend this game because there are already so many negative reviews out there, and I feel like the game is being underrated. But the fact is I wouldn't recommend this game to everyone, only if you fulfil the following criteria:
1.	You liked Deus Ex: Human Revolution
2.	The above made you go out and buy the book Deus Ex: Icarus effect
3.	You liked the book
The reason for this is that the game focuses on Benjamin Saxon, one of the main characters in the book, and it’s really cool to play him. The story takes place right after the end of the Icarus effect and it’s quite true to the events that take place there, there are even some recreations of the events in the book (I won’t get into details so there are no spoilers), and the dialogs are pretty much untouched from what you’ve read in the book. All of this makes for a good overall experience when playing the game, because you get to know what happens after the end of the book, and the story is very solid.
The thing is that that’s pretty much it… The graphics are indeed horrible, the mouse look doesn’t work at 100% (the vertical axis his way less sensitive than the horizontal axis), you can’t change the controls (although for me that wasn’t really a problem). As for the audio issues, I didn’t come across anything. If you play the game with a headset, you should be fine.
This being said, I’ll go on the L.I.M.B here and dare to say that gameplay wise, there are even some small improvements compared to HR. There are some cool new augs like the stealth dash and the body armor is no longer a passive aug. In HR this made the body armor a must get upgrade, because the result was that it made the game easier without any management. In The Fall, you have to manage when to activate it (which consumes energy) and when it activates it creates a glow around Saxon and you see a meter that tells you how much armor you have left and it drops when you take damage.
There’s been some talk about the game ending in a cliff hanger but I don’t think that’s the case. The story isn’t finished, that’s obvious, but it wraps things up in that specific mission scenario. If part 2 ever comes out (which looks very unlikely, considering how things are going in Square Enix), I’ll want to play it, even if it’s flawed like the first one because for me the story is worth it and the flaws don’t make the game unplayable.

As much as I love the first game in the series, Hotline Miami 2 falls short for me as far as the campaign goes. It has a great story, certainly, but the characters and their specialties range from fun to frustrating. Level design is alright, but focuses too much on wide open areas that can occasionally feel unfair, allowing offscreen enemies to snipe you. It creates a sense of trial and error, but that sense is lost on later levels that go on for much too long. I'm talking, for the most part, about a jungle area that I felt killed the entire game for me. One of my favourite games on Steam, easily. It will usually go on sale so you can pick it up then, but it's worth the money IMO, considering you will be spending literally hundreds of hours playing this game, it's DLC, and the mods made for it.
Mount & Blade: Warband is a "medieval" sandbox that allows you to control an entire army composed of the units of your choosing (there is a wide range) where you are their commander and aspiring ruler of the world (if you choose). You can engage in battles ranging from 10 vs 5 to 800 vs 800 where you are your own player giving commands to your army. This includes open field battle, multiplayer skirmishes, and full castle sieges. The combat is very fun, can be played in both third person or first person, and is fairly challenging.

If you get bored of Calradia, you can download a mod and try to conquer Westeros, or any other fantasy world mod developers have created.
Overall, this game certainly offers a lot, is highly entertaining, and is difficult to get bored of. Highly recommended.

A third person shooter with a cover feature and a twist: a "glaive" you can throw at enemies and it comes back to you. Mostly unoriginal, heavily inspired by Half Life 2, originally made for consoles, looks like another victim of publishers. It's fun to play, but has clunky keyboard/mouse controls and a not very entertaining take on combat challenges. I had to play it in god mode (cheat engine) because of the controls, and I enjoyed it. No regrets for money spent. I suspect that originally the story events took place in Poland, or Romania, or Hungary, and later they hastily changed it to Russia, to please the publishers. Because there's nothing Russian there except for Google-translated labels on crates. Sometimes I'd get stuck, not knowing where to go, which was actually a breathe of fresh air after all these modern games that tend to hold your hand and drag you along the script. The story makes an impression of something made up in a hurry, but while being nothing special it isn't insulting either. I like how it drops you in the middle of some action and you're figuring out what it all means. Also I like how you are forced to think and come up with some ideas when you're dealing with bosses - it's not just shooting it X times to kill it. It even has some economy, you can buy guns and upgrade them. It felt a bit short, but then again - it would have gotten really boring, be it any longer. Keeping all that in mind, you're welcome to give it a go, especially if it's on a sale. A sequel with better controls and updated graphics would be not a bad idea. Throwing this glaive was quite fun, especially when charging it with elements.

I say this because most of what the game promises to offer is not even implemented yet. There is not much to do besides hire engineers, buy and build buildings that are pointless and take anywhere from 2-12 months to build, have your engineers research things that take anywhere from 20-500 or more months to research and are also pointless. Also, it takes only 2 months to build an entire facility, yet 4 or more years to research the properties of anything, like alloy or fabric? I could do that in two weeks, on my own! Not with 30 other engineers helping me research!
Another note: The grammar. The grammar is horrible. However, for the most part they use commas correctly (most people in the world don't), but there are huge spelling mistakes and other, much larger grammar mistakes, as well as careless typos like missing letters or words or extra letters or words. And one of the only two working buildings is not even in English.
Overall: The game is crap right now and should not have yet been released to the public. But the game does have very great potential for the future, though not really as a space game. It's mosly more of a political and waiting game.
It seems that at this point in production, and the rate at which they are updating (not at all yet), this game will be done in a few years, if not decades if not centuries.

Fairly unique game. I myself am not too much into horror games(played plenty, just didn't like them), but decided to pick this one up anyway as I like the setting.
The game is simply good, it's by no means a "masterpiece"(pun intended) like Amnesia TDD, but it holds fiercy in the kind of shallow genre horror games are to begin with. The storyline is interesting, but unfolds at a pace too slow to grant any clever player plot twists. Most of it turned out to be surprisingly obvious just by reading the first clues in the game. That being said, you will want to read all the notes and will thus be searching everything in an attempt to find what exactly happened. There're some unecessary gimmicks which I won't spoil, but most of it makes perfect sense within a proper horror story. That being said, the storyline is not awfully original but knows interesting characters. There're revelations which make you think loudly "well that was uncalled for" as they turn the story in the direction of a generic drama tale. But overall it's OK and motivates you to see how the next "layer" is going to be depicted(quite literally I might add).
The graphics are of very good quality. This game looks very good. I also happily add that the sound design is as good. The gameplay is very simple, it consists most of reading, looking at stuff and walking. If you happen to be a hardcore horror player who wants to be scared straight this isn't exactly going to be your cup of tea.
Overall this game is worthy of a good 7,5 or perhaps even 8 out of 10. It tells a predictable but well written story(it genuinely made me sad at one point) visualized in a stunningly beautiful game. At the cut price as it comes this game is most definitely worth it.

This is a side-scroller, inspired quite a lot by Super Meat Boy. This is not a bad thing by any means, it just means that if you didn't like that game at all, you probably will not enjoy this one either.The controls are tight enough, the sound design is competently executed, especially in the later stages, where it goes from good to great. I love the space theme music.
The bosses were a nice touch, which I really apreciated, except for the dinosaur one, who was more annoying that difficult, because there was nowhere to stand to not get hit by the claw except for the springs, which open you up for the laser attack.
The whole game has this 90s' feel, but not just because of the graphics or sounds, it's the gameplay itself, the backgrounds and the premise of the game that, while not new , kept me coming back to see its conclusion. Now that I have finished it, however, I doubt I will come back to replay it, or to try to get the trophies or the gems.
I do have minor complaints:
First of all, there are multiple characters, which is good, but they're not just reskins of GunGuy, they actually play different, in the sense that some shoot faster, some deal more damage and so on. I would like to see some sort of description for the characters, in which they're abilities are described or at least hinted at, something like "Gunguy has a knack for finding chicken in unlikely places" or something like that for every character.
Secondly, can you please make the dissapearing platforms flicker or something before they dissapear, because it's really frustrating to jump at a platform when I start the level, only to find it vanishing below my feet.
All in all, I recomend this game to anyone who has an itch for old-school "difficult", especially FUN action platformer.

If you like original Resident Evil games, you will probably like The Evil Within. It took about 15-20 hours to finish it, but I find it really hard even on "medium" difficulty (died almost 100 times).

The Evil Within doesn't try to do anything exceptionally new in the genre of Survival Horror, but that's part of why I love it so far.
It has solid mechanics, excellent visuals, a storyline that has me interested, and enemies that are a challenge without feeling unfair.  It also has RPG upgrade mechanics to let you tackle things your way instead of just having 'oh the shotgun is better than the handgun'.
If you must have your games be super innovative or new, I would not bother with Evil Within.  If classic Resident Evil-like Survival Horror is your comfort zone, jump right in.  It has enough of the more psychological Silent Hill style stuff to keep it enjoyable on that level, but it slants further towards RE4.

Lost a "defend this point" level because we were killed by INVISIBLE ENEMIES.
Not the first time that had happened either, but it was the first time it cost us a victory. In fact, it occurred in each of the 4 missions I had time to play during the free weekend.
A brief search of the forums tells me that this problem has existed for a long time (found a discussion dated December 2015, probably goes back even further) and has gone unfixed and/or unexplained.
To elaborate, we killed all the enemies we could see, but continued to take damage. We weren't being shot, or poisoned or taking any obvious damage. We also couldn't "kill" these invisible enemies. Swinging our weapons hit nothing. We died, lost our progress and summarily gave up on the game because of this.
I'm glad this game had a free weekend, because if I'd spent any money on this, I would've been annoyed. Bugs like this should not make it into final release. They definitely should not go unfixed for 6 months or more. Players shouldn't lose because of incompetent programming.

This game is absolutley one of my favorite First-Person games I've played in a couple years. I love the combat system in this
game, though it may remind you of a certain series (Left 4 Dead, also one of my favorite games of all time). Using the lore of Warhammer: End Times is a great concept and though I am prasing this game I still have some issues with it. So here is my list of Pros and Cons with the game.
Pros: 1. The combat system: The use of both hand to hand and ranged weapons in the game gives that since of immersion that a lot of FPS' don't have these days.
2. The lore: I myself didn't know a lot about Warhammer lore before I played this game, as a matter of fact I was hyped about it because of the new Total War title that was coming out. After playing 5 hours of this game I was hooked, I researched a lot about Warhammer fantasy and now I'm looking at 40K(and it is amazing)!
Cons:
1. Repetition: Like it says though I've only played 15 hours of this game and it is not because I don't like it, I love this game. The reason I don't play this game like I used to is because I just got repetitive. The main villian of the game are known as the Skaven, ( giant rat people) and its like Left 4 Dead in the sense that you fight the same enemies ever level.
Same bosses, same infantry, the one redeeming factor about this is that you can counter the enemies quickly.
2. The Grind: This part of the game makes me sad. To get descent weapons you are going to have to play the same levels
over and over and over again just to get enough XP and gemstones to upgrade and get loot. With the each DLC comes more objectives and weapons, but to get them takes close to 8 hours of grinding. My group of friends and I would try and get loot and it took us 4 hours of playing the same exact levels! That is a major problem with this game.
Overall, this game is great for the price and it will definitely provide you with hours of fun and grinding

This game is fun for Trekkie fans and it is fun...  for a while.  After you hit Level 50, it becomes a grind fest for prisitige, dilithium, and special sets.  The story is decent, and the controls are good, but after a while, it gets old.  And there is almost NO content for the Klingon side and Cryptic/Perfect World has stated they have NO plans to add any Kilngon content.
If you like MMOs like WoW and FF11, you'll like this, but if you hate grindfests, steer clear.
EDIT: Finally, I have time for a proper review!  This review is during the recent release of Delta Rising expansion.
Graphics:
The graphics are quite good.  Not as good as mmos like TERA or Final Fantasy XIV, but they are good.  The graophic options also let people with less powerful machines play.  I know, I used to run off of an INTEGRATED gfx card!  There is some slight pop-ups in large enviroments.  There is some lag in areas with a large amount of players (Undine Battlezone sometimes slows to a slideshow when many people are there), but most of the time, the game runs fine.
Sound:
The sound effects are good and the retro weapon's sound effects (like the Type 2 Phaser and The Retrofit Phaser Arrays) are faithfully recreated, but there are a limited number of songs that play and after a while, and they are quite bland so they will get annoying after a while.
Control:
The control is quite competant with keyboard and mouse and that is what I would reccomend for playing.  There are FAR too many buttons required to effectivly play on a gamepad.  With keyboard/mouse, you can set your many skills to keybindings with an easy skill try and can even set to fire weapons individualy or set to all fire at once and autofire in space.  On ground, you can switch between rpg combat control and fps controls, and both are fun and easy, and with a few clicks, you can issue orders to your away teams.  But sometimes, skils won't activate when clicked, leading to problems during tense combat situations.
Gameplay:
The missions are out together like a typical episode of Star Trek, which several small objectives put together with abundant story, be it with combat, gathering or other science objectives.  Missions usually last about an hour and are fun!  And when you're done with the game's main story arcs (or just want to take a break from the story), you can play Foundry (user-created) missions!  The issue is that getting end game gear is VERY grind heavy.  You must grind for marks, dilithium (dilithium or one of the game's FOUR currencies) and a component to get access and free players may only refine 8000 dil a day.  And with the recent DR expansion, the components are now almost impossible to get.  Still, even with that, it is still fun to play this game.
So yes, if you are a Trekkie (or Trekker) or just a general sci-fi nerd, give this game a go!  But if you don't like heavy grinding, you may wanna give it a pass.
Its free, fun, has a lot of player created missions that let you make your own storylines or play episodes others had made.

I hate to have to say it, but I agree with most of the reviews and the meta score on this one. Being a huge fan of the Deus Ex game series, especially Human Revolution, I was underwhelmed when I started and completed this game. Upon purchase I saw that the game had terrible reviews and scores however since it was on sale, I decided to buy it and play it without prejudice. With that said I was extremely disappointed and I will explain why.
At this stage of the game, patches have clearly fixed many of the problems that people have talked about. I had no issue with bugs in the short duration the game lasted. That if course is always a good thing.
Obviously coming from playing Human Revolution, I had high expectations for this game on many levels. Upon entering the start up screen, I immediately went into check graphics settings and control settings. The options were poor to say the least. I was able to change anistrophic filtering and that was about it. There really was no other say when it came to the graphics of the game. On that note, the graphics were not that big of an issue for me. I was pleased with them. Although not as good as Human Revolution, it was perfectly fine for its purposes.
Once starting the game I was interested by the story. I like were the story picked up from and how a good amount of the information could be found from in game play. Just like Human Revolution your Augs can greatly help you evaluate conversations. Unfortunately there were not many coversations to be had. Even for the short duration, there are only three or four side missions that you come across without trying extremely hard. The missions are easy and just simply involve a lot of travel between the few small levels of the small map.
That is my next issue. Travel in this game is boring! There are only five or six trully distinct locations that you must travel to in order to complete the game. An hour into the game, I felt like I was just going back and forth constantly and I was already bored enough to put the game down.
The duration of the game however is my ultimate issue. Not having read any of the comments for this game, i really was expecting another full on Deus Ex game. By the game description and the story that starts to unfold, you would expect so much more, rather than a To Be Continued. I love Deus Ex to the point where I search every single room, air duct and storage unit. Even thouroughly searching through the game, It only took me four hours to complete. i was just messing around looking around and only took that long!
Overall the Deus Ex series is amazing but this game, at this point at least, is honestly not worth it. I was extremely disappointed that I bothered with it. The only real reason to have it is to say you at least own every game in the series. Thats all it's really good for. If you do choose to buy this game, do not get your hopes up and set any expectations you have extremely low.
I really don't enjoy having to right a poor review for a game especially such as this series, but such a horrible game warrants such a review. Best of luck to anyone who does decide to play. At least you can play the game again with all your current augs and purchases but on an increased difficulty.

This game is a port of a mobile game, with that comes alot of bugs, glitches, bad graphics.  Plus its real, real, real, short.  Any non-fans of Deus Ex Human revolution should avoid this game like the plague.  DO NOT BUY unless your a die hard Deus Ex HR fan, see the HR thats critical bcause people who are Deus Ex fans but hated HR would hate this too.
All that horrible stuff aside for Deus Ex HR fans its an interesting game.  Be warned the game in parts has real bad graphics with terrible textures.  Many things are PS2 era in the level of graphics, while other things are HD, so its a weird hybrid.  The atmosphere is done perfectly along with the music.  For a mobile port its pretty impressive, there is tons of dialog, and a train that moves, the city really captures that Deus Ex feeling well.  The story ties into Deus Ex, but the letdown is this is short, as in you go to one place in Panama city for missions and thats it, the game ends.  This game was supposed to be episodic but there are currently no plans to make more episodes.  Combat in the game is done only one way right and that is with stealth, the AI seems as bad as Deus EX HR, so if you were ok with that it should work here.  The takedowns are hilarious, you will sometimes not even appear near the person you takedown, for some reason they may warp across the room, showing you taking down a ghost while in the background you may see the enemy going down.  While the bugs are funny, the game does work, it doesnt crash, Deus Ex games were always pretty bad at combat its the story and atmosphere that drive them, this game pulled that part off, but with a cliff hanger at the end of the episode and nor more planned its enjoyable just to play through the golden glory of what is Deus Ex.
ONLY play this with a controller, DO NOT BUY even if you are a fan if you are going to use a mouse.  The k/m controls are broken, often the screen will spin in circles, certain augs will make you constantly rubber band, yet  oddly none of that exists with a controller.  The hacking is broken with a controller yet is flawless with a mouse so gotta use both.  Sound difficult?  Then get some augs to handle what it takes to ride the cyber punk express.
Rating for Deus EX HR Fans:  10/10  Value:  $2.50
Rating for NON Deus Ex Fans:  0/10  Value:  $0.00

Layers of Fear is a psychedelic horror game and let me tell you; it really lives up to that genre. The game is infested with mind-blasting tunes that just seem to beautiful yet eerie, adding to the already dark atmosphere. The latter sums up the game as there is so much to see and click that you are automatically sucked in by the story and the atmosphere. Throughout the story (so far) the main objective, creating an ultimate painting laden with mind blazing darkness, is very successfully accomplished. 30-40 minutes into the game you begin thinking whether you're high on LSD, that's just how vivid the game becomes as the pictures begin to morph and the game begins to puzzle your mind with tricky scenarios; wherever you turn your camera something will happen, doors will lock themselves, eyes will look at you, and much more. It really is a psychedelic horror game as I found myself in chills various times throughout the 1.4hr-ish campagn so far.
Sound: 9.5/10 - The game has fantastic soundtrack and terrifying sounds that play throughout the story to fill your mind with terror
Story: 8/10 - Could use much more polishing as you are practically thrown into the game without a clue as to whats happening, slowly beginning to understand just what exactly is going on whilst picking up art pieces.
Fear: 10/10 - The game consistently throws new traumatic occurences your way, making you believe that there is no shred of sanity left inside you. Perfect jump scares and an eerie atmosphere make it difficult for me to not give the spooky department a 10/10
Other: 8/10 - The game is extremely short as of now but during that length, its truly brilliant. Other things such as a lack of replayability also take away from the final experience. One thing I found myself wondering was why the developers built so many dressers and shelves with a multitude of items within them that you cant even use.
Overall: 88/100 - A freaking fantastic game with a promising future, but lack of content atm and too many tools that you cant use simply hurt its final score.
As of now it really isnt worth $10 because the story is just 1h30min long but in the future, the $10 will be the biggest bargain ever

The game overall is around a 2 hour game if you take your time. It is very well worth the money!!! It has great graphics, great voice acting, a great storyline, and it feels like it is already a finished game. This is by far better than Silent Hills P.T. The scenery and gameplay reminds me of parts of the recent Tomb Raider game...but Tomb Raider did it better.  The graphics and character controls are, quite bluntly, ugly and clunky here--they made me want to go back and replay a GOOD game, like Alan Wake...which is like, 4 years old and looks WAY better. Stability is still a problem. I experienced crashes with an error message 3 times while playing, twice while loading the same map. My friend also experienced the same load times.
tl;dr: Fun L4D mechanics, poor stability and optimization.

Let get this over with....this game is a clone of Left for Dead using Ratmen instead of zombies. Easy to pick up and play for a couple of hours, if playing with online friends. However, there in lies the problem. There are not many online players anymore and most of the ones still out there are higher level players who don't want to play the game for what it is, but just want to run through mission to get through to the end for a chance to get loot (farming). Thus making the game less enjoyable for new players or those that actually want to kill the ratmen. This also dimished the whole team-work concept and thereby defeating co-op. Solo play with the bots is not fun because the bots' AI is pretty bad. So you no longer have a casual game. If the community is not there and the devs are not there to add new content and fix bugs then its not worth spending $17 bucks on this game. The F2P weekend had given me the opportunity to take a peek in this game, which I thought might be the heir to Left 4 Dead 2.
My first impression was good. And remember before reading this review, that I recommend this game, but there are a few things, that I have to point out:
The Warhammer atmosphere is on point. At first, I was a little overhelmed by the selection of five characters, not to speak of the equipment & loot system. I went into the breach with the Imperial the first few missions, but had to figure out a lot by myself. A tutorial would be really nice to understand the game mechanics such as tomes&dogding. Either way, I've learned a lot from my teammates, which is the essential source of knowledge the first few rounds. The battlesystem is really pleasuring for people like me who are into first person hack 'n slaying. But on holdout events, it can be a little confusing when the view is just a mess of splatter and sewered heads.
The placing&frequence of the special scaven seemed random for me. After a few runs on "Bell of Magnus" I noticed that this can be quite unfair, if the Tank is suddenly accompanied by 3-4 special scaven. The spawning isn't perfect and sometimes a pack of scaven just appeared out of nowhere in front of me.
After each round, the absolutely addictive loot system comes in play. It's a really nice thing to finally have a reward for carrying 3 tomes & 2 grimmoires arround the whole time. After the tension of the match here comes once more a rush of excitement to get another high tier item for your favorite hero. But even if luck is not on your side, you can do other fancy stuff with the gained items, like scrapping them or fusing five of them together for a better quality item.
It's really recommendable that you get this game with a few friends, the matchmaking wasn't always that reliable.
Currently, the developers announced, that they will be optimizing the Coop experience. But I'm really looking forward to a  PvP option, because the potential of a true Left 4 Dead 2 heir is there, and it got a lootsystem :3

Once, I found myself in in a tower at a brigde over a river. I had been promoted to sniper in the american army and got a M1903 with scope. There was a point in this battle where we was able to turn the war and was near to get an advantage. The Russian had the point by the river in a house. There was myself and another american soldier. An infantarist with Thompson sub machine gun. He ran to the point, shoot the two russians at point. When he started capture the sone, more russian advance on his location. I count 5-6 person, more than what he could take out himself. I take point in the tower, aim down sight find the first russian with a PPSh, and shoot. Headshot and he was down. Than I shoot 3 more two with semi-automatic rifles and one with a LMG. The last person was shoot by the infanterist in the capture sone. At this point the capture point was secured, but an russian sniper shoot at me. I try to hide, and understand that I must be quick and accurate if  should survive this. I stand up, take aim and shoot. Another headshot. More russians advance on the capture point. More than what myself and the infanterist could take out. Just before two of the russian should storm the point a Hellcat and a M8 started supporting us, with firepower and manpower. This was the point where we started get an advantage and after one hour of fight we stand victorious.
This means that this game is very good. It has everything I can think of that is presented in war: Infanteri, tanks, planes, snipers, etc. This game still need to be worked on. A super fun MMO that really is FREE to play. You can get all the way from 1 to 50 (max level currently) without spending a dime. Sure, there are some neat goodies you can buy (and I often do) but they aren't game breaking and you can get to max level and earn in game money just selling off parts of the ships you blow up or from mission rewards. For example, you are rewarded with a new ship each time to earn a rank (evern few levels) OR you can spend some money and buy the same ship with a different skin and an extra officer slot and a fun console (grappling hook, low damage auto turret, etc.) but the ship reward is just perfectly fine to go out and blow up bad guys with.
The community is top notch and (as would be expected) are a Star Trek lovin' bunch. Lots of great fleets to join as well as all level of RPers.
Character customization is top notch (as you would expect from Crypic) and the ability to customize the look of your crew is a big bonus. From Borg to Ferengi, hell, throw a few Pakleds on your bridge crew. Most of the major races are represented as well as a few of the lesser known ones. Or just make up your own with the character creator.
Ground combat and exploration is fun but the game really shines in space combat. You can level in PVE, PVP or let your crew do the work and send your duty officers and crew off to do assignments. It's up to you.
All in all, it's my go to MMO for when I'm "between games" and since it's F2P I can always hop back in and pick up where I left off. It has a permanent spot on my hard drive.

I'm going to go ahead and rate this as a game alone because as a 360/ps3 port it sucks. With multiple posts in the discussion about ways to fix graphical issues. I still could not manage to calibrate this game to my exact monitor resolution and ended up having to run the game way below my specs.
None the less! As a game Dark Sector can be really fun. As you progress through the game you will unlock more weapons, get to ride four legged tanks, acquire more elements for your glaive (blade boomerang), and go from having just your arm infected to having a full blown exo suit! The storyline can be mildly forgettable (Big Bad Guy who wants all the power) but the game makes up for it with it's dark atmosphere, crisp power suit design, and responsive combat situations. Now I don't know about picking up the game at full price as there are a lot of other games out there with far more modern features on them. Though when the next sale comes around and the game drops down to 50% off. I highly suggest you purchase it as it is a fun little time waster and the combat system and lore within helped pave the way towards "Warframe" which is one of the top played games on Steam.

As a fan of Warframe, I decided to take a look at Dark Sector, the supposed prequel to the Warframe lore. However while this game may have that within, I couldn't be bothered to go beyond chapter 4.
At first I couldn't even load up the game properly, it would just futz around like a fish out of water trying to display in the right resolution. It wasn't until I found a guide on Steam as to how to properly config the game before startup, which revealed to me how laughably bad this port was.
As for the gameplay, being a product of the cover-shooting era of gaming, that is literally all the game is: find convenient waist-high cover to plop behind and just start shooting or throwing your glaive. Obviously none of the high-speed acrobatics that Warframe is known for, but Dark Sector just plays super slow in general. Sprinting feels bad, rolling feels bad, melee combat feels bad, and Hayden has the frailty of a wet sheet of paper. The only thing that really felt good was pulling off insta-killing power throws with the glaive. And even then I got to a point where I realized that the glaive was the end all be all weapon at mid-to-close range, so guns became almost silly to use.
Overall, I just feel like this game has been a victim of bad aging; gunplay is super clunky and unsatisfying, unlike things like Warframe that are super quick and at least somewhat responsive. Then again, that could also be me being used to Warframe and expecting something closer to that. Either way, I didn't enjoy my time with Dark Sector. So while waiting for a major update in Digital Extreme's "new" game Warframe- I decided to go back and play the old game everything spawned from. Dark Sector's default controls are horrendous. Mechanics are clunky even after you rebind your keys. You might as well not even try to actually shoot anything- since there is no actual precision.
All that being said, Dark Sector is amazing. It is a shining example of how good classic old games used to be before the market started mass producing the copy/paste garbage they do now, feeding off of the same series until it's bled dry.
The story was... a bit lacking, but it was original and interesting nonetheless.
The music was PERFECT. Combined with the graphics used the atmosphere of the game actually left me with chills and fear of what was coming.
The enemies were hard, very hard. Part of it was artificial difficulty but the rest was genuinely fun mechanics and skill relating to control of your weapon(s), managing your ammo, and keeping very aware of your surroundings and positioning- of both you and your enemies. The way the market and upgrades worked really made me think about how to spend my money and collected gear. The BOSS fights lasted quite some time and I actually had issues figuring a couple out, one of which I still can't figure out if it was a matter of just repeatedly hitting the boss to progress...
If you would like a good nostalgia trip back to the time of fun old games, Dark Sector would be a great choice. It's decent length, and fun throughout. Constant changes in enemies, environment, and mechanics make what should feel repetitive not- keeping things fresh and fun. Speaking of mechanics, the very simple aftertouch ability is something that really sets Dark Sector apart. I could be wrong, but I'm pretty sure no game did it before, and even now I have yet to see it in another game.
Final Rating: 8.5/10

A quick note:  If you're a fan of Warframe, Dark Sector is definitely a game you want to check out.  I actually had the game on Xbox 360 a long time ago, and I didnt get past the first two chapters;  imagine my surprise when I found out the game is actually a prequel to Warframe! All this time, I had no clue.  I thought Dark Sector was just a third party title inspired by Resident Evil and Gears of War, with a protagonist who I've always thought resembles a young Donny Osmond.
As far as gameplay mechanics go, this game is unique and fun.  The protagonist's main weapon, the Glaive, is really cool to use and is satisfying to kill enemies with.  However, the game is also painfully hard at parts where it doesn't have to be.  Some parts are easy and you feel like a Glaive weilding Super Soldier (Warframe roots in play).  At others, it feels like you've been dropped into Dark Souls. Don't get me wrong, I love Dark Souls.  It's just a very drastic change of pace that happens quite frequently.
The story, felt a little weak.  There were a lot of unexplained things, and I feel like had there been more explanation the story could have been great.  For example, the protagonist comes across a character he seems to have had extensive history with.  Players, being new to the game's story, have no idea who this person and want to understand more.  We're not told anything about their past.  Ever.  This is very unsatisfying in the long run, because it just feels like wasted space for character connection.
Even details about the main character himself, Hayden Tenno, are missing - we're shown where he is throughout the gameplay but we're not really sure how or why he's there.  The story does explain some of it, but not enough to really make sense.
The game has a "Black Market" where you can buy weapons and apply upgrades you collect throughout the world.  However, the system seems almost pointless.  It takes forever to get enough money to buy a weapon.  And, if you get a weapon and decide "meh, I don't like this", chances are you won't have enough to buy a different gun if you sell it back.  I made this mistake, and went through half the game with a gun I didn't want.
Pro tip (not a spoiler, really):  Although the Black Market "VX Carbine" looks like a normal semi-automatic rifle as depicted in its picture, it actually functions like a bolt action sniper rifle and has a scope you can't remove.  Why the devs did this, I don't know.  And yes, that was the gun I got stuck with, which wasn't bad because I like snipers, but was annoying because I thought I was buying a semi-auto mid-range rifle.
One final comment I have is about what I'd call the game's "Puzzles".  The game tends to go from fast paced combat to slow paced "figure out how to progress" parts.  Some of these puzzle areas feel less like actual puzzles and more like "figure out what the devs actually intended for you to do", which was frustrating.  Some took one minute, while some took 20-30 minutes for me to un-stick myself from.  This would be ok if I was playing, say, Portal, but it feels very out of place in this game.  I think the devs were just trying to be creative with how the player could use the Glaive to interact with their environment, which is always cool, but it wasn't executed well.
Pros:
-Prequel to Warframe, shows how it all started
-Fun Gameplay; The Glaive is a very unique weapon.  A fun side note:  The Devs are adding more of it's features into Warframe (I can't wait for that).
-Donny Osmond
Cons:
-Story ≠ Clear
-Game has one difficulty, yet seems to switch between Easy and Hard very frequently.
-Poorly implemented features such as gun shop and environmental puzzles.
Overall game ratings based on your enthusiasm towards Warframe:
None: 5/10
Kinda: 7/10
Warframe Addict: 8.5/10
Play on, Tenno.

Let’s get this out of the way. Deus Ex: The Fall isn’t a very good game. There are four games in the Deus Ex franchise (Deus Ex, Deus Ex: Invisible War, Deus Ex: Human Revolution, and Deus Ex: The Fall), and while I wouldn’t say it’s as bad as invisible war, it’s definitely worse than Human Revolution. Multiple factors work against the game, let me cover a few. Since it was originally a mobile title, the devs were constrained to working with inferior hardware. The levels are much smaller than Deus Ex: Human Revolution, often requiring two or three loading points to get to a certain mission. The textures and graphics are a downgrade from its predecessor as well; you can see the constraints that were put on the game with worse hardware. You can clearly tell the interface was designed for a tablet, with mechanics as simple as a jumping being removed, the inability to change key bindings, or the remnants of in app purchases. To make matters worse, the port of the game is very poor. All sorts of issues arise if you don’t turn on vsync. The sound cuts out if you are using surround sound. Performance in general just isn’t that great.
However, there are some redeeming qualities about this game; you just have to look for them. For the most part they are able to preserve what made Human Revolution so good. The combat, stealth, and hacking mechanics are all for the most part there. The environments and atmosphere are reminiscent of Human Revolution. Furthermore we get to see more of the Deus Ex universe, with the game being a sequel to the book Deus Ex: Icarus Effect.
So should you buy this game? Maybe. Despite its many flaws, I still had fun with it.  Whether you should buy this game really depend on what you thought of Human Revolution. If you really enjoyed it, I would try The Fall. It's not a terrible game, it's just below expectations.
