Alright, first review ever. I'm going to talk about my first experience playing this, and then my experience a few years later. As a side note, I fall into the socializer/explorer categories of player types as defined by Richard Bartle.
Player base: When I first started playing this game, it wasn't all that old. I don't remember when I played it the first time exactly. There were tons of people EVERYWHERE! The main hub for where everyone starts, was a bustling, populated city. I could ask anyone for anything. I could get help doing just about anything in that area because there were so many people! Yet, when I came back 3 years later, I feel like I stepped into a ghost town. Long gone are the crowds of people that once inhabited the main city and the surrounding areas. There's people who just stand in one place and broadcast advertisements to join their guild, but there's just not the number of players that there once was. I've roamed around in zones where there were hundreds if not thousands of people at one point, and I only ever ran into 3 people while I was on for a few hours. I have been able to get help from the players to do a few things here and there, but it's mostly high level people who want to go grind dungeons. I don't know if the game will ever get back to that point of populous it once had.
Character creation: When I first played, there was a variety of classes to choose from at the beginning. My only gripe here was there wasn't really any explanation of how the classes worked/played. I was just presented with a choice, and I had little to no idea how any of them played. I tried to research how they played or how they functioned, and to my surprise there were guides explaining how it all worked. BUT, only if you can speak French. I can't speak French...so...yeah...that was a little upsetting. Now things are slightly better, I have been able to find a few videos on YouTube that were in English, which was nice, but not nearly as in depth as I hoped they would be. The forums on the community aren't all that helpful either. On the plus side, there have been more character classes added to the game, providing more ways to play the game to the user base.
Combat mechanics: This entire game is in an isometric view. This adds a cool aesthetic to the game, which is cool and all, but that makes it difficult to navigate sometimes. Luckily in combat, the game is a bit more helpful. Any sort of attack, whether physical or a spell will show the area where it can be cast. The combat is a turn based strategy, which reminds me quite a lot of Fire Emblem or Final Fantasy Tactics. Physical attacks aren't as easy to do as spells, and so you end up being a mage due to pigeonholing mechanics. You can usually only get one, maybe two attacks, where you can get 4-5 with spells. It's just not as effective. Maybe it's different in higher levels, but starting out, it's super difficult to be a brawler instead of a mage (at least with the classes that I played).
Economy: The economy is completely player controlled. This is kinda awesome from a player perspective. Players can print their own money. Yeah, print their own money. Strapped for cash? Go get the ore and mint some Kamas (K). Want to sell something really good for a rediculous price? Go to the market board and sell it! Like, it's a super fascinating way to run things! I'd love to see someone do an economic study to see how this really works. Half the time though, you're either mining or selling stuff, because grinding gets you gear and only a few K for each battle. So I think that this helps deal with problems that hyperinflation has on other games. You're only as rich as you want to be. There's a few problems with the market boards though. Granted, I can sell what every I want at whatever price I want, but one big issue is that they're unique to their areas. Stuff on sale in the main hub cannot be bought on another island (well, it could still be on sale, but there may be a price difference at least between 10-10,000 K, like no joke, it could be more). Also, things are on sale for only 3 days at max. So, if you find something you want, you got to get it fairly quick or it disappears or is bought by another player.
Environment: The environment is also completely player controlled. To my knowledge, the only thing that happens natuarlly to my knowledge is that ore respawns, and animals multiply if there's a lot of one kind in an area. I've seen plants mature, but I never saw them spread. This made for an interesting environment starting out. There were fields upon fields of wheat, tons of thistles and trees in the main hub (which are great crafting materials for beginning players). When I logged back in a few years later, boy what a stark contrast. The wheat fields were now full of turnips (which you can't harvest until level 15). There was still some wheat and some thistles, but not nearly in the amounts that were originally there. The trees stayed fairly constant, but the animals, my goodness. It seems the animals have replaced what used to be the players. There are so many of them everywhere. There's even areas dedicated to certain types of them now. It's crazy. However, in the time I was gone, I think there were people who overharvested the plants and overhunted the animals (as these are what you end up fighting 90-95% of the time if you want to level up). They implemented two new mechanics that were ment to help with the environment of the areas. First is a little minigame where if you win you get 40 of the resource you were harvesting. Second, there's NPC leaders of an area who give little blurbs of what an area is lacking or has an abundance of. So these help a little bit, but it's still hard for newbies to get their hands on some of the basic starting items for crafting.
Crafting: Boy, this is a can of worms. I think that this was another interesting design choice. First off, when you kill an animal, you may get a handful of K, but most of the time you got crafting items. I can see where this helps to keep hyperinflation down. However, crafting itself I have a few issues with. First of which, anyone can craft everything. No joke, I could literally make everything there was in the crafting books if I invested the time to do so. This leads to the pizza topping problem. If I can get a pizza with as many toppings as I want, I'm going to get set on the same few I like, and never try something new. If I was forced to choose a set of crafting skills, then that would have helped with this. It would have made me more focused and specialized instead of defaulting to the guy who mints money. There are so many crafting skills that I never looked at or explored because of mechanics too. Second, it was hard to have to remember how much you needed and what level you needed to be in order to make something. I was constantly opening my crafting book just to find the recipe and check my inventory. I feel there could have been a better way to do that instead of having to check the book every 5 minutes. Third, getting to the right level so you could collect something was frustrating too. Like do I really need to be a level 35 lumberjack to cut down an apple tree? Getting to the right skill levels takes forever. Plus, you have to continue to find higher levels of things to harvest, because lower level stuff has diminishing returns the higher your level (see also y=1/x). You could always try finding the items you needed at the market, but as we discussed before, that's hit and miss depending on the area you were in.
Storyline/Quests: Not much here after level 15 or 20. The overarching quest is you're the chosen one who's going to defeat the big awful bad guy. After 15/20, there's maybe a few quests sprinkled in, but not really all that much of a storyline to it all. It's a bit of a hodge podge of stories mixed into one experience.
There's not enough lines for this review...sigh...I will make a follow up post.

This game is not very intuitive, or straight forward, as soon as you are at the first "puzzle" there is no objective displayed on what you are supposed to do. There is one door that you have to go through in the first level, but an indicator saying the door is locked, or "Press E" to open the door is not displayed, so I had a hard time figuring out what the hell I was supposed to be doing.
Furthermore, this continues throughout the game, there is never an objective displayed to you. As I continued playing I was always lost, constantly felling like I had no purpose in the game, and always having to reference guides on the internet, or walkthroughs to figure out where I am supposed to go. Its like the company was writing a story but is never going to telling the audience what the story is about. In addition to that, you constantly have to sneak around. Your character is so weak at the beginning of the game, if you try to fight any of the monsters you'll die near instantly, without any tool of defense. You are given a gun, with one clip of ammunition, which is 6 bullets, and is not nearly enough to kill a monster, even with every shot being a head shot. Like wise, you'll be lucky to find anymore ammunition and you'll be left with running for dear life. Not only to mention, that you can sprint for half the distance of a Call of Duty player (yea, I'm referencing call of duty, sue me) before your character is out of breath.
Moving along, the default graphics setting is locked 30fps. Excuse me, this is PC, not console. I have two GTX 780's in SLI, I better be cranking settings as high as they can go, and running well beyond 60fps. So I changed it, and the only other option is locked 60fps is V-Sync, you cannot turn V-Sync off, hooray for input lag. Also, mouse acceleration is forced, with no option to turn off. You cannot play at a resolution higher than 1920x1080p, also, letterbox is basically forced, when I tried to turn it off, my FPS tanked to 5 from 60. Like wise, the overall graphics are not very good. Better than most games, but Tomb Raider looks better than this, and Tomb Raider came out before this game. There are blotchy textures everywhere, rocks, ground, blood, etc. With vehicles looking like they are from Grand Theft Auto 3.
Also you cannot rebind keys, anytime you try to, it changes another (completely at random) key. For example, I tried changing my sneak from CTRL to C and when I did, it changed my forward movement from W to CLTR, C... This game does not feel finished, or optimized for PC at all.. This not something I would have expected from an "experienced" game studio, and Bathesda obviously did not play the game or even look at it, and as them being a publisher for this, I definitely would not have expected seeing all these over sites from them.
In conclusion, I would easily rate this game a 2/10, this game feels like it is still in alpha. The game is playable, and has not crashed on me, so the only real points I can give to this game are it's stability.

This game is surprisingly good. If you are a fan of Resident Evil 4 or 5, or a fan of Dead Space, then you will enjoy this game. Although it is a little rough around the edges, Dark Sector is a gem that is severely underrated.
Gameplay: The game plays like other third-person shooters. It is cover based, so you will spend most of the game with your back against a chest-high wall while bullets fly all over the place. The weapons are pretty standard fare; you have some pistols, submachine guns, and some assault rifles. As you progress, you can find upgrades hidden throughout the levels that will let you augment your weapons at the black market dealer, as well as purchase entirely new ones. The most unique feature of this game is the Glaive, which is more or less a frisbee made out of sharp blades. You gain access to it after the tutorial level, and throughout the game you will gain new abilities, such as guiding it in flight or having it conduct electricity or fire. Guiding the Glaive through the air and slicing into enemies is very, VERY rewarding. Boss fights often center around using the Glaive to exploit a weakness of your enemy. Also, the Glaive can be used to pick up enemy weapons and ammunition from a distance, which is rather nice. As far as exploration goes, the game is very linear, with some puzzle solving here and there.
Story: The story for this game is average, nothing out of the ordinary. You play as Hayden, a special agent who becomes infected with a virus that changes him into....well, you get the point, right? Your infection grants you superhuman abilities, and the Glaive as well. Aside from that, it's a decent storyline that gets the job done.
Graphics: This game looks rather nice, maybe a little dated now, though. The enemies look good, and the envirnments are rather appeasing as well.
Overall, this game is well worth the money. At only $10, it's a steal. If it goes on sale, then you should definitely think about purchasing it. However, you don't have to wait until it's on sale to buy it. If you want a game that is in the same field as games like Resident Evil, or Gears of War, then look no further. It also doesn't just copy and paste those games, but rather it goes in it's own direction.

-THIS IS A SPOILER FREE REVIEW-
First of all thanks to Bloober Team, I had amazing 2 hours so far! I really don't often feel the urge to write a review but this EA game just blew my mind.
Visuals:
First of all I am very impressed by the visuals (especially considering this is based on the unity engine which is not often referred to as being this good) and the overall quality of the game so far.
The ...often... disturbing images are crisp and clean and the effects implemented so far simply look and feel right and stunning. Unfortunately my GTX 770 is not able of calculating my native screen resolution of 3440x1440 above 30fps constantly (no prroblem if you're running on full HD though and have a comparable gfx card).
Sound:
Can you please do a bit WORSE in the final product? It's just ... too good?! Music is placed where music should be in this genre, it's subtle and more often absent than present. But in case you hear some ambient music tones you can breathe again because just for a few seconds you might overhear the super creepy background noises like creaking wood and a childs steps echoing through narrow corridors.
Why we love games like these!
Layers of Fear plays with the Lovecraftian kind of horror, the horror in your mind playing tricks with you. Scaring you even though you're not constantly pushed by visuals but rather sound and pure atmospheric immersion. Spiced up with the idea of (japanese silent hill'ish) shocking moments this game has what it needs to be on a par with P.T..
What I really like about Layers of Fear so far is that it is not gritty or disgusting as the The Evil Within or Outlast approach to scare the **** out of us players. It is the Stephen King like approach of telling a story in a very psychological almost Kafkaesque style. I guess the first Amnesia would be a good comparison if you really need one.
In any case I can highly recommend this game (so far) and will definitely play the rest of it but for today... no more redwine and its 11 pm here anyway. Good night and sweet dreams!
PS: English is not my native language in case you find grammatical inconsistencies feel free to keep them. :)

No go for PC. If you're intrested in the very basic MMO for your mobile (Android/IOS), however, and don't mind simplistic gameplay with generic "kill x lizards, gather y herbs", well... Don't hold yourself.
For a start, we have decent cartoon-styled visuals, and many funny NPC lines.
Funny in a way like "do you know about stupid annoying tutorials? well, forget it! I've killed the guy who was doing tutorial, so there will be none there, learn how to play by yourself!" What a joek, right?
Anyway, it's really easy to play, you have 5 buttons for not upgradable spells or skills (depending from one of the 3 classes you'll choose, mage, fighter or thief), you just click the buttons and wait for timeouts, then click them again. The maps are tiny, the actual gaming skills are not applied, the autofocus works very awkward, and expecially awkward are zones of effects. Like: you can't shoot the lizard with the fireball since "it's too far", but that lizard can kick you in melee from the same place at the same moment!
Oh, well, I've tried to like it. But it's too generic, too boring right from the start. Even Chuck Norris wouldn't saved this game, or at least made me play it again. And it's not about "early access", it's about tiny level design, and other puny things. Jeez, I've played '90s MMO's which were better organized  and were offering a better support, bigger scale and all.
My rating would be 5/10 - for good visuals and good codework, but also for a cheap and puny levels, and so many other annoing things I can't tolerate in the MMO, like stupid quests, mindless grind, and craven community.

Though Super Monday Night Combat was once a fantastic game (and still is, in terms of gameplay), it was mishandled by UberEntertainment to the point where the game has little to no playerbase and is no longer being updated by developers at all.
In it's prime, it was being updated every week with a rotation of free Pros to play as, new maps and characters were being added frequently, and lots of cool cosmetic options were being added over time for every character.  The game itself has fantastic visual design, wonderful voice acting, and animation that's second to none.  It's full of character, highly competitive, and blends the best parts of MOBA/ARTS style games with the gameplay of a 3rd person shooter.  Super Monday Night Combat was awesome, but those days are past and the only remaining players are all angry, bitter, anti-community folks that have nothing else left to play.

Interesting concept, but flawed game. It's not that is bad or anything. It's fun, but it could have been so much more than it is. The things that made this game "fail":
1-It tried to fit itself within the fads of it's time (AKA feel like a Gears of War knock-off) rather than try to have it's own thing.
2-The upgrade and weapon marketing system it's just there to make you look for bonus items and money, making the campaign a bit longer (hint: play the game only using the single handed guns, it plays waaay better)
3-Fighting the soldiers is more interesting than fighting the mutants, but in most of the time, you fight the mutants.
4-The campaing was too short (especially if you ignore the bonus hunting).
5-The story is a mess of events and characthers that you don't see most of it. Who is Yago, what's the beef with Nadia, what I did in the past that was so horrible and haunts me to this day? none of these are answered.
But, I still recommend it: tons o' fun, each single handed weapon (the pistol, the sub-machinegun, the revolver and the sawed-off shotgun) complety changes the way you aproach a level, and at many times, you'll feel like a boss when completing a mission. In short: this game coulda been awesome, but it's just... good.

The story is really meh, it's all over the place,  the writing isn't particulary good and the voice acting could be better. Basically you're this guy named Hayden who comes to this one place with a mission but before he manages to complete it, he gets infected and gains really awesome powers and you also have to stop this Mezner guy (who looks a lot like the main antagonist from Crash Bandicoot). Honestly this story looks like an excuse for you to be running around as a dude with really cool powers, but it doesn't really matter since YOU'RE A ♥♥♥♥ING DUDE RUNNING AROUND WITH REALLY COOL POWERS.
Which brings us to the elephant in the room when it comes to this game and that is the glaive. It's what defines this game as BADASS! As you progress, you get more and more powers involving your infection and some of them are for the glaive, you can throw the glaive around and control it in mid air to slice your enemies more precisely when it comes to the limbs and hear their screams of agony! You can also apply elements to it like fire, electricity and ice for some really satisfying results. While the special powers are cool, the guns themselves aren't particulary great, except for the shotgun and the revolver. Oh, and the boss fights are really good altought there are some that have attacks with insta-kills, which makes the fights a whole lot more intense but at times quite frustrating. Overall, I'd say this game is worth it.

An awful game that really just deserves to be forgotten. Despite playing as an elite military operative, you are completely unable to reliably hit targets at 10 feet with any weapon. This incredible inaccuracy makes Dark Sector one of the most annoyingly dull games I've ever played, a problem that is only compounded by the fact that the enemies become more bullet-spongier as the game progresses.
The story makes no sense and the promise of turning into a resident evil style bio-weapon Ninja is cut short by the fact that, rather than undergoing a full body mutation as the game makes you believe, the ninja shown in the trailers is just the protagonist in a weird ninja suit. Furthermore, this ninja suit doesn't actually do anything. You can't take more damage, you don't do more damage, you don't move faster, the invisibility skill is obtained on route to pick up the suit..
The only thing it really changes is that you're able to pick up miniguns dropped mech-suit enemies. Considering the reason you go to get the suit in the first place is to defeat another weird ninja suit guy and that fight doesn't involve a minigun the whole thing just feels ♥♥♥♥ing pointless and dumb; which more or less sums up the whole game.
You'd be better off playing Warframe, the spiritual successor to Dark Sector, and is actually half decent if incredibly grindy.

I've read quite a few negative reviews about this game, so let me try to make it sound a bit better. There are some things that aren't quite amazing about it, however. No game is perfect, but when you find your niche in AoS, it can be really fun.
I had first played Ace of Spades after watching a YouTuber do an indie test drive of the game. It was simple, unique, and loads of fun. I played for hours in the early stage of the game. Fast forward a year or so (I can't recall the exact time period), and I had begun my Steam adventures. It was pretty excited to find AoS on the front page, becuase I remembered how much fun it was before. I opened it up only to find a completely different game from what I had previously played. It was entertaining, but it wasn't something that was played very often by me.
The newer version of the game just wasn't enjoyable. The Marksman were too common which resulted in barely being able to do anything in the open. The Miner allowed you to dig across the map which almost no effort or risk. The Commando involved a rocket launcher, which if used correctly results in an instant death. I found it difficult to do much of anything on the Engineer class. There just wasn't the strategic aspect that I had come to love about the previous game. It can still be fun to play, especially on Zombie Mode, but I wouldn't recommend getting AoS purely for the new Deathmatch versions.
It wasn't until I discovered there was still a Classic Capture the Flag gamemode that I fell in love with the game. Classic CTF is a simple, yet complex gamemode that really made the game fun. It was one class (in custom matches there is an SMG and Shotgun) which keeps things fair. It was a challenge to divide your team for each task at hand. One would need enough players to defend, yet enough to try and get the opposing team's flag. It really comes down to skill; how well you can shoot, how well you can build, and how well you can plan attacks. I played for hours and even ended up joining a clan. That made it even better because I had a close group of people that I could work together with. It's a nice community when you find the right people.
All in all, it's a good game. I would reccomend it to anyone who wants a unique FPS game. It's just fun. There's no other way to put it. The newer version really isn't all that great, but Classic is simply amazing. Well worth the money.

Gra Ace of Spades, obwołana została Minecraftem FPS-ów, co z uwagi na wielki sukces produkcji studia Mojang, jest bardzo zachęcającą rekomendacją. Wszystkich zapaleńców, którym marzy się możliwość budowy własnych fortów oraz walki na śmierć i życie z przeciwną drużyną na własnych mapach – muszę z przykrością rozczarować. Gra jest po prostu średnią strzelanką, a jej jedyne podobieństwo do wspomnianego wcześniej Minecrafta, to świat zrobiony z sześcianów.

Jak zacząć?
Ace of Spades jest nietypową produkcją i szczerze powiedziawszy, nie mam pojęcia od której strony ją ugryźć, żeby rozpocząć recenzję. Z jednaj strony mamy świetny pomysł, bo któż z tych, co Minecraft przypadł do gustu, nie marzył o możliwości epickich starć z innymi graczami na zaprojektowanych przez siebie mapach? Z drugiej strony, mamy tutaj masę zmarnowanego potencjału, gdyż budowa nie jest nawet w połowie tak precyzyjna, jak być powinna, a i czasu na nią w ogóle nie mamy.
Nachodzi mnie uczucie, że sami twórcy nie do końca wiedzieli, od której strony mają się za swoją grę zabrać, gdyż w żadnym swoim aspekcie nie osiąga mistrzostwa, przez co świetny pomysł skończył jako zwyczajny przeciętniak.
Czym jednak tak naprawdę jest Ace of Spades i jak się w to gra? Weźmy więc dla porównania dowolną strzelankę online i już jesteśmy w domu – przynajmniej na początek. Wybieramy z listy serwer, bądź pozwalamy wrzucić się na losowy (co odradzam, gdyż zazwyczaj kończyłem na pustych serwerach), czekamy chwilę na załadowanie mapy. Te są z reguły sporych rozmiarów i pozwalają na swobodne przemieszczanie się po całym terenie w poszukiwaniu wroga lub innych celów, które różnią się w zależności od trybów rozgrywki. Tak jak każdy szanujący się dzisiaj FPS, tak i Ace of Spades daje nam możliwość wyboru klasy, a nawet umożliwia w bardzo ograniczony sposób wybór broni. Profesje są cztery – Commando, Miner, Marksman i Rocketeer. Każdy z nich ma swój zestaw oręża, tak więc Commando biega z bazooką lub minigunem. Miner dostaje w swoje ręce ładunki wybuchowe, shotguna i coś w rodzaju połączenia wiertła z bazooką, Marksman prowadzić powinien ostrzał z daleka za sprawą swojej snajperki. Rocketeer natomiast potrafi szybko przemieszczać się po mapie za sprawą jetpacka i sprowadzać na wrogów śmierć z wysoka swoim wiernym karabinkiem. To jednak nie wszystko, każda z klas ma do swojej dyspozycji łopatę, służącą nie tylko do walki wręcz, ale również do kopania (o czym więcej za chwilę), klocek do budowy oraz zestaw kilku przygotowanych struktur.
Struktury te różnią się w zależności od klasy, którą wybierzemy. Znajdziemy między nimi schody, bunkry, platformy, zasieki, itp. Bardzo łatwo jest je zniszczyć, tak jak i resztę terenu, jednakże, dobrze rozplanowane, potrafią dać drużynie nieznaczną chwilę przewagi.

Buduj i niszcz
Jedną z największych różnić, które sprawiają, że Ace of Spades ma szansę zaistnienia na rynku Battlefieldów i CoD-ów jest możliwość wpływania na otoczenie. Wszystko, na co padną nasze oczy, możemy zniszczyć czy zabudować. Podstawowym narzędziem destrukcji jest saperka – składana łopatka, która służy również do zabijania wrogów wręcz. Kopanie nią jest dosyć chaotyczne i trudno mówić tutaj o jakiejkolwiek precyzji, jednak do szybkiego przebicia się przez ścianę nadaje się idealnie. Jeśli jednak nasza żądza zniszczenia nie zostanie zaspokojona małą łopatką, klasa Minera powinna dać upust destrukcyjnym zapędom. Garść dynamitów i wspomniane wcześniej wiertło, potrafią w kilka sekund stworzyć tunel lub wyrwę w najgrubszej ścianie.
Niestety, nie ma tutaj podziału na materiały, z jakich świat jest zrobiony. Każdy klocek rozpada się równie szybko, niezależnie czy jest to ściana, piasek czy wrak metra. Budowanie z pojedynczych bloków natomiast jest przydatne jedynie w momencie zablokowania dziury w murze, gdyż budowa czegoś większego mija się zwyczajnie z celem. Z pomocą przychodzą tutaj predefiniowane struktury, które postawić możemy jednym kliknięciem, jednak bazy operacyjnej z ich pomocą nie postawimy.

Walcz i giń
Arsenał jest dosyć oklepany i jego niuanse opisałem już wcześniej. W tym rozdziale recenzji postaram się opisać najważniejszy aspekt FPS-ów, czyli jaką frajdę daje w tej grze strzelanie. Osobiście przyznam, że małą. Amunicja kończy się strasznie szybko, więc warowanie się nie ma najmniejszego sensu, gdyż udać musimy się w takim wypadku do paczki z amunicją, która wraz z apteczką spawni się w wybranym miejscu mapy. Większość czasu grałem jako Rocketeer, gdyż uzależniłem się od jetpacka i zwyczajnie uciążliwym stało się bieganie po mapie za sprawą własnych nóg. Do dyspozycji miałem więc karabin, który dużą celnością pochwalić się nie mógł, tak samo zresztą jak i zadawanymi obrażeniami, przez co musiałem wystrzelać nie raz dwa (celne!) magazynki, żeby wroga ubić.
To jedynie moje odczucia, jednak wydaje mi się, że walka, co jest kluczowym elementem gry, nie została do końca dopracowana. Strzelanie do wroga po prostu przyprawiło mi więcej frustracji niż radochy.

Kwadratem być
Oprawa graficzna jest dosyć szczególna i czy będzie się podobać, zależy wyłącznie od gustu. Wszystko zbudowane zostało z sześcianów, jednakże, w przeciwieństwie do Minecrafta, są one dużo mniejsze, przez co twórcy uzyskali znacznie większą szczegółowość modeli postaci czy broni. Sam świat natomiast, nie potrafi wprawić w zachwyt, tak jak wyżej wymieniona produkcja od Mojang, gdyż tekstury nałożone na kwadraty są jednolite, przez co wszystko wygląda szaroburo. Samo niebo niestety jest obrazem o niskiej rozdzielczości, co tylko potęguje uczucie brzydoty otaczającego świata. Sytuacje ratują niektóre mapy, ukazujące majestatyczne katedry czy wzgórza, udowadniając nam, że odrobina pracy mogłaby zmienić cały wystrój gry na dużo atrakcyjniejszy.
Do udźwiękowienia nie mam natomiast najmniejszych zastrzeżeń. Dźwięki broni są solidne, każdy strzał, każdy wybuch brzmi tak, jak brzmieć powinien. W tle przygrywa radosna muzyczka, swoim stylem nawiązująca do produkcji z automatów. Niekoniecznie musi się ona podobać, nie można jej jednak odmówić swoistego klimatu pasującego do całej gry.

Minecraft FPS-ów, czy przeciętny shooter?
Zdecydowanie, Ace of Spades nie powinno być tak ostentacyjnie porównywane do Minecrafta. Pomimo drobnych podobieństw, różnice są tak wielkie, że nie ma mowy o jakimkolwiek zestawianiu tych gier ze sobą. Recenzowana przeze mnie produkcja jest wykonana solidnie, jednak wiele jej aspektów powinno jeszcze zostać dopracowanych. Uważam, że wielu graczy z przyjemnością przywitałoby jakiś system rozwoju postaci, odblokowania nowych broni czy możliwości zaprojektowania własnych budynków. Gra ma jednak wiele silnych atutów, takich jak całkowicie modyfikowalna strefa walki, możliwość stawiania obiektów czy kilka zróżnicowanych trybów gry. Jeśli więc to, co napisałem, nie zniechęciło nikogo, a wręcz przeciwnie – ma ochotę na demolkę wszystkiego – jak najbardziej powinien się grą zainteresować.
Plusy
•	Możliwość niszczenia
•	Dobry pomysł
•	Zróżnicowane tryby gry
Minusy
•	Kiepskie budowanie
•	Zmarnowany potencjał

: if you're a Deus Ex fan, this game might be worth getting. If you're not, you simply will not have the patience for its crap. So with that out of the way, the rest of the review....
I snagged this game during an Amazon sale for significantly less than full price, and I have to say it's not nearly as bad as I expected.  Hardly stunning praise, but I'll freely admit to having some fun playing the game, in between dealing with its problems.  The biggest problem is of course the mangled interface, specifically the hard-coded keybindings and the mouse smoothing+acceleration combo that the game forces. Once I used AutoHotkey to fix the bindings though my biggest problem with the game went away. The mouse issues, while still present, aren't as bad because frankly the AI isn't tetchy enough for it to matter. They always give you ample room to aim at all their vulnerable bits.
I'm not saying it's a great game. It's certainly nowhere near as detailed and complex as any of the previous Deus Ex titles, not by a long shot, but given the price I paid I'm willing to forgive that. It's also surprisingly easy, undoubtedly due to the straight mobile-to-PC port.  Any experienced Deus Ex player is only going to have trouble with this game if they insist on going for a perfect no-detection non-lethal run, especially with built-in health regen and items you can literally buy mid-battle. Despite that though, the game is still
in the same way that DX:HR was fun, albeit not as well fleshed out and
shorter (you can breeze through the full campaign and all sidequests in a few hours). It's sort of like eating a frozen pizza: yeah, it's not as good as a restaurant-made pizza, but it's still a pizza, and if you like pizza sometimes that's enough.
Really though, what drags this game down are the control issues. The rest of the issues with the game - low rez models, simplified level design, almost ridiculously dumb AI - can be given a pass because the game was ported from a mobile platform. The controls though... that's kind of a basic, required component of games, plus, this game is a Unity engine game. Someone with three weeks of programming classes could make remappable controls in Unity. Not making remappable controls in Unity engine is beyond lazy, it's downright negligent. And to add further insult to injury, this awful hackjob of a port costs more than the original mobile version, despite having nothing new to it.  Completely inexcusable.
Bottom line: if you can get past the control issues (or use a workaround like AutoHotkey), there's a fun game lurking under here, along with some interesting depth and backstory.  Unfortunately there's
to get past within that, and that coupled with the somewhat dumbed down game may make it too much for you to be willing to deal with.  If it's not though, the game is worth your time, but not the full asking price.

This game is not as horrible as people make it out to be yet it's origins as a tablet game are obvious.
I was expecting this game to be as bad as Invisible Wars and it is not. However, it doesn't hold a candle to Human Revolution. Yes 98% of the NPCs, weapons, textures, objects, sound effects and items are ripped from Human Revolution. Unsurprisingly they are all lower quality and a lot less of them. This is due to the performance constraints of iPads and Android devices.
This means the levels feel empty, underpopulated and lack that living world feel that made the original Deus Ex and Human Revolution so great. This becomes apparent in Panama which just feels dead and empty especially in the last mission. You are told to expect a massive fight yet are greeted by less then a half dozen guards and a single bot. In fact in no place are you ever confronted by more then six or eight NPCs at a time be they hostile or friendly. I guess the tablets couldn’t handle any more.
Another thing that carried over from the tablets is the inventory system. There are no stores or NPCs selling non quest items like ammunition or energy bars. These items are also rare in game with guards only dropping a handful of bullets. This was done to force tablet players to spend money through micro-transactions. Fortunately in the PC version we only spend credits found in game on these items. I was doing a stealthy non lethal play though which meant I was going through energy cells and bars very quickly so I had to keep buying the bars. Expect to spend a lot of in game currency on these or ammo if you do a lethal play through.
The AI is not as good as Human Revolution and is extremely scripted. Yet it's not as horrible as people make it seem. The AI is not horrible but not good either. Like Human Revolution they walk on fixed patrol routes. Yet they vanish instant you kill or knock them out. This removes a key part of the strategy of Human revolution which was not only planning how to knock out an enemy but how to hide their body. Now you just have to sneak up on them which given how few enemies make up the world isn't that hard.
Should you get this game? I clicked yes but have one key caveat. I bought it for $2.99 USD on sale and after beating it in under 8 hours feel like I got my moneys worth. I don't believe that buying it for $9.99 USD I would have felt the same. I'd say wait until you can get it for around $2 to $4 USD. There is still a fair amount of that famous Deus Ex to be had story and some atmosphere too. I'd say that alone would make this game a good buy at a reduced price.

This is the closest thing to a House of Leaves game{1}. And that's a good thing. House of Leaves took horror in writing and put it into a phenomenal setup, but it left many people desiring grand and spooky visuals to accompany their fears{2}. Luckily, while this isn't a HoL game, it manages to fill that void while being its own entity. I know most people are going to compare this to P.T.; but I felt a HoL vibe more than anything throughout it all. The endless and increasingly dangerous corridors, the increasingly alien structure and a pure, unadultured HATRED that emanated from the surroundings that only sought to make you feel more unwelcome than anything else. The "protagonist" also manages to serve as an antagonist to his own self, but is also facing some other malevolent threats at the same time. Needless to say, this game makes use of familiar or "comforting" space such as a house and flips it on its head for a total mutilation of anything you might have once considered safe and sound{3}.
Graphically this game is, of course, gorgeous; the use of the Unity engine is absolutely fantastic, and while I did need to reduce my graphics quality to play without framerate drops, it still looked absolutely beautiful even at medium quality. Also, I absolutely loved the small detail of the character limping. That detail really grounded this game in a realistic setting and it made for the game to feel even more stressful knowing that I could not run from anything should that ever need to happen. I will say, though, that the punishment for "death" was a little too lenient; I did indeed waltz directly into the loving arms of my burnt and melting wife a few times, once without meaning to, another because I simply wanted to, and thirdly because I liked the colorful room she was in. Which is a bit silly, but also at the part with the rat swarm, I really could not tell if there was something I needed to do to escape, or if I just let them consume my flesh.
All in all, this is a game worth buying in early access. Even the cliffhanger ending is worth reaching just for the spectacle of it, and I cannot wait for the rest of the game to be completed. There are, after all, still two more forbidden paint tools to be uncovered...
{1} House of Leaves is a Horror (or Romance) novel by Mark Z. Danielewski about a supposedly nonexistent film documenting a house that tries to trap and destroy its inhabitants
{2} At least, I certainly wanted more from it all
{3} You weren't safe to begin with, Where a shadow exists, horror awaits. That dark hallway in your house will always be able to be dark. Do not walk in the dark. Do not explore the dark. Do not listen to the dark. Do not speak to the dark. Do not touch the dark. Do not let the dark touch you.

The Deus Ex series is one of my favorites of all time, and this is a letdown in every possible way. I must have purchased it without realizing it was a mobile port, because the first thing that struck me were the terrible graphics. Unfortunately, everthing else about it was just as terrible. Flat voice acting, horrendous AI, non-customizable controls, obvious touchscreen interface and microtransaction leftovers, etc. The game is also very short, limited to a few small areas, and ends with "To be continued..."
It takes more than one close-range headshot to kill an unarmored enemy, I sometimes have to click a button in a menu five times before it responds, hand-to-hand takedowns are shown in a "cutscene" format the breaks the game flow, enemies are "unloaded" when you step past certain borders, causing them to pop in and out of existence when I enter and exit rooms to hide.
I'd write more, but there's really no point. Just look at the Metacritic rating (currently a 46), all the other recommendations and pass over this game. It's an embarrassing low point in the series and it's better off ignored.

A cute lil no brainer to relax with. A great game to introduce a kid to the turn based strategy genre. My  7 year old son loves it. This game is a great way to spend some quality time with your child and get some chuckles while doing it. The multi-player system IS dated, you send data packets back and forth to each other via a lobby chat room type thing ... you take a turn, upload your turn to the server, the opponent Downloads your turn, takes his own turn and uploads it back and this continues until the game is over ..... it doesnt take long to take the turns and it isnt that bad once you get used to it. This harkens back to the early days of Multi-player over the internet and a game called "Empire" on the Amiga 500 where you did this exact thing ... take a turn ... upload it (or save it to a floppy disk back then) or e-mail the turn to a friend ..... not sure why they did it this way other than lazy programming or a lack of knowledge on the Devs part as to modern day programming techniques but it is what it is. I still think it is a great way to introduce kids to the TBS genre and my son and I love it.

The game has potential, but ultimately. It's just a shame to be reminded of the direction AE has taken since AQW. First thing I thought was for the hope that they would not go the AQW approach of emphasizing Rare items (limited for a certain amount of time before removed forever), yet as soon as I enter the Class Shop, and looked on the wiki at what was removed...there's no excuse.
The next thing is the upgrade system. While a nice throwback to the one-time upgrade to Guardian to the original AQ than the AQW approach of a sub. fee for upgrade, unfortunately just like AQ's Z-Tokens, Dragon Coins are the real deal that matter, but it's repulsive how excessive this is to even freakin' potions costing Dragon Coins. I mean, seriously?! And that is where I must highlight one great, glaring, disgusting design choice.
The mobile game practice of Timers. It's not enough to go back and forth for monotonous grinding to craft gear, but there is also a time for said gear to be crafted, of course you can always use Dragon Coins to speed up the craft! Alternatively than wait, buy now..for a chunk of Dragon Coins. Yeah - Farm, then pay with the currency that requires cash, or play a waiting game.....Yeah, I expect this garbage from certain mobile games, not a PC MMORPG. Disgusting.
How bad can this get? There is an NPC, for those who are not as familiar with the game's characters and such, named Cysero. He has a crafting shop and one of them is "Adventure Weapons". Now, not only do you have to farm the random series of "random adventures" for Battle Gems and Battle Gem Shards which are completely random loot, but on top of that, there are items in there, and solely for cosmetic purposes mind you, for 18 Hours to 1 Day to craft. This is how badly they bait cash for Dragon Coins.
That's all this game boils down to - Farm, Craft, Wait or Cash.
It really is a shame, as a long-time fan of AE, to see their motives more driven by what can gain them more money faster, rather than being mindful of what is balanced, and what not to do. The game would have so much more potential, if AE had more heart like in the good old days.

The Evil within is a good game with a good story. However I cannot recommend it . This game is brutally difficult. Don’t get me wrong I’m all for a challenge, but when I sit down to play a game I want something that’s fun and fulfilling, not an experience that leaves me ripping my hair out and wanting to quit. Being forced to run from invincible enemies through an entire level is not a fun gameplay mechanic and if it weren’t for the obnoxious number of times which I’m forced to do so, I might actually enjoy the game. In fact when I’m not fleeing from my undefeatable enemy I am enjoying myself.  Searching through the creepy and very well done level design for ammo, collectables and keys for upgrades is a very fun experience. But it all goes down the tube when u face off against an enemy which you simply cannot defeat. It leaves you feeling like all the upgrades and perks where for nothing because now you’re forced to run away regardless of how much experience you dumped into your health bar.
I understand that the invincible enemy is supposed to be scary, u cant kill it so u have to think your way around them instead of going in bullets blazing. However the game simply dose it far too often. It becomes tedious, frustrating and boring.  Once again, I cannot recommend this game.

After finishing the game, I must say I recommend it, but only to the people who are into the genre. If you loved the good early Silent Hill games, you will probably like this. I do not like the dumbed down, Americanized Resident Evil, but these psychological horrors with a twist always intrigue me. Unlike many people, I had zero technical problems with the game.
The gameplay is mostly okay, the standard survival horror blend of careful aiming and resource conservation, figuring out the bosses, sneaking, etc. I don't like boss fitghts, so the end was somewhat less good for me.
Atmosphere - it's where the game really shines. The levels are incredibly moody, and capture the subtle effect of how depression or anxiety alters your perception of your surroundings. The whole "going insane" aspect is very well done, and is the highlight of the game. There are lots of subtle touches like paintings with hidden references, carefully placed props, well designed levels and so on.
The story is average overall, and there is no catharsis nor liberating conclusion.
Overall, 8/10 from me, mostly for the unrealized potential in the story.

It is as everyone says it is, very much a Left 4 Dead clone with Rats.
(And therefore different types of rats;
Gas Rat which throws poison bombs, similar to the Spitter.
A rat with grabs you and drags you away, similar to the Jocky.
A rat which is huge and it's punches throw you around, similar to the Tank.
A rat which sits on roofs and drags you away with a rope, similar to the Smoker.
Although one different, there is also a Gatling Gun-wielding rat. Slightly different. Kinda cool)
Pros:
+Large levels
+A number of different gear pieces (Melee Weapons, Ranged Weapons, Trinkets)
+5 different classes with their own Melee and Ranged Weapon types (And yes, each class can get an expansive number of different melee and gear pieces suited to each class as well)
+Excellent atmostphere. (Dark Fantasy fits it's descriptiop nicely).
+
Cons:
-The weapons offer no immersion/satisfying experience. Guns have little to no recoil, no powerful sound behind each shot. Melee weapons don't have "Weight" so to speak. All weapons feel generic in the sense they all play the same, just with different damage, attack speed, range/effective arc and looks.
Now before you say, "WELL WHAT ELSE COULD YOU CHANGE?! THAT'S HOW IT IS WITH LIKE EVERY GAME EVER!!!!111!"
What I personally would like to see is weapons from something like the Souls series, or the Warriors-esque games. Where each weapon offers a definable and unique experience. If a two handed hammer that takes up to 3 seconds to pull of a charged swing actually caused damage to a larger Tank rat. That for instance would be very different to a pair of very small daggers which would tear apart smaller rats in seconds, but not do much to the Tank rat. Weapons should be more devestating in my honest opinion.
Ranged weapons are the same. The difference between a handheld cannon and a pair of pistols is very little except range/effective arc, damage, reload speed and so on. But again. The weapons don't really seem to do anything except cut through rats like paper as you waltz through levels almost completely unscathed.
I'm not really sure how I can explain it in a short amount of words. But basically. The weapons feel generic. And for me is literally the only thing I can find to dislike about the game. Which is why this sole point has taken up more words than the first part of my review......No actually, thinking about it there is one more thing I dislike.
-Difficulty.
It is arbitrary and meaningless. As is the difficulty with far too many other games. Enemies aren't smarter, enemies don't do better in any situation. They just do more damage, special enemies appear more often and they have more health. That is literally it.
Personally it doesn't make the game more fun or challenging. It just adds to the grind and forces you to take things slower. Ultimately creating a significant grind factor that not even I could find in Left 4 Dead.
OVERALL:
The game is fun, play it on your on or with Random teammates (Although I only found one online Teammate unfortunately, who left after two missions) or very likely best, with friends.
There is a touch of RNG to the loot. Of which the chances to actually find something worthwhile or good from a chest, I found was not very good. I opened many chests, 70% were empty.
A nice amount of content in the form of levels and gear
It's very generic in the weapon-play.
The atmosphere, the dialogue, the sound design are quite good. If it weren't for the mediocre generic weapon play I would actually say this is better than Left 4 Dead in every way, but Left 4 Dead has it one upped in terms of weapon design.
Overall, Solo. It isn't worth much, but it has some good points to admire about it and the atmosphere is definitely it's strongest point in my opinion.
But Co-Op. It is more enjoyable. Noticeably so.
On a final note. I was immensely pleased with the performance. Having avoided it at launch because of bad/mediocre performance reviews. I was surprised to say at 1440p absolute MAXIMUM settings. It ran like a dream between 60-70FPS never at any singular point going below 60. That's on a GTX 980 at stock clock speeds, 6600k OC'd @ 4.2Ghz and 16GB DDR4 RAM.

The permanent death is the thing that really ruins this game.
It talks about unlimited replay value and random generation, but the random generation makes almost zero impact. It's not like this is a dungeon crawling game or a real Rogue-like where the maps and layouts actually matter and impact the game. You just walk through dark hallways and rooms looking for the objective, the random layout makes almost no difference because there's almost nothing happening in the layout to justify random generation. The point is, having to replay this game over and over and over doing the exact same thing of wandering through dark hallways over and over and over looking for the objectives; isn't justified with random generation. The difference between this hallway and this hallway, this room and this room, this map and this map is completely negligible. In the end all you're doing is just looking for the objectives, the random generation is worthless yet the developer added in permadeath thinking the pointless random generation would make replaying the game over and over tolerable. It does not, at all, because the gameplay is not exciting enough to warrent forcing players to replay everything just because they died once.
The hazards and scares of the game itself are of mixed quality. Some scares are just copypaste spawn in a little girl character model or a burst of steam out of nowhere to artificially scare the player. While other scares are actually well done and genuinely frightening to experience. So, it's fifty fifty whether the game will generate the uncreative generic pseudo scare or the cool and well designed one. Although the game seems to favour the former. The hazards are also the same, some of the hazards are interesting traps which add onto the gameplay by having a unique obstacle players have to traverse besides avoiding the enemies. But most of the hazards are stupid looking skeletons which stand around the room and instant kill the player if they spark a light anywhere near them, stupid looking skeletons which hurt you if you get too close yet they don't consistently react to you being close and they are often put into small rooms or corners where sometimes you can't even avoid them, and traps which require inconsistent methods to traverse or just straight up hit the player instantly out of no where. The games constant use of clean skeletons and bones as props and scene assets being the lowest point of the visual quality, as clean skeletons and bones look like holiday decorations in almost any environment.
Players will encounter the traps and scares over and over as they play through the game, and encounter them even more everytime they die. Once again, the game working against itself by forcing players to re-experience the same sometimes good sometimes stupid scares and the same sometimes annoying something cool traps over and over because of the permanent death.
The game also likes spawning extremely long, boring and tedious hallways as well as constantly re-uses assets in the map. Endlessly replay value.
This is a good horror game, but it's not a good enough game to warrent hours of replay. There is not enough content diversity, and there is not enough interesting gameplay. Yet players will be forced to replay the game over and over because everytime the player dies there is a fifty fifty percent chance it wipes their save completely. Literally, when you die, you choose between two doors and one door wipes your save the other lets you retry.
Over time you will become overly familiar with every scare, every hazard, all the while wandering through the same dark halls which are totally randomized and totally meaningless because they're all just generic dark halls. To the point where it essentially becomes grinding.
It's even better when you die spontaneously in the middle of a hallway with no enemies, that is what ended my first run of the game and I assume there's some enemy that can no-clip through walls; in a game which can spawn extremely long and winding narrow hallways filled with traps players have to stop to confront. Yeah great combination, very fair. It's also possible for traps to briefly block doorways, which will get players killed if they are being chased and thus cannot move forward to escape. And be sure to not miss the elevator power switch which may or may not spawn hidden completely behind a pillar you can walk past without ever checking behind it yet you can't actually progress without finding that potentially hidden power switch. The game also has a stamina system yet there is nothing which can be used to keep track of how much stamina is left, so players have to manage stamina blindly which can also get them killed in a chase.
It's a good horror game but expect to be forced to replay it to the point where it becomes stale and tedious. Expect to have to replay the same low difficulty floors everytime you die on a high difficulty floor, just so you can reach the high difficulty floors again. Every single time.
Although the quality of the game steeply drops after the third dungeon. After the third dungeon, the next three dungeons are burning apartments instead of stone undergrounds. Not only is the apartment atmosphere empty and completely unintimidating, but so is the spooky scary black skeleton who gets added into the enemy pool and the game spamming the same audio jumpscare specifically on these floors. There is also a time limit, although dying to the time limit does not reset the game; just that floor. However, it is possible to fail just because it takes so long to go through the tedious hallways and search everywhere that if random chance isn't on your side you just won't find your way out in time.
During these floors, there are optional film reels which players can find to serve as "clues". You can view the film reels in the hub. The first one, is a several minute video of various blurry black and white scenery images followed by a minute of footage of a burning farm. Riveting. The next floor, I purposely did not look for the film since there's a time limit and the last film I saw was boring and pointless so why bother. The game lamented the fact that I missed the second film; three times with in-game pop ups.
Developer, if you are going to make optional lore items; don't put them in areas where there is a time limit, and don't make them boring and pointless film reels of scenery. And don't harrass the player if they miss them, maybe the player didn't get it because they were too busy trying to escape the tedious unscary dungeon within the arbitrary time limit.

This game changed me. In what little I have played so far, it has already affected me on a deeper level.
First off, it made me realize my mortality as a human. Everyone is fragile in this world, and just because you play the "hero" doesn't make you special. If anything it taught me doing these things are straight up suicides if you don't get your timing right, but even if you do there are inconsistancies, like who is going to investigate, where will everyone be, will the melee or gunner people check first, and who has the faster reaction time?
It also made me understand that going in with seething rage won't help either. Yes, a game where the goal is to kill everyone, going in all rambo-like does not get you the girl. It gets you the grit of your teeth splattered all over the floor. Thinking things out before doing them is the way you have to take it unless you are very lucky and have your timing down.
And lastly, the pleasure of finishing a level doesn't come without it's costs. Once the final victim gargles his last breath of air and blood the mood changes with the music as you grab what you came to get, and slowly walk through the blood and guts of those you killed to get there. The sound of the strings echoing through your headset or speakers as that little voice in your head whisperes "Look at this. This is what you did. Do you understand?" just makes you stop and take in the scenerey for just a moment. Well... do you?
There's something very special about this game. It could just be how much it reminds me of playing free flash games on the school computers back when I was a teen. It's brutal and fun, and rewarding while being punishing and shameful. Some delicate balance was acheived when this game was made. I strongly reccomend it, even from only 2 hours of gameplay.
Really, the only thing I don't understand is the story-line so far, but I have a feeling it'll click the more I play. I got the general idea of what might be going on, but it's still as fuzzy as that pause screen (Which my god, the pause screen in this game takes me WAY BACK to my childhood. Like, damn.)
Interesting experience, definitely worth the low price. But I doubt the writers have ever heard of something called "sublety"

First things first, I did not want to drown your reputation in mud with this review back then. But then I'm been playing for quite some time and things never changed. Well, time to post a review I guess. For those that don't know, I'm one of the earliest player in this game, a "Founder" if you may (no I did not buy the guardian package thingy).
Like ever other game there are a few pros and a few cons in this game. Let's start with the uh, "more positive" stuff shall we?
PROS:
-Amazing art. Knowing AE, their 2D art has always been excellent. But I did not expect this. The character modelling and the terrain models are cool, and the animation style is not too bad.
-Cross-platform.
-Terrain that we can actually parkour with. Seriously there's no limit to where you can jump to. There were people who literally jumped up into the sky in Greenguard before the release and it's awesome (I'm sure it has been removed). Really, this feature allows you to explore more of the maps. Good job.
-Balanced classes. For those FREE classes, they are pretty balanced. There's no such thing as a particular class outshining the others. Each class has their own unique perks.
And now, the CONS:
-The goddamned microtransactions. At first I thought this game is a free to play, until I tried to solo taht particular dragon in the volcano, both of us having the same level. I retried several times with different classes to no avail. Just then, a guardian of the same level came in and solo killed the dragon. Wtf? Do we have to pay to have an advantage in farming/ soloing bosses? And those cool-looking costumes, especially the seasonal ones. You will NEVER get them unless you pay, or in a less kind word, whale. Ballyhoo for free gems please.
-The goddamned grind. From the first day I played to this day, the grinding hasn't changed much. You have to grind for hours and hours and hours (and hours x 100) to get enough materials to craft a piece of armor. If not crafting, then it's leveling. The miserly amount of exp given by monsters makes it hard for players to progress. And the quests, oh my god aren't they tedious. You have to kill the same monsters for about an hour to clear a single area.
-The goddamned crafting price. Who knew the cost to craft stuff would be 50x the amount you can grind in an hour? Seriously you need to make the monsters drop more gold, or more gold from quest rewards. I played AQW and man my gold hit the limit and refused to increase anymore but this. Man ain't this pricey. Not to mention that you had to wait an hour to a day for a piece of your gear to be crafted.
-Bland gameplay. Aside from the grindfest, we (free players) are only offered 3 classes, and those whales 4. I understand that this game is still in its early stages of development but come on. It's been more than a year since I played this game, Shouldn't there be a least 1 new class to be bought? (WITH GOLD PLEASE. GOLD.) Like, maybe the Ranger class from the Greenguard? Or the Necromancer from Doomwood? It'll certainly make the game much more interesting.
-(I had something else to say but I forgot what it was. Gonna come back for this one, sorry.)
So yeah, much to my regret to say this, I wouldn't recommend people spending hours just to get one or two levels up, and that's below the level 10 mark. God knows how long would it take when higher level capacities are introduced. The one thing that I'm still concerned about is the mircotransactions. Please at least give us free players a class like the Oracle from AQW to solo stuff with, even if it takes forever to kill stuff. You are AE, not EA. And I certainly do not wish to see your reputation going down the drain with them. After all, you made one of my most-played game when I was a kid.

The Evil Within is an atmospheric horror survival game by Shinji Mikami the creator of Resident Evil series.The game is a survival/horror that has some gore filled disturbing moments and a nostalgic feel of the old school horror genre.
Sebastian Costellanos who is on his way to investigate a mass murder at the hospital with his partners Julie and Kidman. Upon arrival is a man sitting on the floor spouting its impossible when suddenly a hooded figure attacks Sebastian,  and he finds himself  upside down to see a man carving humans up like pigs at a shop and thus begins the game story.
Literally the story is pretty insane, There will be moments where the mind is in a state of chaos. Is this game about a supernatural horror? some kind of new virus? Is it psychological? Wtf is going on? The main character himself will be confused but as time comes along, Putting, the text newspaper clues found throughout the game and story progression  together is when the the pieces start falling together, which turns out to be quite decent.
The game graphics are quite good and surprisingly atmospheric. The fogs, the lighting, and the way the aesthetic is laid out across every map, The blowing curtains and drapes, the littered corpses, and crumbling buildings are just some of the example of what makes this game immersive. Most of the maps in this game are arena sized areas with set  path with corridors and unlike other horror games you cannot repeatedly come back so make sure you search the area thoroughly before progressing.  Players can choose to divert their attention to search for keys or map pieces, There are times when the graphics get a bit muddy or don't make sense (Wine bottle tossed on the player makes it look like strawberry jam on him).
The voice acting in this game is decent though some are not as impressive they are, however, passable. The sounds heard from weapons, monsters and the aesthetic themselves are really nicely done and majority of the time, there isn't much music in the game except the ones that come from save points but that's the beauty of it. The silence is what makes it scary when players aren't sure what exactly is going to expect.
The game play of the game plays much like resident evil 4( of course its made by the guy who created the game). There is a stealth game play mechanic that allows players to kill the enemy quietly or with guns and  damage thier body parts  such as the head to take them down, stomping on them or and use matches to prevent them from back up. Matches can also prevent future corpses. There are also melee weapons in the game but they are one time use items such as the torch or axe. Though it is a shame that You cannot drag bodies into fire.
The game Ai is pretty stupid at times and act much like resident evil zombies if anything but can also be argued that its because they're undead. Overall they function well when they are working together to kill the player, and the bigger enemies will have no mercy. The boss fights in this game are hard and will require players to conserve ammo to fight against. Running is an option but there are times when that option is completely out of the question. The puzzles in this game is sub par at best and isn't something to make people think too hard on.
Sebastion is always armed with a lantern as a source of light, as for the weapons in the game included are pistols, shotguns, sniper rifle, grenades, Magnum, and of course the agony bow which uses a different variety of arrows such as poison, ice, explosive fire,   and can be used as traps. There is seven total It is the all in one crossbow weapons. Throughout the game players will encounter traps that can be disarmed by either holding space or timing a needle to hit a green mark to materials and create the agony bow ammunition. After completing the game players get a rocket launcher and machine gun.
In the beginning of the game when players are weak and have no ammo, there isn't many choices except to stealth,hide, distract enemies, or kill them in one shot using torches and axes. Melee is probabaly not a good choice because enemies will grab on to the player if given the chance and can deal  a hefty amount of damage. The  later stages of the game will have less if not any hiding at all.
The health stats, stamina,  weapons damage, crits, accuracy,  and even ammo amount is part of a stats system or rpg element  that players have to upgrade in order to improve their overall character performance. This gives the player options and variety in what they want to be their greatest strength and never will he be more overpowered than the enemy. Upgrading requires green gel to do so in certain amounts.
The camera rest behind the player shoulder that can zoom in on strange ways at times and can be a nuisance to some.
Smashable objects such as pot and boxes, hidden compartments are how players find ammo in the game, along with  secret keys to open locks in the safe haven ward to obtain extra goodies to aid.  There will be plenty of things lying around to find yet they are limited so using them wisely is the key to survival. There will be times when not being conservative will get you killed.
The controls are clunky at times and reminded me of an old school resident evil and took a bit of time to get used to Of course once one gets to use to it, everything will be a bit more smooth and fits in. The mouse acceleration during the screen needs to be patched, and hopefully we'll see one but aside from that the game interface is clean. Players can set weapons/items it to 4 keys at a time otherwise there will be a radial menu which can be pulled up and slows down time in the game  for swap outs.
The map spans 15 chapters and takes about close to an hour each to complete, sometimes more if one chooses to look and explore everything.  Game time can range between 13-15 hours to complete the game
There is no multiplayer players are able to replay the game in this hardest difficulties Nightmare and Akumu whereas akumu is one shot death mode.
My Opinion? Check the video below, typed out way too long and over the limit for steam I had  fun with the game, and I know there will be a handful of people who will enjoy this game also from their own perspective. All negatives aside this was a decently made game that was immersive, atmospheric, gore filled horror and if anything more horror action survival than a run aroundhide type of horror game. One scariness is different from another and the constant change of gameplay every chapter keeps the game from being stale.

Game is great, a shame about the technical flaws. Thank Bethesda for that one. If you're a fan of Resident Evil (4 especially), then you'll love The Evil Within. In many ways, it feels like the lost Resident Evil 4 (fog, hook, etc) with more strict ammo.
I'd highly recommend downloading Flawless Widescreen, since there's a few tweaks like FOV (the default is disgustingly close) and 21:9 support.
I bought the game at $60 and loved it, it seems to go ~$20 average in sales now. Seems like a good time to jump in.

If you loved RE4 you should really enjoy this game.
What I loved:  It's a lengthy adventure in psycho terror.  The intensity and atmosphere is exactly what I look for in a survival horror game.  Using your sparse ammo appropriately is always a thrill (i.e. taking out 6 zombies with one match instead of using tons of bullets).  You are generally on edge the whole game and some encounters (especially in harder difficulty) are downright terrifying.
I've read some people complain about the story, but I really enjoyed it.  There are also accusations that it isn't real survival horror.  I personally disagree with this.  Try a no-upgrade or Akumu run (or if you are totally insane, both).  I'm not sure what more you could ask for.
What was so-so:  The characters aren't really that great.
I absolutely loathe QTEs, which for some reason have lately been way overused (RE5 and bleh... RE6).  However, this game applied them where they didn't bug me, and in some instances were quite good.
What I disliked:  The controls and camera can definitely work against you.  I didn't like having to do a tank like loop to turn around, and sometimes when I'm stealthing, I can't get the camera to see properly around a corner.  These things don't matter too much in Casual/Survival mode, but in Nightmare/Akumu mode it can bring controller smashing infuriation (not sure that's a word, but I'm using it).
Some checkpoint restarts make you have to watch cutscenes which were pretty unnecessary.  Other times checkpoints throw you right into the fray where you don't even get one second to plan out your attack.
It would be nice to have some sort of mercenary mode after you complete the game.  Maybe in the DLC?
Summary:  I've played through the game on all modes except casual, so it must mean I enjoyed it enough to revisit the experience.   Some things definitely bugged me but not nearly enough to avoid playing it.  I have a middle of the line rig and aside from some texture pop in the game performed well and never crashed (I got the game after the latest patch which addressed some issues).
Definitely going to get the DLC.

8/10 -Disturbing. I love the over the top gore it has. It is so satisfying shooting a gun in this game. The story starts out slow but builds up and keeps you confused on what's going on until the very end. This game is not really pop out scary but it's a stressful kind of scary in the sense of surviving. You can set up and disarm traps, upgrade weapons, sneak around stealth killing, hide and even craft bolts for your bow. You can stun, explode, start on fire, freeze and shatter people into bits. The game rewards you for exploring and it really pays off. I did alot of exploring in fact where it made me OCD looking left and right finding jars for upgrades, keys for unlocking stuff, disarming traps to craft with, ammo and health for survival. It's a really long game but you don't feel like it's too long since you will be upgrading and getting new weapons as well as seeing how the story unfolds. The mouse and keyboard controls are spot on. How many matches can a healthy adult human male carry? In this game, the answer is 5. In words: Five. If you want to be able to carry more, you have to inject green jelly taken from killed zombies into your brain. If you do it for some hours, you might be able to finally carry 30 matches at a time. No, I am not crazy, the game is.
Oh, that kind of concept applies to all of your abilites and everything in this game. If such makes sense to you or you find this very interesting, then this game is for you.
Otherwise, think twice before bying, even on sale:
It looks good in screenshots, but is a bit clunky to play. Rather bad console port, not that many fps.
The story seems to be "guy goes mad and gets teleported from one scene to the next", which probably is an excuse to have rather different scenes and screnarios which are not coherent graphically as well as storywise in some way. It's just a mix of mad nightmares and sometimes bad showmanship, probably by total different level designers, which is interesting at first, but wears down later.  The demo was promising, however the full package didn't hold what was promised.
In my taste, you have to run away too often. There is no coherent way to handle things, sometines it is just a guessing  game to try if any of the following works (or, in most cases, NOT): Run away? Kill this enemy? Or do I need to find something before I can progress? Press a lever? Piece my pants? Oh, and you can't save whenever you want, checkpoint style, that means you have to repeat a long sequence to try out again what to do at the end of that sequence. Not too much fun after a while, maybe for the hardcore masochists only that like to get unfair challenges.
I will probably finish this game sometime, however changes of me replaying this are rather low.

In Vermintide, you have to fight as one of five heros against hordes of rat-like "Skaven", that claimed the city Ubersreik as their own, trying to get it back.
I really like the cooperative, action gameplay of Vermintide.
The procedure of the missions is pretty simple. You fight yourself and your teammates through parts of the city, and reach a point where you've got to fulfill the mission task. This kind of reminds me to Left 4 Dead actually.
The game runs very smooth and there are only some little bugs. The environment looks different and gloomy in every mission, which gives the game a good atmosphere.
What could be a little annoying are the hosts. As players host, there can be lags because of the host's connection.
There are some things for your character/hero that you can unlock and use, like weapons. Also, there are some free DLCs.
Overall, I think Vermintide is a great game, especially if you want to play cooperative with you friends (hosting your own lobby is very easy) and have some hours of fun.
It's got it's fair share of problems but otherwise a fantastic game.
