Since Star Trek Online is now free to play, there is no real reason to buy it other than to save yourself a 4 GB download. This is a massive multiplayer online game that is part role playing game, part over the shoulder shooter and part star ship navigation and combat. I love Star Trek as we probably all do to even be here reading this. I've always wanted a game that gives you the total feeling of captaining a star ship, commanding an away team and interacting in a universe. Star Trek online feels shallow and hollow in some areas, yet needlessly cumbersome in others.
The game is shallow with interactions and choices. The game delegates talking with characters down to a portrait and written text. No voice acting, but maybe I have been spoiled. I take that back, there is some horrible voice acting from Leonard Nemoy to start the game and the holographic doctor that acts as a tutorial is one of the flattest and worst voice acting I've ever heard. Especially when the EMH doctor on Star Trek Voyager uses the same lines with a pop and snap. The dialog is so bland that I just skip through it because everything you need to do is marked with an exclamation point. It would have also felt better to be able to interact with more random objects like scan flowers that are not marked and have a 1% chance every hour to find something. There are still interactions like anomalous readings that open up a wave pattern mini game that is very easy to say the least.
Right off the bat it is a disappointment as you are thrown into a conflict with the Borg who in the Star Trek universe should not be for beginners. Nor should they fall easily, but you might as well have a fly swatter for all the Borg you'll encounter.
Luckily if you have a problem with the missions, there is an actual mission editor. You can submit your missions and have them put into the game which is a nice touch.
Like any MMO, you get to pick a race, pick a class from three (red, blue and yellow). Everyone seems to pick red. Each race has special traits and you can customize your look with excessive detail. It all feels very superficial.
When you're not walking around and talking, you're either flying a ship or shooting things. The shooting is good and pretty easy even if its one dimensional. Point your phaser at the target you want to die or blow up and keep firing til its dead. Shooting civilians doesn't matter... and it should. You get an away party that you make up of crew members that you find or recruit throughout your play. Its a fun micromanagement thing and your allies are pretty competition and takes away from a MMO when your party is made of computer characters. The ability to just jump into someone else's party to replace the computer would have been nice.
You have some basic controls to fly around, but it seems a little cumbersome, throttling up to go forward and then going to impulse... Flying around objects and toward objects to blow them up or beam off survivors. The visuals are beautiful here, but the fact you're over dead space makes things seem pretty lifeless unless there's a space battle going on.
Space battles are where the game excels. You have 4 "power" settings... attack, defense, speed and balanced. They all do what you'd think to make it easier for you to survive. In a space battle, your star ship has 4 shields, front, rear, left and right. Taking too much damage to one shield will leave your ship vulnerable and easy to kill. So you need to maneuver around the ship you're facing firing off phasers to drain their shields and torpedoes to finish them. Oh and aft weapons as well. The weapons have cool down times just like any MMO. Some space combat missions feel like a slog when you're on your own... kill 4 enemies here, fly there, kill 4 more enemies, fly there, kill 4 more and go back and they respawn... 1 ship vs 4 quite frequently. There are no quick battles until you level up. Then there are massive battles MMO style where its 10 players vs 1 super ship or 10 players vs 10 ships then 10 more then 10 more then 10 more. There is a noticeably slowdown on my laptop for those.
You can visit your bridge and ship interior from your vessel, but there is little life there. There are plenty of NPCs and big hollow areas, but no one speaks and its more of just a little head nod that... yes we have your ship interior. Perhaps in further stages of the game the bridge opens up, perhaps when your ship is boarded by alien hostiles... but that is just a prayer that's what happens. Perhaps drama of your ship filling up with deadly gasses and you and a party need to save everyone. Oh and another glaring detail is the fact that when you start the game you pick how your uniform looks... why is it no one else from my crew is wearing the uniform I have chosen? Am I the rogue ensign captain that does as he wishes?
The missions greatly vary but after a while they feel very copy and paste. Some missions are well thought out with plot twists. Other missions seem one dimensional, like space battles where you need to destroy 4 satellites protected by a squad each... then fly to pick up dilethium that is guarded, then drop off dilethium but you can't, because your transporters are being blocked by a jamming station that is guarded, so when you return after destroying the jamming station the dilithium drop point is guarded. Constant space battles are not a good thing. Neither are the missions where you are exploring random planets where 2 of which have been baron and devoid of life or action. You are sent down to scan 4 objects on one with no enemies and barely anything to look at. Another planet had me in a cave with no enemies downloading audio logs that I couldn't listen to... what? Those are the bad missions and the missions seem to each take 40 minutes with sections that take 10 minutes.
5 or 6 hours into the game, you get duty officers that you get to send on away missions. These are not missions that you do, but rather as a captain you need to assign the right people for the job. Its a nice little add on, but not needed for sure. The officers have jobs and personality quirks like stubborn, a team player, logical and so on. The missions specify what traits and jobs are best suited for each away mission.
In all, with no voice acting for the flat characters and bland dialog coupled with mediocre missions I can't get into it and I'm a big fan of the lore. I really think that the game makers missed the point of Star Trek and that wasn't space exploration it was drama. Sure you travel to far away planets and dogfight against other star ships, but the point of the TV series and movies was the characters and this game has flat characters. The game doesn't really feel like an MMO. After 15 hours I've never really interacted with anyone except for seen them flying by and the big boss battles. Nothing seems to have consequence, there could have been factions and alliances instead of just Federation vs Klingon. Or your own personal alliances like Morrowind.
For Star Trek nerds who get all the references. Also, a pretty good mmo outside of the star trek fanboy crazyness.

This game changed me. In what little I have played so far, it has already affected me on a deeper level.
First off, it made me realize my mortality as a human. Everyone is fragile in this world, and just because you play the "hero" doesn't make you special. If anything it taught me doing these things are straight up suicides if you don't get your timing right, but even if you do there are inconsistancies, like who is going to investigate, where will everyone be, will the melee or gunner people check first, and who has the faster reaction time?
It also made me understand that going in with seething rage won't help either. Yes, a game where the goal is to kill everyone, going in all rambo-like does not get you the girl. It gets you the grit of your teeth splattered all over the floor. Thinking things out before doing them is the way you have to take it unless you are very lucky and have your timing down.
And lastly, the pleasure of finishing a level doesn't come without it's costs. Once the final victim gargles his last breath of air and blood the mood changes with the music as you grab what you came to get, and slowly walk through the blood and guts of those you killed to get there. The sound of the strings echoing through your headset or speakers as that little voice in your head whisperes "Look at this. This is what you did. Do you understand?" just makes you stop and take in the scenerey for just a moment. Well... do you?
There's something very special about this game. It could just be how much it reminds me of playing free flash games on the school computers back when I was a teen. It's brutal and fun, and rewarding while being punishing and shameful. Some delicate balance was acheived when this game was made. I strongly reccomend it, even from only 2 hours of gameplay.
Really, the only thing I don't understand is the story-line so far, but I have a feeling it'll click the more I play. I got the general idea of what might be going on, but it's still as fuzzy as that pause screen (Which my god, the pause screen in this game takes me WAY BACK to my childhood. Like, damn.)

It sets out to bring the Deus Ex experience to the IOS market, and succeeded in doing that. That is, it succeeded in bringing a very small, cut down, simplified version of the Deus Ex experience that lasts 5-6 hours and consists of a tutorial, a lengthy chat with your friend, and ONE hub area.
Visually, I think the only upgrades provided for the port are MSAA and resolution selection. With the tablet-optimized graphics, you could set the resolution to 640x480 and fool yourself into thinking you're playing a PS2 game with some bloom and some Doom-3-on-Xbox-quality per-pixel lighting on Ben Saxon's face. It apparently runs on Unity as well.
Story-wise, it's ok until the end. Not nearly on the level of even Invisible War, the previous ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ child of the series, but passable... until it just abruptly ends with a cliffhanger for a sequel/episode 2 that may or may not even happen, with no main-quest plot threads tied up whatsoever. Oh, and as an added bonus, nothing you do with your augmentations or weapons in the prologue carries over to the rest of the game, so save your credits!
Control-wise, it's a mess. In porting, the developers decided not to bother with customization support, so you're stuck with the defaults. Admittedly, its defaults do line up with a lot of other games' default controls. Mouse sensitivity is the biggest offender here, as vertical and horizontal are not in sync with each other (with no separate control option) and mouse smoothing is most certainly in effect.
Hate in-app purchases? Guess what- they're still here! Near as I can tell they're in-game money only now, which is far less awful, but it's also the only way to acquire equipment that isn't laying around. Need credits? They're everywhere, and you can even get some just by offing civilians. Just don't expect to know how much a weapon upgrade costs unless you have enough money to afford it AND start the buying process, as it won't tell you otherwise.
Overall, it's... ok. Something to pick up and rush through when it's on sale, but nothing great. Hell, for better value, you could instead just pick up The Missing Link DLC for Human Revolution or play Deus Ex: Nihilum, which give you more of a proper Deus Ex feel with a much better cost-value ratio.

Once again. I'll start off with how great the game looks. The game doesn't have Crysis-like graphics, but it still looks wonderful. The game introduces a lot of quick change in settings. One minute you're in a hospital, then you'll find yourself in a dungeon-like atmosphere in a building located on the otherside of town. The game gives the player a good creepy-like setting that can make the player "jump" at any moment. Jumpscares are definately present in this game. Though not very often. In terms of duration, the game can be at a long duration if you decide to collect all collectables such as map fragments. There are also a lot of upgrades for weapons, stats, and ammo capacities which require a lot of points to upgrade. In this case, it is known as green gel. It is almost impossible to upgrade everything during the first playthrough. New Game+ is present once you have completed the game once. My only concern is the performance of this game. The game tends to run at a better performance when only utilizing one graphics card. SLI seems to run the game at a far more unoptimized performance. A single card configuration is recommended for this game. But even so, the total frame rate still tend to drop. Perhaps the graphics card isn't enough (In this case, the GTX 970). Or, it still require updates. Despite this issue, the game is still worth your time. I had a blast playing this one. If you're a fan of Resident Evil series (Resident Evil 4 in particular), or love the horror genre, this is the game to add to your Steam library!

People kept hyping up for this game but I was completely neutral about it. I didn't watch the trailers and when it's was announced I was furious because I was waiting for that announcement to be the next Fallout game. I was wrong and even though I didn't know back then that this was going to give me hours and hours of fun and appreciation for the developers' creativity. I waited for it to get discount to buy it but let me tell you, even if I paid the full price for it, I wouldn't have any regrets.
Game is visually very strong but I'm not talking about super high texture qualities and such(come to think of it, textures are actually looking a bit bad when the camera zooms in). I'm talking about the artistic choices, the visual style. The filter reminds you of old horror movies, which is good and differenf from other games. And let me tell you, even though the game is kinda linear, thanks to it's levels it never feels that way. Every level feels different from each other, special enemy types and bosses appear in unexpected times, they're all unique in their design and backstory. I loved them personally, especially "the Keeper". Ambient sounds, the music, the visuals, whole atmosphere is just mind blowing.
But, all these things do not tie together very well, because the story-even though it's very interesting- is a little too complex for it's own good. That's the biggest problem for me, games has very memorable moments but lacks a structure bind them together without flaws.
The gameplay is good, you can never have too much ammo to run around and play Rambo. There are traps everywhere and there are special sequences in which you need to avoid a room full of traps for instance. Controls are a bit-just a bit-clumsy, melee attacks are not very effective and these facts fuel the horror side of the game, but not much. Gameplay is more fun than scary.
And game is long, compared to most singleplayer games. It takes about 15 hours to complete for a normal person I suppose. I finished it in 21 hours but that'S just me and my good old "take-it-slow" style. And you can not buy all the upgrades in first playthrough, you need to continue to new game plus mode if you want them all. Games also rewards you with new weapons for each difficulty you defeat and there are 4. And combining these with beautiful levels designs and fun gameplay mechanics, game has a good deal of replayability.
As a side note, people complain a lot about the performance problems and I'm not saying that the game is a good port. But my CPU and RAM doesn't even meet the minimum requirements and I was able to play the game in highest settings with bearable performance. Games is said to be unstable by lots of people, so download the demo before buying if you're worried.
I definitely recommend this game, I loved it, even wanted to give it a hug but then it creeped me out.

This is an Early Access, independently developed horror game running on the Unity engine.
HOWEVER,
this is a rare example of a game that amazes, even in such an early state. The graphics are beautifully done (if a bit unoptomized), the sound design is excellent, the story is intriguing, and the gameplay is terrifying.
The psychadelic aspect of the horror and the fact that you play as a character who is losing (or has already lost) his mind differentiate Layers of Fear from the hundredsd of other similar games. While there are more what I would consider "cheap" jump-scares (sudden loud sounds, scary faces etc.), the majority of the horror comes from varying changes to the world around you. I even know that I missed a few scares from not paying enough attention.
You get out of Layers of Fear what you put into it. If you go into it without wanting to be scared, chances are you won't. However, if you keep an open mind about a slightly different horror experience, it will actually scare the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of you. I definitely am glad I played what there is so far, and I'm glad I'm supporting the developers as they continue creating (and hopefully tinkering) this game. It has the potential to be a masterpiece along the lines of Amnesia: The Dark Decent or Silent Hill 2. I have my fingers crossed that the development continues on strongly, as we have all heard the horror stories of Steam Early Access.
I recommend the game in its current state to big fans of horror so they can watch the game develop and provide feedback to the developers, but to those with a more casual interest, keep an eye on this one for its release, I'm optimistic about the game's future.

As a fan of Warhammer franchise for over 15 years I was excited the first moment I heard: Warhammer co-op game, L4D/PD2 lookalike. Yes! Great idea! Knowing the previously mentioned games, liking them for being really addictive and enjoyable, I couldn't imagine, how Vermintide could be bad. Well, it could. It is, really.
You can't say that graphics or music is bad, these are ok. Nothing really outstanding, but audio-visual aspects are simply right. The end.
The main part of the game, the thing, that should push it, the water for the watermill, the fuel for the engine, the air for the living creatures, should be the mechanics. That aspect sucks. Why? Here comes why:
- Linearity to the limits of boredom
- Fighting system simple to the point of boredom
- Characters levelling - pointless, because you really gain almost nothing with every level. Boring
- Replayability doesn't exist. Because missions are simply boring.
- Characters differences? Almost none. There was no big difference playing as witch hunter or waywatcher - felt so similar.  Boring.
- Customisation? What customisation?
- Weapon modding? Weapon collecting? All praise the RNG-sus, as this is the way to go.
- Equipment choice? Ridiculously small. I don't write about initial choice, I write about the general: you are limited to just a few weapons, that can be only slightly improved. Randomly.
Generally it is ridiculously poorly executed opportunity. There was such a great potential. The possibilities were endless:
- Creating you own hero with some skill/class system, at least bigger differences between preset heroes! Something like support classes with healing and differences in gameplay as tank or agile fighter. Faster and slower ones. Tougher and weaker.
- The forge - weapon creating system that could give you some room to experiment. Maybe secret recipes to find in game or as a reward for achievements. The forge here is just disappointing.
- More possibilities of ending the level - the choice of strategy, maybe different ways of going to the goal.
- More open locations, less linear, some environment features to be more tactical.
- More equipment - armor sets, more slots for collectibles, med supplies, but as well tougher enemies (inflicting more damage), what would make the game more demanding.
- More appealing system of rewards - something, that would attracts you more. Gives you new possibilities to explore. Now the only reward is some weapon - great chance, that it is something you are not interested in. Even if you do, upgrading your equipment is, as everything, random. It's ridiculous!
Well, long story short: a big letdown. The game is just boring. Absolutely wasted potential.
P.S.
There is a possibility, that there will be a lot of features in the future, in paid DLCs. It would be cheap and disgusting trick, because the basic game is just too poor, too simple, underdeveloped. Paying for such add-ons would be like paying for the base game, but part after part for years... In that exact moment it feels, like you are playing early beta.

This game is uncannily similar to Left 4 Dead. I know that is an overdone comparison, but it's true. Everything from the voice callouts, the special enemies,  the player highlighting, to even the feel of the gunplay and melee reminded me strongly of L4D. Where the game differs is in its stronger focus on melee and the progression system.
I primarily enjoyed my time ingame (more on the metagame later). The combat is visceral and the weapons all seem to achieve an appropriate response i.e. the warhammer had plenty of stagger while rapier and pistol had none. The maps were impressive in scope, well varied, and some had interesting gimmicks, particularly the wizard's tower.
Ammunition for the ranged weapons is a greatly limited resource (on some maps) resulting in reliance on the melee. The melee system is basic, but effective. Weapons have a block, bash, light attack, and heavy attack. Which you'll use depends predominantly on what weapon you're using.
This brings me to the main flaw, the weapon unlock system. Not only is this game a grind-athon, but the item unlocks are mostly random. The system works with a roll of dice at the end of the round, some of which are added or replaced based on ingame item collection. Usually the item received is of the lowest or second lowest rarity, but there is a way to craft items of a higher rarity from 5 of a lower. The biggest problem with this system is not the frustrating nature of the RNG, but the fact that you are most likely not going to receive an item for the class you're playing, unless you have an item that gives you a good chance at it (I'm not certain how to get it, but apparently it's common).
Other than the loot system there a few minor complaints I have with the game that don't detract too much from the core enjoyment thereof. The AI can occasionally be bad; enemies and allies occasionally get stuck, sometimes simply refusing to move when they have a path. Difficulty for the missions is all over the place, and the AI director occasionally makes questionable choices (Two Ratling Gunners and a Rat Ogre at once is not okay). Slightly more importantly, the Developer has left their previous projects, War of the Roses and War of the Vikings, which creates questions of how long the game will be supported.
Overall, while I did enjoy my time playing this game (I beat it on normal and played a bit of hard) I did not feel like I'd want to play it much more, unless it was with friends (but what game isn't fun with friends?). I'm not comfortable recommending it due to an overall lack of value and frustrating mechanics.
Thank you for reading. If you downvote my review, I'd like to hear your constructive feedback in the comments because I feel like I gave it a fair overview.

I wish I could say that this game is worth your time, but it's not. If you can get through the download, and get a stable enough client that allows you to actually play the game; then you're in for more disappointment. While TRPGs (or SRPG) aren't exactly the most exciting games on the planet, the excitement you'll feel for the gameplay lasts until around level 15. Which, you might think is a decent chunk of time...but it's not. The first couple of levels go by quick, especially if you're like me; and you don't mind doing extra battles to learn mechanics.
It takes around 15 levels to realize that there isn't too much going on in the game. The mechanics are fairly simple if you've played these types of games before. You'll never have that moment of "Oh, it all makes sense now!" where your able to piece things together. The game maintains some intrigue since there's multiple starting classes with their own gimmicks. But again...give it a couple levels and you'll be back at square one.
So why does the game die a slow death around level 15? Because that's when the grind hits you. Before the game really starts, you'll be grinding. Not for gear. Not for money. Not for experience with the battle system. Just for levels. Because the start of the game is level locked. You'll reach a point after some story missions in the starting town where you'll have to pick a nation to become a citizen of. Once you do that, you'll make your way over to the docks; and be turned away until you're a high enough level. So now you get to splash around for about another 10 levels in the baby pool that is WAKFU's battle system. Killing the same monsters over and over. Doing the same area events over and over. Before you even get to start the actual game.
So, if you're cool with the first ~25 levels of a game being a grind instead of a learning zone that progresses some sort of story, then don't listen to my recommendation. Grind away! But if you're curious about filling that niche of strategy with a hint of MMO elements, stay away. You'll only be wasting your time.

Dungeon Nightmares 2 The Memory is a very well made randomly generated horror game. It is surprisingly very effective at maintaining a constant feeling of tension and fear from start to finish. The game is a roguelike, but the developer added something in the game that was a good idea: If you die, you are taken to a “Pick A Door” room where one door lets you continue, and the other door is Game Over and you start over from the beginning. You don’t know which door is which. So you get a 50/50 chance at being able to continue whenever you die. Another thing that is really good about the game is that this is not another roguelike game that is insanely hard. The difficulty of the game is more tame compared to most other roguelike games. Which is a major plus. It’s nice to see an indie game developer that understands that just because you’re making a roguelike game, that doesn’t mean that you have to make it insanely hard. Just because Edmund McMillen made some insanely hard indie games (Super Meat Boy, The Binding Of Isaac, and The Binding Of Isaac Rebirth) that turned out to be very successful, that doesn’t mean that you have to copy what he did and make your roguelike games insanely hard too. Super Meat Boy, The Binding Of Isaac, and The Binding Of Isaac Rebirth are good games and I do like them. I just wish that more indie game developers would understand that it isn’t necessary for you to make your games insanely hard in order for them to be successful and popular. Dungeon Nightmares 2 The Memory is an excellent example of this. The only flaw of the game that I think is worth mentioning is that the game is too dark and there’s no brightness/gamma setting. You may have to turn up the brightness and the contrast on your monitor to be able to see anything. I get that it’s a horror game and darkness in horror games is expected. But there’s a difference between dark and too dark. This game is too dark. That’s the only flaw that I think is worth mentioning. But it’s not a deal breaker to me. Dungeon Nightmares 2 The Memory is definitely a very well made horror game. It’s tense. It’s scary. And I highly recommend it to horror game fans

Really wish there was a neutral option... overall though, the game is still recommendable, however, nowhere nearly as good as the first -- despite being the larger game (quantitatively):
Graphics and Visuals: virtually the same as the HM1.
Music and Sound: sound same as HM1, however, HM2's tracks to me are better (very slightly). That is saying a lot considering how HM1 had a great soundtrack. Since HM2 is a bigger game, you'll also now get more tracks, and they're all pretty cool.
Story: Here is where the negatives take over... After what the first game established, HM2 could have gone in a very cool direction, however, it feels like a big mess. HM1 felt very random, like you were in some sort of psychadelic haze of murder, but in HM2, they drop that for most of the game. The characters aren't well established, the motives aren't well established. It is very poorly done. If you played the first game, you'll know exactly what I mean. They really dropped the ball, since HM1 had a very cool premise even with its randomness. There were times I felt absolutely lost and confused at what was happening -- this is not the same as in the first game where you wake up in a nightmare-esque state surrounded by shadowy figures, or wondering who is calling you. There are long conversations (seemingly about nothing) between characters whom you have no emotion for and lack any idea about what is motivating them. And when the story gets bad, the game becomes boring. The "protagonists" are killed at one point, then the game resumes with other people. They pull some interesting twists where your "psychopathic killer" is just a police officer, but they take this good idea nowhere. The story is a big mess.
Gameplay: Again, very similar to HM1, but ultimately worse. I'll outline the pros/cons:
+ More characters, with unique abilities (a good idea, but ends up being gimmicky)
+ More weapons, both melee and firearms (you won't notice or care)
+ More enemy types, not by much though
- Less masks to choose from, it allows for better balance, but the mask idea was cool and could have been implemented better (this is what the different characters was about, but they could have used both mechanics together)
- Game is more... difficult? Difficulty is not bad, but there are many times where I feel like I was being shot cheaply off screen, a lot more when compared with the first game. More times where I had to just sit by a door and swing a bat as people would run into me to their deaths. Maybe not everyone will agree with me here, but this was my experience. I would put myself as a "casual Hotline Miami" player. It just felt overall like either the level design/level balance was done better in HM1.
So that's it. In summary if you loved HM1, you'll like HM2 most likely. It's largely more of the same, in a larger package. However, the story fell well short of its potential and you will have to put up with an increase in difficulty (I would say cheapness factor has increased moreso than well balanced difficulty) -- this to me is the reason HM2 fell short of the first game.. In the end, despite its flaws, there is another awesome soundtrack and I do hope they continue the series -- hopefully they'll look back at what made HM1 successful and expand on that.

The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly
The Good:
Creativity - The creativity involved with most of the design of the game and monsters. My two peronal favorite game publishers are Bethesda and Capcom (the old Capcom) and this is why I pre-ordered.
Upgradeable Character - Skyrim alone is proof that players love to build up their character into an invincible force to go kick some tail.
The Bad:
Ammo - The serious lack of ammo (at least the first time round) is why I have only played this game 4 hours so far. There are many better ways to make a game challenging. This is probably the worst thing to do in any game. Players like to feel like they are kicking tail, how can they feel like that without any ammo?
Cheats - When I first learned that there were cheats I had renewed hope for plentiful ammo but I have not been able to get it this cheat to work no matter how much ammo I have on hand. Why not use the tried and true Skyrim console in the future?!
The Ugly:
Aspect Ratios and Resolutions - When I first played this game I really struggled with the aspect ratio. This is something that players should not have to worry about. Most PC gamers have at least 1080p, but many are pushing beyond that now. Games should be made to take advantage of video cards as much as possible. We spend hundreds of dollars on video cards for a reason. Many of us have a 144Hz monitor so limiting games to 30 and 60 is just stupid.

Just finished playing this.
I am lucky enough to own a high end gaming desktop with NVIDIA 3d capability.
Several things I notice with this game compared to HR or Missing link. Mainly to do with graphics.
1. The 3d visualisation is the best I have seen in any game as far as geometrics and perspective are concerned.
However, when wandering the streets of Panama, the lack of textures means that the player feels like he has been shrunk and put down into a city model.
This is especially true of the last playing level at the top of the hotel. It was very entertaining, after changing the allegiance of the box-bot and watching it shoot all the bad guys. The rescue tilt - jet came in and landed. Then after that just walking around and looking at all the objects in 3d was amazing. However, those objects did all look like well made models.
2. Yes. 3d works good until you draw a weapon. Then things get a little messed up. You have a gun barrel on each side of the screen. That needs fixing.
3. The graphics engine takes a lot less out of my system than running HR or Missing link. Usually when I switch to 3d with those games the liquid cooler system cranks up to high speed. However with The Fall, processor core temperatures stayed nice and low without too much cooling effort. Fallout 3 or New Vegas gets it screaming.
4. The gameplay was much easier. Maybe even dumbed down. Then I learned that it had been ported from Android. So I guess everything had to be fitted in with available controls.
5. And that is probably why you can't change the keyboard mapping. I did find annoying and I never really did get used to it.
6. The modifications in the augs. Some good, some not so good. I really liked the stealth dash. I found it useful on a number of occasions. But I miss not being able to jump on top of stuff with augmented legs. I prefer to play stealth rather than muscle. It always yields more loot. So I liked the fact that the hacking system had not changed from HR.
All in all, I am waiting eagerly for the next installment but I hope I get to keep all the augs and weapons I have picked up so far.

==================
While I like this game for it's low budget cyberpunk feel, I can't honestly recommend it until they correct some issues.
- The audio is broken on surround sound systems. Set your audio device to stereo to fix that problem.
- Sometimes there is a slow-down that is apparently due to memory management.
- The game environment sometimes disappears and you just see the background image.
- I've teleported places after jumping over objects or climbing ladders.
Last time I was teleported into a wall, I got the bright idea to save the game and reload... nope, still stuck in a wall.
You have one save slot so my game is ruined unless maybe I find a trainer that will let me no-clip out.
It's not a terrible game (I'm easy to please) because I like the feel of it and it has some story info that supports Human Revolution, but it is a poor port and due to the issues this game has I don't recommend buying it unless you pay less than $1.
UPDATE 1:
I started a new game, it played fine, and I completed it. The only change I made was that I set my video card (GTX 780) to adaptive power management (NVIDIA CP, 3D settings). Not sure if that mattered, but that was the only change; no more teleporting. The game is still a buggy mess but I enjoyed the story. I actually liked the audio but it's too bad that it doesn't work in surround mode.
I won't change my recommendation because the game needs work.
UPDATE 2:
Getting all achievements in this game is fairly easy so I played through a total of 2.5 times to get the achievements. On my second playthrough I got stuck in a wall again; actually I was just stuck against a wall, I guess. Same way, climbed a ladder or maybe I tried to move a heavy box.
I found that by using the Stealth Dash that you could then move around. Stealth Dash yourself to the nearest ladder and climb it, this will let you freely move again but some things may still be broken (I couldn't open a grate or move some boxes). Use a trainer if you don't have the resources to buy Stealth Dash but be careful that the trainer doesn't load you up with money/praxis kits and ruin any challenge.

I really wanted to like this game. I really did. However the game just laughed at me when I lost everything and failed numerous attempts to regain my status as an adventurer. As a result, I'm now so angry that I want to tear this game to pieces. Unfortunately this game is digital and I have nothing to tear.
========================================================
Here's how this happened. I started this game, did some combat traning, and took my first quest. Everything looked fine. I felt an epic adventure ahead of me, and was excited.
Then worries started to appear when I found that I don't have a stable source of income. On the other hand, staying in towns costs money. Keeping warriors in my party costs money. Everything just costs money. There's no doubt I need a large sum of money to power my party up and keep surviving. So what should I do?
Take more quests, of course. So I took another quest of cleaning up some bandits. I chased down a group of bandits, and the game said we would fight with 9 against 11 guys. Well, I thought, who knows, maybe those bad guys are really weak, so I chose to attack despite the disadvantage. Then we lost. I lost my entire party.
It didn't really matter, though. I'll just try to make money by myself, and recruit a stronger party, and start over, I thought to myself. So how do I make money without fighing? By trading. And until now that's the only way I found, that you can earn money from without fighting. If there's yet another way, don't blame me for being stupid, blame the game for not telling me.
The game is kind enough to provide an "assess local price" option, to tell me where to sell stuff to in order to make money. So I became an merchant and bought and sold stuff. Now I could finally build up some wealth and start recruiting men, right? Wrong. Bandits robbed me. Being alone, I certainly could not fight with them. What's worse, the amount of money I lose to bandits is actually higher than the amount I earn from one trading trip. So trading isn't the way to make money, at least not when I'm alone.
After being enslaved by bandits again, I found myself to be completely lost. I had no money. I had no warrior in my party. I had no strength, being at level one. I couldn't fight. I couldn't trade. I only had a bunch of ongoing quests that I would never complete. What do I do now?
Again the game is kind enough to provide a "retire" option. That's the only thing I could do. So I retired and became a beggar, and game over.
========================================================
One of the reasons we love games so much is that, achieving success is much easier in games than in real life. When we meet adversities in real life and become depressed, we can always rely on games to rebuild our spirits and get ready for tomorrow.
However Mount and Blade works the opposite way: instead of boosting my morale, this game actually takes on the role of the real world to depress me, and remind me that adventures are only for the wealthy people and the big parties. Just when I'm in this stage of life when I see a bright and promising future before me, this game jumps in to give me realistic experience on how life feels when everything is lost.
I hate this game.
I usually give a rating to every game I review. However I'm not doing it here, because such a rating would be extremely personal and subjective, and thus meaningless.

If however, you take this game for what it is-- a silly, casual-arcade style shooter, where zombies can topple your uber-tower by digging out the foundation, where your teammate's head may explode into tiny red blocks and splatter your clothes... and if play with some friends, you will definitely have some fun.   It is worth the buy when it's on sale (full price may be too much)!
BOTTOM LINE: If you're looking for some stupid fun and a break from the run-of-the-mill shooters, this may be what you're looking for.

Excellent game. It might not be an AAA title, but damn if it doesn't try.
The aesthetics are really sweet even if the graphics technology used feels a bit last-gen.
The missions are varied, most of them have interesting victory conditions to offer players a challenge different to just carving a way through to the end.
There's quite a lot of weapons, and each of them feels distinct from the rest.
Every character uses different weapons and thus plays differently. The wizard offers the most unique experience, but even the dwarf is a fresh take on the warrior archetype - in contrast to other characters, you never have a clear overview of the situation on the battlefield because of your puny height! It might sound lame, but it really feels fun and unique once you try it out.
The controls are solid. They're not just mindless W+1 (forward and left mouse button), you actually have to get a feel for each weapon's speed, strength, range and special traits to be efficient with it. Once you learn to control the weapon's weight, you might even catch yourself physically shifting your own weight with each swing.
Two of my main gripes with the game is the performance and lack of versus play. I've got a pretty beefy PC, yet Vermintide runs at below 20FPS on highest settings. I hope the devs do get around to implementing versus some day.
Despite a few flaws, I highly recommend.

I absolutely love this game. I play it often. It does take time to get 'used' to. But, when you get the hang of it, it is an absolutely easy game. With that said, it takes time like any mmorpg. If you are looking for an old school MMO with a classic style turn based strategy gameplay, this game is tons of fun. The early levels will leave you confused, and it may deter some new players, but, leaving and coming back was often the biggest mistake. Currently I have almost six classes at 150, and frankly, leveling is not even on my mind. I just get a bunch of gear and do quests, and that is sufficient enough to keep it going. With the said, picking a class is often the most difficult part.
-Tanks- Feca, Sacrier, Pandawa, and I have heard some folks use foggernauts as a tank supplement.
Each of the afore listed can also supplement in other aspects of the game, such as posititioning and dealing damage, either from long range or mid range, to melee.
-DPT (Damage per turn)- Every class can fill this role, but there are a handful of classes whose roles excel in this condition: (in no particular order) Cra, sram, ecaflip, xelors, iops, sadidas, osmadas, enutrofs, rogue, foggernaut, masqueraiders, huppermage's, and eliotropes.
Each DPT class fulfills a very different form of dealing damage, some just deal pure damage, like iop, cra, and foggernaut. These three I believe deal the most "direct" damage without gimmicks and can be the easiest to transition into this phase. While the others can serve a purpose as supplementing and even tanking to healing. The masquraider can heal and I believe in dofus it can tank, but in this game it would be difficult without a lot of support.
-Healing classes- These are by far needed in at least the later levels around 70+ once you start doing harder dungeons like the 66+ dungeons. While a lot of classes can heal, eniripsa is considered the better or more traditional healer. I have not healed with the other classes, as such, my comments will remain bias, as my eni did well enough to drop a second eni and pick up a sixth dps class in its stead.
Eniripsa, huppermage, eliotropes, masqueraiders, pandawa, sadidas, ecaflip's, and osmadas (although they might have a level condition to healing.)
Apologies for the messy review.

Been playing this game on and off for a few years. It's getting on in years but is hands down one of the best standalone Souce mods out there.
It still has a small, but active community, and whilst some of them may be a bit... interesting, you will be made to feel welcome. Very rare to see any drama in this game, although kids will be kids and being a free game and all it has it's fair share.
The gameplay is easy to understand for a new player, just remember to capture the chests and attack the team with the most chests and you will be sailing (no pun intended). Games are split between 3 teams, Pirates, Vikings and Knights (obviously), so new players can tend to get confused as to who to attack, but like I said, attack the team winning.
Combat is different depending on which team and class you choose.
The Pirates have the super quick Skirmisher, the high DPS slow paced Captain, and the Sharpshooter, a low health class armed with a long range musket.
The Vikings have the low armor Bezerker capable of high damage but with little versatality, the Gestir, armed with a spear and throwing javelins (a very versatile class and my personal favourite) and the Huscarl, a highly armored axe wielder which is a great class for a new player in my opinion.
The Knights have the Archer, which is self explanatory and has probably the highest skill ceiling in the game. A great archer is a force to be reckoned with. The knight is the tank of the team and the game really, highly armored and capable of heavy damage but slow. The Man at Arms is French, quick and farts.
In short this game is definitely worth a gander if you like the idea of fun melee fest with a couple of old timey muskets thrown in for good measure. If Chivalry is too grim and muddy give this a whirl for a different kind of melee experience.

Its a good game, with a lot of problems that might turn people away for a start. I can see why not a whole lot of people have stayed with the game, and I'll give you some pointers/warnings.
1) BLOCK. I can't stress this hard enough, and unfortunately not a whole lot of tutorial for blocking happens at the start, especially with how IMPORTANT of a mechanic it is. You might not expect being one shot by bosses at level 1, but here we are - you walk outside the city, see a juicy monster with a golden skull above its head... then BAM. There goes your all your health. If you don't block, you WILL get your head bashed in, even with the "tank" classes.
2) Pick this game up with the intention to play with friends, because I find some bosses quite a bit frustrating to solo without grinding ahead to get a damage advantage. You can tell some of these bosses and mobs have been given mechanics to cater to a 2-4 man party, because bosses like Barbuda literally stunlock you to death (almost like it was expected that there would be some sort of healer/buffer/tank around to help you).
3) There is no lategame if you're playing solo. Epic Mode is literally unplayable without a party. Unless you're that stubborn, in which case, you can go ahead and try. It's either minutes of gruelling wet-noodling with a tank build or instantly dying with an offensive build.
Its a 7/10. Cute visuals, great music and has a funny Zelda reference. Pick up on sale, and its just a couple bucks for a quick, pixelly, little nostalgia trip.

It is an improvment over the first game. The story is improved, and the soundtrack is quite good. I also like having multiple characters this time around, which I prefer over the original's limitation of slecting a mask. However, this game still does not fix the main problems I had with the original that ruined the experience for me. When I first began playing HM2 something just made the game feel better; I was actually enjoying the game but didn't find TOO much changed from the original to explain it. Then I got farther into the game and figured it out:
Those were the beginning levels.
Yes, progress into the game and the frustration all comes flooding back. The AI will fail to hear a shotgun blast one room adjacent from you, but somehow the guy on the edge of the screen notices. I'm most of the way through this game, currently on chapter 10 and I have to say I am bitterly disappointed. It is neither an ode to Silent Hill nor a glorification of RE4, but a shambling incohernet mess of a game with many techncial issues. It has only become playable since the recent third patch for me so I have arrived late to the party. The terrible ID4 engine has been used and yet again there are texture streaming issues even on a SSD and r290 videocard with 4GB ram, and the aliasing is just terrible..it's just not a pretty looking game. I'm playing with a 360 gamepad and it feels clunky, it is far worse with a keyboard, particularly if you are a twitch shooter, so get used to loading textures every time you spin.
The save points are spreadly quite thinnly, which worked well in Alien Isolation, but here I have been continually robbed by cheap deaths (such a locked in a room with fire looking for a needle in a haystack or emptying all my ammo into an invincible enemy). I don't often rage quit but it has happened three times in this game, it can be quite unfair to the player and then to add insult to injury it sends you back 20mins progress..grrr..

While I did quite enjoy this game, I really can't recommend it, for two reasons. Firstly, it ends very abruptly. Now, you may have played games with sudden endings before, but those probably made sense - this one just doesn't. I thought it was a bug at first. There's no indication it's coming. There's no resolution to what you see in the game, no explanation, nothing resembling a story beat. There's no indication of why the game ended at that point. It really is like they just ran out of money and decided "well, let's ship what we've got even though the game ends half-way through a level".
Secondly, there are a couple of incredibly frustrating bugs. Firstly, there are many spots where you can get inescapably stuck on the level geometry, and then you have to restart from the last checkpoint. And secondly, sometimes you'll load your game and find that you're *already* stuck in the geometry, and have to restart again.
tl;dr: Buggy and unfinished. Do not buy.

This is a very good simple FPS game with elements of building and sapping thrown in. It's basically a stripped-down version of the system in "Factions" survival servers in Minecraft, but don't expect it to replace MC or anything because like I say it's rather stripped down to the essence. This is good because you can pick it up immediately. The class system is well balanced, and you can pick a class that focuses on frontal assault, sniping, or building defensive structures or sapping the enemy structures. (All classes have weapons and build/destroy capabilities, but some are much better at different things than others.)
This is a great game for when you want some FPS shoot-em-up fun where weapons destroy voxels and the strategy isn't super complex or super involved. And to make things better, if you feel more like building or tearing stuff down to help out your more heavily armed yet no so structurally inclined team members you can pick a support class that gets major bonuses to those things at the cost of some direct offensive power.
So it's not a Minecraft replacement, but it's also not just a crunchy pixel shooter with editable voxel-based arenas. If you were expecting the latter then the game will probably exceed your expectations.

There are definitely better shoot 'em up games out there that deserve your time and money more than this one. I have a few issues, and while I can probably think of more later, this is what I thought of off the top of my head.
1) The random guy mumbling random sayings.
2) Constantly flashing lights for no real reason. That makes it a problem when you're trying to see what you're supposed to shoot or avoid.
3) Constantly floating backwards when not controlling your ship at all. It's so annoying when you have to stay in a spot to heal you have to keep going right to keep up. In other games, you stay where you're at.
4) Maybe this is just me, but I don't remember many side-scrolling shoot em ups to have enemies come from both the top and bottom of the screen when there isn't a ground or ceiling. This means staying to the left of the screen is the only real "safe" place, but it's near impossible to stay there when the screen is almost filled with enemies and bullets. It feels cheap staying to the top middle of the screen only to die because an enemy popped up off screen and hit your ship.
5) Regular weapons can overheat. To some degree I can kind of see why they went this route, but considering the amount of enemies on a screen at certain points, it takes too many stat points to properly upgrade that stat and other games that don't have that mechanic, I found it frustrating not being able to defend myself while the screen is filled with enemies. Have you ever wanted to play a shoot 'em up where your weapons can overheat? If so, then this is the game for you.
I'm sure the creator put in some effort to make a competent shoot 'em up, but it seems like it really didn't bother seeing other quality games in the genre (i.e. Gradius) and using similar mechanics, and it made me feel like the creators were okay putting something out that was average at best, and I'm being really generous about that statement. I had this on my wishlist for a while, and while I'm glad I got it on sale for 3 bucks, I can't recommend buying it at any price. If you're wanting a good shoot 'em up, check out Revolution Ace. Sure it's an overhead view and not a side view, but the mechanics are much better, a 2 player mode is available, there are RPG elements, and if you catch it on sale, you can find it for 16 cents, which I wouldn't spend that much on this game.
Bottom line: Save your time and money for better games in the genre.

If you're a Trek fan, there's a lot to love.  You'll recognize people, places, things, and plots from across Trek's 50 year history, you can even play a TOS-era character as an alternate start method.  Gameplay is very combat heavy, but this *is* an MMO.
The F2P model is very fair (if you're not trying to PVP at a high level, anyway), and you can finish the game without spending a single dime if you wish.  Zen (the store currency) can be bought with in-game resources, but even not counting that you can use entirely free ships and weapons to finish the story and dive into the endgame, it's just a bit harder.  The endgame grind can, admittedly, be a slog.  Mostly in time, not in repetiveness if you plan it right, but it's still there.  That grind is only as important as you want it to be though.
STO is not without its problems, but that's not uncommon with MMOs.  Yes, there's bugs, yes, it can be laggy, but for most people it's not so bad as to hurt the experience.  If you want a fun romp full of Trek nostalgia, STO is worth a look.

In certain games it can be difficult to wrap your mind around what kind of game the developers are attempting to make, resulting in a frustrating and confusing experience. In the first 10 minutes this game, you get an idea of it's potential while simultaneously showcasing it you.
The movement when your not in combat is similar to a MOBA, but while in combat it's similar to XCOM minus the RNG. As far as abilities and different characters, this game seems to cover them all, and while you choose a character in the beginning you can still OBSERVE/CHALLENGE the other characters (in the form of NPCs) in the world and get a sense of how they fight and work.
Overall I would say that this game is near perfect in what you want out of a strategy game of this type and style... it is at least for me. Interestingly enough, what got my attention to even try this game was a gif posted on a social site of one of the level up animations of one of the characters on 9gag and it was beautiful... ads are getting smarter they say.

FULL GAME REVIEW
PROS
+The atmosphere and setting is just so good.
+Great and varying jumpscares.
+Truly an amazing soundtrack. I wish it played more often though.
+Not only a beautiful game to listen to, it's also pure eye candy.
CONS
-Little to no gameplay/challenge. Layers of Fear is basically a "walking simulator".
-The ending is a little unsatisfying in my opinion.
-Some "puzzles" leave you wandering around and around.
-Some parts are direct rip-offs from PT Silent Hill.
-One playthrough is only 3 hours.
The early access was amazing but sadly I had high hopes for the full game. Too high.
With that said, it's still a great game. Layers of Fear is a psychological horror of stunning visuals, sounds, setting and scares. What it lacks of is the gameplay; there's almost none of it and what we get is just straight out annoying "puzzles". Nevertheless, still worth buying and playing if you're up for a scare.
7/10.

Where To Begin..
Taking a deep personal journey through what appears to be alcohol-related psychosis, nothing is ever as it seems in this game. What was familiar territory two minutes ago turns to be a heart-thumping and radical new approach. Layers of Fear provides an immersive experience, a pulse-racing atmosphere, and deep-rooted fear that makes you not want to pan your camera around to witness the horrors going on around you.
In Short - The Good:
Variety - nothing is ever as it was, this game will make you second guess yourself.
Immersion - the atmosphere is dark, the sound effects are spectacular, you will feel as the character feels.
Psychosis - This is an interesting twist and a big plus to the horror genre. I would like to highly accolade the staff and programmers for the variety this effect produces in-game.
Graphics - Top notch, very few bugs (if any) that prevented gameplay even for early release.
Scary - This game is terrifying. Simply put, using headphones and playing in the dark adds to the experience and immersion.
In Short - The Bad:
Content/Length - The only thing I find lacking, is the antithesis to early release so I can't even bring it up legitimately. I cannot wait for the finished product and increased content once released, keep up the great work!
This is the first review I have ever written and find Layers of Fear to be so deserving. I stand, bow, and clap to the staff, programmers, and producers for creating such a unique and terrifying experience; kudos to such a great product!

It is an improvment over the first game. The story is improved, and the soundtrack is quite good. I also like having multiple characters this time around, which I prefer over the original's limitation of slecting a mask. However, this game still does not fix the main problems I had with the original that ruined the experience for me. When I first began playing HM2 something just made the game feel better; I was actually enjoying the game but didn't find TOO much changed from the original to explain it. Then I got farther into the game and figured it out:
Those were the beginning levels.
Yes, progress into the game and the frustration all comes flooding back. The AI will fail to hear a shotgun blast one room adjacent from you, but somehow the guy on the edge of the screen notices. I've been shot by offscreen baddies who are standing in a hallway so long that not even the look feature could see them (leading to a horribly cheap death), and yet when I purposefully try to bait an enemy he just stands there. Melee swings will fail to hit someone half a foot away. The highscore system rewards playing like a madman, which will usually get you killed. What will work is, mentioned earlier, baiting the enemies into coming towards you to hit em' with a crowbar, but it isn't fun. Only consider buying this game if you can get it combined with the original for $5; emphasis on "consider".

It's not perfect, even in the flawed way that the first one was, but it's pretty great.  The aesthetic is fantastic; the music is good; the gameplay is a lot of fun; and the story seems to even make a little more sense than the first one did.  Definitely worth the time and money.

The game has its flaws, but it is still one of the best games. It is a third person shooter with MOBA elements in it. You choose a character and the character has different weapons and 3 abilities. Each character is fairly unique and they each have their own personality to them. Each character had their own unique outfits you could buy with real $ and their own taunts which is unique to this game. The taunts were a great way to add character to the different "Pros" as they are called in this game and even rewarded you for doing it after a kill... but it was risky because you would be stuck in the animation for a few seconds and not be able to cancel out of it so if you did it near a enemy player they would just kill you during the animation. There are also announcers that are constantly commenting on the game, making it seem like a pro sport than a actual game adding to the feel and environment of the game.
The game consists of 2 lanes and each lane there are bots constantly spawning and you have to push the bots into the enemy teams base because there are turrets set up along the lanes that are shielded and cannot be damaged until a bot shoots it first. Once a bot shoots the turret and gets rid of the shield you are then able to attack the turret and eventually destroy it. This encourages defending your lanes at all times and trying to push your enemies back so that you can get more map control.
There is also a jungle and depending on the map it is either above you or below you. The game has a lot of vertical movement and requires quite a bit of skill in aiming for certain characters. Throughout the game you can spawn your own bots with money you earn from killing other players and killing bots / turrets. The bots you spawn vary depending on where you buy them and they can either help you push a lane or you can buy bots that directly target enemy players and ruthlessly hunt them down. Usually it is best to just buy the pushing bots, but if you are good enough you can follow your "kill bot" as I'll call it and hunt with it and find a player off by him/herself. In the jungle there is also a useable node called the Annihilator. It is EXTREMELY important, what it does is it costs $1000 to use and it has a channel time and if you do not get interrupted it will damage enemy players and KILL all bots on the enemies team. There are also several different mascots that spawn in the jungle throughout the game in order to give your team money / buffs depending on which one spawns.
As I said, the game has its flaws... The population died pretty much to nothing when they accidentally released the game by sending a ton of beta keys out when they were still in closed beta and they foolishly decided to launch the game instead of just throwing a "Open Beta" tag on the game. When people actually played it, they saw that it still had its moments where lag would screw you over because this game has Grapples which every character has, it basically locks you into a animation with a enemy player and does damage based on what character you are. Players would sometimes get grappled out of the air because of latency issues and it was very frustrating. The game also didn't have enough characters, I believe it had 14-15 character when they accidentally launched and I'm pretty sure that turned off some people. The game also had quite the grind to unlock characters and mods and the characters at release cost way too much. The price of everything has gone down quite a bit and is MUCH more reasonable... however, I believe it was too late. The devs have sadly abandoned this game as it hasn't received a real update in about a year. I am still sad to this day that the devs let such a great game die such a early death because it is truly a great game... they just made too many mistakes.

I LOVED the original Dungeon Nightmare game when it came out way back when, and when I heard there was a second I just HAD to try it out. Unfortunately, this one is done so much worse, and I had to PAY for this one.
First of all, the game is way too dark to be remotely playable. It has absolutely no brightness settings, and I'm not going to change the brightness and contrast on my monitor for 15 minutes to be able to play a game. I get that horror atmosphere's are supposed to be dark, I LOVE dark games, but making it TOO dark is just as dumb, if not dumber, than making it too bright. Then, the candles do next to nothing when trying to see better, and the flick of the cigarette lighter (or whatever it is you have if you don't have candles) takes way too long to re-use to make it useful. Flick it for .2 seconds, then absolutely unequivocal darkness for 5 more seconds. Repeat.
The level layout is pretty damn bland as well, with nothing really interesting to do but roam around in a maze until you die or find an item. I guess that's probably why they made the game so dark: to cover the fact they have no quality level-design skills. The original game wasn't great either, but at least it was free! This is basically the same thing except it's A) Darker, and B) a little bit nicer graphics. I did read from another review that this game has randomly generated levels? I don't know if that's true, but if it is: don't. It is MUCH nicer to have a well-crafted linear level then a bunch of terrible randomly-generated ones. Spend the time and make your game actually play well.
If I'm going to make suggestions, though, add some kind of music or background noice other than light breathing, footsteps, and a heart-beat. The game sounds boring when you're groping around in the darkness every which way. Doesn't have to be fancy, it can definitely be subtle, but having nothing is lazy and subtracts from the experience.
The graphics were a really nice upgrade, but they don't make up for the actual mechanics. I wish I could say this was a good game, but it has no potential unless they fix the issue with the brightness. This game is not worth the price when the first game is free and better than this one. It was just done better.

The short: This game was a lot of fun with a great horror environment, graphics and monster design with some exceptions. The random level generation was my favorite and most hated aspect of this game. Would recommend.
The Good:
I had a lot of fun with this game. The graphics were really well done for the scope of the game and the sound design was spot on to build suspense, peak, and then relax to repeat. However my favorite part was the random level generation, while also my most hated part (I'll get to that in a sec). Failure at a level means that you can go back in and try again knowing that you will have a different experience. It made repeated failure more tolerable with one exception.
The Bad:
This game made me yell profane things I am not proud of at my TV screen. One level in particular was the entire cause of this. Without spoiling too much, it's the only level with a timer. My problem with this was that the random level generation would build a level that leaves you making too many uninformed guesses that can lead you to a no-win scenario. The level generator was clearly adjusted to try and prevent this by making levels more linear, but in the process was the cause of the problem too.
I frequently found that I would be presented with a fork in the road near the start of each level. One would lead to the exit key and the other would lead a very long path that eventually is the level's exit. Once you have realized you chose the wrong path and missed the exit key, backtracking to get it wastes too much time and you won't make it to the exit in time. If you get to the exit and don't have all 3 required "keys", you will have to replay the level. Pair that with the fact that you have a bunch of monsters that want you very dead and you are in for a bad time based on far too much guess work where even memorization is useless thanks to the random level generator. It just felt unfair.
This level almost made me rage quit, but I kept on because I was so far in at that point that I really wanted to stick it out with the rest of the experience being a total joy.
Final Thought:
If you like horror games in the realm of silent hill that explores the perception of reality in a very dark and grimy way, I would strongly tell you to give this a try.
To The Devs:
I want to personally thank you for a (mostly ;] ) fantastic experience with some really cool designs and play that kept me always wondering what the next part of the game would show me. I love the variety and pacing of this and I wish you the best of luck with whatever you make in the future!

I was thankful to step away from this game for a very long time to come back when the game has the chance to prove its self again. Thankfully the stuff I talked about before has either been improved (to a extent only you can determine) and the Russians have been balanced. But the biggest importance to this game is bringing it to steam after all the short-comings the developers brought us. Its contiuned to survive and strive.
So far, I really like the game and will continue to play it for a long time. Here are the pros and the cons of Heroes and Generals:
Pros:
-Massive Multiplayer campaigns; Nations slugging it out under the command of the General players that determine were Assault teams will be sent and fight to a area. Its quite awesome. The end goal of each nation is to capture a certain amount of major cities and then eventually win the war. The war of course resets after and you can again choose the nation you want to fight for! Some of these wars can last from several days to several hours, depending on how the Generals direct were battles are fought and if the players can win those battles.
-Big battles; around 40+ people can fight in some of the biggest battles you will ever see. With a sometimes a balanced experience of tanks, aircraft and other transportation vehicles making battles deceisive to capture a point and either hold it or to advance. (Depending on the game mode of Skrimish or Assault)
-Tactics & Strategy; Now, working with your team is a small feat in this game, but if you get a full squad of friends and go out into the battlefield, your tactics and strategy can change the course of the battle in minutes. This can also be applied on how you drive tanks (were to position them, were to fire on a enemy tank), aircraft (dog-fighting and aireal manuvers) and gun-play (what type of guns to use for long-range, medium-range and short-range engagements)
-Gun variety; Many guns to choose from and many ways to earn them. With the ribbon system, you can rank up quite easily with a weapon by simply killing enemys with it! So getting upgrades such as heavy barrel, specialized triggers or etc. can make you customize your gun to the max! But, in general, the gun selection is nice, but not massive. But there is still variety to make it enjoyable.
-Heroes and Generals; Heroes are the guys on the ground, the men that fight via infantry, armored, paratrooper, recon, and pilot to determine the fate of battles. Generals are the men that command the Assualt Squads by buying them through War Funds. They deploy these men in battles to determine who wins on the war map. I think this is a cool feature, but there are some disadvantage of this.
-Awesome Main Theme Soundtrack; The music is awesome.
Cons:
-(Microtransactions) The microtransctions are everywhere, for guns, vehicles, camos, changing name of weapons, and etc. through using Gold. Now, within the recent updates its gotten a lot better as players now have to unlock that next weapon or unlock that next vehicle before they can use the gold they bought with their real money to actually get it. But, in the long run, if you want to get a weapon or vehicle quickly without grinding to get the credits for it, the microtransctions are right there to maybe help you get it more quickly while emptying your wallet. I also think with the Walker update that Ribbons now make it hard to P2W as you have to pay out the♥♥♥♥♥just to get to that next gun. You can't simply buy the weapon anymore with gold. The same can apply for vehicles.
-(Game Performence and Graphics) The game runs poorly at times, depending on the map. Me having a very excellent computer (FX-8350 4.1 ghz, GTX 770 4 gigs, 16 gigs of ram, massive CPU Fan that keeps my CPU temp down to around 40 C or lower during gameplay) is quite disappointing. In recent patches, they have addressed this low FPS by optimizing the game. I have recently been able to get around 30-60 FPS.
Having good FPS for this game makes ALL the difference in combat, so if you have a sub-par computer, this might be a issue for you. I also feel the graphics for this game are not amazing and if anything are average for a game around 2010 or earlier and pretty poor for a "next-gen" 2015 game (as it is still in beta). But from what I heard, they will be up-'ing the graphics after FPS and multiplayer sessions have been improved and expanded.
-(Clans) No distincable clan system without a General. I can't really have a in-game way of tracking all of my members or be able to have the ability to have some sort of chain of command without using exterior system that I would have to create on TS3, a website or etc. Its not a huge issue, but if you have a lot of friends and want to keep track of them or want to form a in-game clan, you better start thinking on how you are going to go about it. Without a General, its hard to have a real clan without paying 50 bucks up front or having a person who grinded all the way to a General.
-(Weapons and Maintenance)The Grind is a huge factor for many to contiune to play a game. The grind for Heroes and Generals is not awful and it does not bother me, but for many of you, I might bother you. In early levels, it does not take long to get a tank or a decent weapon, but it takes a very long time to get a medium grade weapon (Tompson, MP40, M1/M2, STG44, and etc.) without microtransction it. Important weapons such as Anti-tank weapons don't take long thankfully but are very expensive to maintain, so killing a lot of tanks with a bazooka or other anti-tank weapons will cause your credits to drain quickly from usage. Maintaince is high of everything and ammo is expensive. Thankfully all weapons start with "auto-refill and repair off" so you can manage it, but it still costs a ton of credits to manage it and to continue to use it.
-(Leveling) Leveling up and becoming a General is quite long. There are two ways you can become a General, grind and work very hard to hopefully eventually reach the level were you can pay to become a General via in-game credits or pay with real money for around $50. The grind to become a General is quite long and hard and for those who do not have much money to spend on games, it will take you a very long time to become a general and to actaully command the larger battlefield.
In Conclusion...
Overall, Heroes and Generals is a fun game that keeps me coming back. With recent updates, the game is just getting better and better. It has a long way to go before its really complete, but its making good strides.
Give it a try and see how you like it!

Pros:
+ Better characters, there's a lot of variety in the characters, you see where they came from, and they actually have a personality.
+Better story, overlaps a bit with the last point, but it's basically an origin story, a prequel and a sequel of Hotline Miami 1 all in one. For example, you now know where Beard came from and why he was in every store Jacket visited. Also, I'm a huge fan of the Guy Ritchie-method of storytelling where you have a bunch of different storyline that at first seem unconnected, but that all collide into eachother at the end.
+More gameplay features, every character has his/her own unique game mechanic, which is showed off really well in Deathwish for example. There are more settings like Hawaii, the subway, a container ship etc. Overall the game is way more expansive.
Cons:
- The level design. Oh, the level design. This is by far the biggest con in the game. You can be shotgun-sniped from 6 miles away through 9 windows and an open door. The game basically forces you to alert almost all of the enemies, stand around a corner and one by one give them a bullet to the gut as they run up. I guess the developers felt that with a bigger and more expansive game, you should have bigger and more expansive levels. Hotline Miami 2 did the same thing as Dark Souls 2 and Portal 2. They expanded, but because of that the game felt much less solid and compact.
- For the most part, the game decides who you're gonna play as. Some of the characters' game mechanics are really annoying (Evan and Alex & Ash for example), but you can't switch to a less annoying character.

Free. Amusing. Entertaining. These are just some words to describe this game. But in spite of being completely free of charge with no hidden fees included, this game is all but gratuitous. I have been playing this game casually, every now and then, for the past 10 years now, and I have got to say that this game is probably one of the funniest video games that I have ever played in my entire life. The voices of the characters, the absurdness of the teams available - pirates, vikings, and knights - of which only the knights and the pirates would have realistically fought each other (albeit not in 13th Century harnesses with greatswords against 18th Century blunderbusses wielded by pirates), and the entire atmosphere of the game all make Pirates, Vikings, and Knights II a game that keeps on being enjoyable, year after year.
However, Pirates, Vikings, and Knights II has been in development for over ten years now. This is something that may be considered as a good thing, because it shows dedication and persistence from the development team, but it may also be considered as a minus, because the development of PVKII has been rather slow in the past decade. All of the classes that have been intended to be included in the game have not been finished, yet, and there is currently no ETA on when the rest of the classes will be implemented. There are also some balancing issues with some of the classes in the teams. For example, the Man-At-Arms of the Knights has been criticized for being too overpowered against his enemies, mainly due to his surprisingly long-lasting and powerful special attack that leaves the opposing players, first of all, very dead, but also in an unblissful awe of how childish and lame the Man-At-Arm's special attack is.
But in spite of the minor class balancing issues and historical inaccuracies, or maybe because of them, Pirates, Vikings, and Knights II is still an epic video game that continues to lure in new players, perhaps out of curiousity, even though the game has been around for over a decade.
