I got this game expecting a decent horror or survival-horror experience, and was sorely disappointed. It's basically Resident Evil 4, but with an even more nonsensical plot, an unsatisfying weapon/character upgrade system, and lackluster gunplay.
There's very little horror in this game - if you want a horror-themed shooter, go play F.E.A.R., because all you'll get here is some dirty, grimy settings that try to squick you out with blood and gore. There's one, and only one, decent horror scene, and that's fairly early in the game...everything else takes the Saw route of "horror" with 90% of the game being basically just torture porn. Most of what little scares they try to provide are nothing more than jump scares. Then again, I am particularly difficult to unnerve, so this is a very subjective complaint.
The plot is horribly explained, at least for what little they actually bother to tell you. You're never told what the antagonist's plans or goals are; hell, you go through the entire game learning next to nothing about even your two partners. The main character is boring at best and completely unlikeable at worst. They try to give him some character development via bits of journals you can pick up during the game, but it's not enough to redeem what's just a very boring character. He has only one conversation of note during the entire game that gives any sort of look into his psyche, and that conversation ends after two lines about his alcoholism. Due to the setting of the game, you're whisked around from location to location on a whim - the game plays very loose with its deus ex machina. By the way, the phrase "deus ex machina," is particularly relevant to this storyline, so I don't use it lightly; it is LITERALLY a deus ex machina. I'd say the story is full of plot holes but, to be frank, so little is explained that I'm not sure; it's hard to find a plot hole in a big pile of absolutely nothing. You get more plot explanation from the model viewer's info dumps than what you're told or shown in the entire course of the game.
The upgrade system seems shoehorned in. What's this green liquid? Why does it increase your ability to put more shotgun shells into a shotgun? Why do you need to shock your brain to know how to carry more matches? Narrative nonsense aside, many of the upgrades are useless: you barely need to upgrade your stock since the game does not give you enough ammunition to take full advantage of the extra space, you don't need to hold more healing syringes because most of the attacks that can kill you are one-hit kill grabs, there are very few situations where extra sprint is useful (and during all of those the game actually gives you an unlimited sprint bar anyway), and upgrading the explosive range of your explosive crossbow bolts can actually be detrimental since it hurts you as well. The only useful upgrades I found were the damage upgrades for the main three weapons (revolver, shotgun, and sniper rifle). Here's a tip, by the way: there's a missable magnum in chapter 11. I didn't get it, ended the game with an inventory full of magnum rounds, and was♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥to find out from the wiki that you only get two chances at the gun in that one chapter.
I compared this game to Resident Evil 4 initially, but, really, that's a disservice to RE4. That game's shooting mechanics were far tighter, it didn't have a wonky stealth system that sometimes just doesn't work, and the bosses in that game were far more entertaining to fight than in this game. Nearly all of the bosses in The Evil Within have at least one instant kill grab attack, which wouldn't be so bad if the game allowed you to skip the cutscenes (I can't recall a single cutscene before a boss that can be skipped, despite the game allowing you to skip cutscenes during other parts of the game) that happen before AND DURING some boss fights. There's a fight against one particular boss, the Keeper (the enemy with a combination safe for a head), where if you die you'll have to sit through 2 cutscenes DURING THE FIGHT. EVERY TIME YOU DIE. That's not good game design, Bethesda!
As for technical issues, it crashed on me twice during gameplay (of which I put in ~15 hours, I think). Not sure what that was about. Other than that it runs fine enough. I didn't notice any obvious framerate problems, graphical glitches, etc. Not stellar, but passable on that front.
tl;dr If the game had either good gameplay or a good plot I might recommend it. However, it has neither. This is simply, in my opinion, not a good game. It's not worth your time and it's certainly not worth your money, even during this current sale. My recommendation instead, if you want a horror shooter? Go and get F.E.A.R., and if you like that, get the sequel (stay away from F.3.A.R, though). If you want a third-person shooter with "zombies?" Go and play Resident Evil 4. Either way, you'll have a lot more fun than you would with this game.
Addendum 04/09/15:
I guess I need to clarify something, since multiple people over the last few months have brought it up. I didn't say F.E.A.R. was scary. I said it was a better horror-themed shooter. I said this for two reasons.
1) It's a better horror-themed shooter not because it's scary, but because the atmosphere is more unsettling. Granted, that's a subjective assessment, but see if you can understand where I'm coming from. Most of The Evil Within depends on walls splattered with offal, grates that shoot fire, and gigantic swimming pools of blood to try and unnerve the player; F.E.A.R. depends on dark, enclosed spaces, and an unbeatable and unknowable evil behind potentially every corner. The Evil Within had a very similar character and powerset in its main villain compared to F.E.A.R.'s Alma, but Alma was used more effectively and made her presence more well-known (even if she was a rather tired example of the "black-haired evil little girl" popularized most recently by movies like The Ring and The Grudge). Many times I wondered when I would next see Alma and dreaded it; my only emotion in seeing Ruvik was exasparation that I'd have to suffer through another chase sequence. The Evil Within spent a large quantity of time (not most of the time, but a significant portion) in brightly lit, sunny, outdoor areas where enemies were plainly visible well ahead of time; F.E.A.R. is set mostly in an office building, so even when the lights are on enemies can be hidden behind office furniture, doors, etc., and your only clue to their existence is radio chatter.
2) It's a better horror-themed shooter because it's a BETTER SHOOTER. Strip out all of the supposed horror elements, regardless of whether you find them scary or not, and what you're left with is, almost objectively, a better shooter in F.E.A.R. than in The Evil Within. Better (and more entertaining) weapon variety, better enemy reaction to being damaged, better enemy A.I., better gunplay, a better melee system, a better stealth system despite not even HAVING a stealth system...granted, all of that is subjective, but how many of you are going to honestly say that sans the supposed horror The Evil Within makes a better shooter than F.E.A.R. sans its supposed horror?
Everyone's free to disagree with my points. We all have different opinions and it's more than likely that I've made misguided or even outright incorrect statements somewhere. I don't mind being called out on those. But it's important to note that nowhere in the review did I call F.E.A.R. scary. While I was brought to the edge of my seat more often in F.E.A.R. than I was in The Evil Within, I didn't once say it was scary. I never even once used the word "scary" in the review. Not once. I said it was a better horror shooter.

Okay so, The Evil Within.
Where to begin?  Well it should be mentioned that I am a huge Resident Evil 4 fan.  Shinji mikami is the man, and that game still rates as one of my favorite survival/horror games of all time even though I played it back in 2005 on the PS2.  Mikami returns gloriously to the scene in 2014 with The Evil Within, and let me just say this game is beyond my expectations!
The first 45 minutes or so are very slow and somewhat scare free, but please do not stop there my fellow gamers, for the best is yet to come!  After this introduction to the game, the action and frights accelerate to a wild degree, throwing you from one tense and horrific situation to the next.  You hardly get a moment to breathe, but I mean that in the best of ways.
This is truly a SURVIVAL horror game.  Expect measly amounts of ammo, no regenerating health, the stamina bar of a severe asthmatic, and a limited inventory.  "Oh then I'll just stock up on ammo" you say... WRONG! The Evil Within lets you feel like you're just about well supplied then BAM it throws something at you that makes you panic and all that precious ammo is gone just like that.
For anyone who loved RE4 like me, this is a dream come true.  Mikami's newest game is the proper Resident Evil game I've been waiting for, albeit with a different name.  I Only have 2 hours of playtime at time of this writing but I can't wait to jump back into this game and have the living Sh*t scared out of me again!

Absolutely great. Games like this really just need to be scary. The gameplay is ok and there are some notable criticisms that I think are fair. At the end of the day, I don't care about any of that because this game scared me witless. Gameplay is highly reminiscent of Resident Evil 4, although the movement controls are a bit more smooth and make the game somewhat more dynamic adn fast paced. Lots of variety - the game runs you through a large number of fairly distinct scenarios and environments, several of which only tangentially involve combat. The developers do revisit some ideas a few times, but most of them don't actually wear out their welcome.
The real draw are the scares, environment, ambience, etc. Scary is subjective, but I have a hard time believing most people won't feel the intensity on this one. The creature designs are all abominations that frequently evoke visceral unease. On top of that, many of the sections of the game involve pressure-cooker scenarios based around trying to accomplish some objective while the game's parade of horrors attempt to take you down. In short, much of the game absolutely forbids you from moving at your own pace, and I find it works pretty well. Some of the sections are intense enough that I just had to put down the controller after having had enough psychological strain.
You can read some of the relevant criticisms in other reviews. For me, this one is worth it just because it's frightening and unpleasant. If you're like me, that's all you'll need.

This game. This game before you right now. It is not worth money. Any amount. It is not worth any asking price at its current state. This is a horrible slapdash PC port of an iOS/Android game that took nearly a year to gestate, but it still came out completely malformed. The graphics aren't horrible, but a stickler for PC gaming standards would swear this off the moment they see the game in action, because it looks extremely old, like by Playstation 2 and original Xbox standards, but I'd be able to live with it. However, the problem with this game is the sheer lack of effort and Quality Control that went into the port. For the best gameplay experience, you would need to be willing to switch controls between the keyboard+mouse and an Xbox 360 controller on the fly, there's just so much wrong with this game's controls that it's hard to explain in a short amount of time.
The experience of playing with a keyboard and mouse makes me feel physically ill from the amount of visual whiplash involved in the simple act of turning when you walk. It's like the mouselook is locked at 45 degree angles, regardless of mouse sensitivity options, your view speed will be extremely sluggish and stopping your view anywhere between the preset angles will cause your view to snap to the nearest one. Strangely enough the xbox 360 controller does not have this problem, so I would suggest that for walking around and looking at things and maybe shooting. I say MAYBE shooting because you use the right trigger to shoot here and it's extremely unresponsive as well, in addition to the fact that guns, when fired, appear to snap your field of view back and forth to try and loosely simulate recoil. You cannot jump, and I cannot find a button on the controller that allows you to sprint or run. In hacking, the controller is overly-sensitive and uses a method for node capture that is liable to send your view of the hacking puzzle careening in whatever vague directions you were selecting with the left analog stick. You can browse menus using the controller mostly with ease EXCEPT, in order to scroll through the list of quests, you need to use the mousewheel, so in short, the best gameplay experience as far as controls is swapping between a controller and keyboard+mouse on the fly.
Stealth afficianados will notice that the only bits of stealth left in this are line of sight, silent takedowns, and cloaking. Enemies will not react to hearing you, only to seeing you, and it doesn't seem to matter anymore to care about where you take out an enemy, as their bodies dissolve into gold triangles as soon as you take them down, lethal or not. The levels are very short, shorter infact than Deus Ex: Invisible War's. There's also no shops, you carry a replicator in your pause menu now that makes you whatever item you want for an in-game currency fee (this was were microtransactions were in the iOS/Android releases). You can even buy praxis kits. The story, while it might have been well-written and thought out, is delivered very poorly with deadpan and comedically bad voice acting across the board and occasionally way too long dialogue that overstays its welcome long before it's finished.
On the positive side, it does look and feel like Deus Ex: Human Revolution, if it were to be put under by a mad doctor, had random guts taken out, and then lobotomized. The saddest thing about this game is really all the wasted potential. Square-Enix could have made this natively for PCs or Consoles rather than jumping headlong to the current Japanese game industry standard of 'everything is better mobile'. This game is proof positive that that is not the case, or at least that what works for one system does not work for another. The port job in and of itself, disregarding the original iOS release, is terrible and on the verge of unplayable to anyone besides the most patient or tolerant of gamers, and the controls all on their own should relegate this title to discussions where you would mention Superman 64 and E.T. for the Atari 2600 in the same breath.
At least, all this is the case unless they somehow pull the best patch ever out and fix everything, which I hope they do, because I really want to enjoy this game, but you know they won't. This PC Port is a sad case of wasted potential, and now this is technically the earliest entry in series canon, meaning Deus Ex, as of now, begins with The Fall, and ends with Invisible War. It's like a delicious gooey center that is Human Revolution and the Original game, sandwiched in rancid feces, and we certainly didn't ask for this.
***Edit: After recording more footage for the game and getting excessively frustrated with playing the game, I looked for solutions on the mouselook issue since writing this review. Lo and behold, there is an almost-fix, turn on the vsync. I didn't have vsync on at all because I was trying to record footage and I found that usually when I use vsync during recording, it usually screws with a game's performance or the recording, but apparently without vsync on, the keyboard and mouse controls do not work properly at all.
Using this trick made the game far more enjoyable, to the point that I'm actually kinda getting into the story (now that it's finally also going somewhere), but that doesn't excuse the fact that I dunno what kind of failures of programmers or QA a development team would need to have to have the stsatus of the vsync, a GRAPHICAL option, effect the CONTROLS of the whole game, thus adversely effecting the gameplay. I could do a better job than whoever Squeenix or Eidos-Montreal or N-Fusion hired for this game, and I have no programming knowledge whatsoever outside of altering .ini files.***

I decided to actually play through the entire game before just writing a review, trying to find anything that saves this game, but there really isn't anything that does. This game is not worth it any way you slice it. But, I'll try to judge it off it's merits.
First off: The story is the strongest part of this game, but it is still weak compared to other deus ex games. Maybe there was something I missed, but the story to my knowledge just didn't feel like a true deus ex game. The worst part is, it ends in a cliff hanger until they release more DLC (which, if it isn't free DLC, it isn't worth it: see below)
Second off:  The game isn't worth the asking price (especially if they're going to make you pay for the rest of the story). I played the game through, smooth operator style completing side quests (but I think I missed a hidden one) and it took me 7 hours to do. Given the (current) price of $9.99, that's about $1.42 per hour of gameplay. Deus Ex: Human Revolution and the Missing Link DLC, plays for about 40 hours with so many ways to go through it, that you'll want to do it again and again. I've played DX:HR 2 and a half times (non-steam), then bought the director's cut and played it all again. That's roughly 140 hours. At the current price of DX:HR director's cut (which includes the DLC) of $19.99, that's about $0.14/hour of gameplay. Even at its full release price of $59.99 and the DLC's full release price of $14.99, it is still worth about $0.50/hour of gameplay. So, even if you paid FULL PRICE for human revolution, you're still getting a better deal.
Third off: There is no incentive to play the game over and over again. With a the rest of the story missing, and no multiple saves, and a game world which is almost painful to go through (loading screen mania and walking simulator)
The nail in the coffin: The graphics and bugs. I understand this is a port from mobile devices. But come on guys, did this not go through Q/A? Did this game just get released in beta or what? If this was 1994, I would have rated this game a 10/10 game of the year. But it's not. It's 2014. And 20 years later, we expect better. What am I talking about? Here's a list of all the issues I've found so far that shouldn't be here (this is PC after all):
Constant loading screens
No multiple saves
Horribly low detailed textures
Incredibly low polygon models
No real graphical settings
Terrible animations (lip movement was the worst. I'd rather have their mouth not move compared to this)
Awful inventory management
Emersion breaking ability to just buy everything anywhere you are
AI is bad in general. They don't really bother looking for you. They'd rather hide.
Awful shooting post processing effect
Absolutely awful voice acting (I can't even tell if it's synthetic or people purposely sounded robotic)
And bugs:
Some repeat textures don't line up correctly
Anti-aliasing breaks models because they're so low polygon
Pathing characters will walk through you
Clipping through walls
AI sometimes forgets to react to things
So, unless you're a die hard Deus Ex fan who just wants every single bit of lore, I say stay away or keep your expectations low.

It's fun. Unbalanced, but fun. Actually, taking Balance out of the equation is probably what makes it fun. How many RTS games do you know where you only get three factions and there's not really much that sets them apart? The factions in this game have completely different playstyles, advantages, and disadvantages. Knights have good cavalry, but electricity and flyers can make their lives hell. Anything that isn't elven has access to siege equipment, with Dark Dwarves getting the cool stuff. You can be snake-people, plague-bearing abominations with hydras, Conan The Barbarians, minotaurs, Undead Humans, Knights, Humans-that-aren't-knights-or-barbarians (they get mages but are kind of boring), fey-cretins, grossly misinterpreted orcs (it says those units are kobolds and gnolls, but they do not look like it), and daemons for maximum edge in case DarkSpiderElves wasn't edgy enough.
Your hero unit can be of a race separate from the Faction you play as, and you can make Dumb things like a daemonic paladin, or a fey Dragonslayer, or you can play an archetype straight. It progresses like an RPG character, slowly growing in power as it wins fights. Advancement is simple enough to be done mid-battle, and if you're a trickster, you can use the lairs on maps that spawn NPCs that are hostile to everyone at regular intervals to farm EXP for you or your troops, or destroy them to release a Very Powerful Unit close to an enemy base.
The graphics are two dimensional, polished-up versions of the original game's sprites. So, they're dated. Not to the point that you should be unable to tell what you're looking at (in most cases), but enough to have that constant air of cheesiness about it. But the cheese is good! Most of the time, anyway.
The campaign is more RPG than RTS. You're sailing on a ship when a Portal To Hell opens up on some island, and it turns out something is trying to escape the portal in order to go wreak havoc upon The World, and for some reason it's your job to stop it. Bland stuff, nothing really groundbreaking in terms of plot, but it's fun for what it is. Just watch out for when the campaign randomly decides to throw a lvl 75 hero at you when you're barely lvl 20.
It's important to switch on Compatability mode on any computer that isn't a complete dinosaur, and maybe downgrade the version a bit to the last official release if you aren't digging the setup that got released here that is riddled with text popups about how your buildings are being converted that'll make you wonder if a thirteen-year-old modded this for the re-release. Easy enough fix with the proper files.

No lizard women or daemon women, no zamby women, no plaguemonster women, no minot- wait not having minotauresses kinda makes sense. Vee's Rating: It's as good as any generic fantasy is going to be, but with knight-druidesses and their harems of dryad-chicks and crazy fiery salamanders and succubi. Good cartoon, dumb fun, would watch more of.

This game has a very cool premise and some interesting ideas. I liked the writing style, but it doesn't really have anything like a story, so gameplay is the primary concern.
The big problem of Last Federation is that fighting everything is the fastest way to achieve pretty much any goal. And fighting, while fun at first, quickly gets very stale. There is no tactical depth to it - some cool ideas are there, but you will quickly figure out how to beat a battle (if it is even challenging) and then you need to do exactly the same thing every time this battle happens.
E.g. at some point you will have several pirate bases up, let's say 6. That means 6 absolutely identical combat missions to take them all out - and not doing it is simply the wrong move if you want to win the game (they give a bunch of everything you want).
If you don't put combat difficulty on maximum, fighting will be effortless and even more boring. If you do, you will just sometimes be bursted down and the already tedious battles will take ages.
If you don't fight, you will simply pick a "dispatch" (effect over time) and stare at the screen while the simulation runs. While the effort put into making a simulation with so many variables is admirable, all of that stuff becomes pretty irrelevant when, for example, one race randomly conquers another before you can react at all.
I cannot recommend a game that bored me after 13 hours that costs 12.6$ even here in Ukraine.

When you first try playing it, your initial reaction might be that the game is smarter than the player. At the end of the day though, the game is actually pretty straightforward, it's just very unique:
You are playing a roguelite game whose setting could be roughly understood as a 4X game. Imagine a game like stellaris or civilization being run automatically in the background while you play your roguelite spaceship game on top of it. The two bubbles mostly operate distinctly, you can only slightly effect the simulation that's running on the planets in the background.
Given this, the game has a bit of a learning curve just because it is not a goal that any other game I know of has in common. That said, after you get a feel for it, the game is pretty straightforward. The game is in some ways a bit spreadsheety, so part of what's overwhelming about picking it up is learning what numbers you should care about and how to make money in the first few years ("property development" and build buildings, focus on the "attitude" ones that let you sway how the races feel about each other).
Now, with that massive preface out of the way, the bottom line: The game's fun after you figure it out, and it isn't that hard. There are two difficulty settings, "combat" and "strategy", I played on Normal / Normal and won my second game without the dlc active. It honestly was pretty straightforward even with some flailing to figure it out towards the start, I beat most ship encounters without paying much attention to the power distribution mechanic (either max guns or some extra in engines), though it does work pretty well and I imagine would be very important on the higher combat difficulties.
I think a fair amount of the difficulty in the game stems from the number of possible victory conditions. Going for a perfect 8 man federation is going to be much more challenging than exterminating the solar system alongside one power species (though both are probably among the harder choices, for different reasons). I've only played two rounds and won by doing what I feel is probably the easiest choice:♥♥♥♥♥♥off one of the two warmonger races and unite the galaxy destroying them, then crush the remaining evil hive race for refusing to assimilate. As far as the game is concerned this victory is no different from working to convince them both to join the federation, but it would've been much harder and I would have needed to play the game completely differently. (There are specific achievements for various victory conditions and alliances that can occur over the course of gameplay, for what it's worth).
For this reason, though I recommend the game and think it's a great example of a unique idea executed well, it definitely requires a certain mindset to play it. Only pick this game up if you're okay with an open-ended win condition. The difficulty (at least on Normal, this probably changes at the higher difficulties) means you will probably win somehow or another. It's more about the story of how you tried to get an alliance working before it fell apart due to a war, so you formed a different alliance instead to force a peace, or something akin to that. Or the alliance that formed without your planning and started to take over the galaxy before you could react. You have a plan and things go wrong and in the end you either have a galaxy under your control (in other races names) or not under your control (in other races names), the end is basically the same either way (because as I said, the background setting of the game is basically a game of Civilization or any other 4X... In the end someone gets one of the victory conditions whetherit's diplomacy or conquest). At the end of the game you're still just one person in a spaceship and your species is dead, so even though you "win" in the end, it's really the story of those other races and what happened to them.
I haven't played the DLC yet but so far I recommend the vanilla game for a fun game about being "the man behind the curtain" and pushing much more powerful empires around with careful nudges. If you want a game about fighting or winning wars, this is not the game for you. This is very much so a game about
wars. Maybe through orbital bombing support killing 2 billion people over the course of 20 months while someone else does the real fighting, but that's about as extreme as it gets.

Yikes.
Bash me for the little time I've put in the game, but I believe my points still stand regardless.
Pros:
- Nice variety of characters (5) with different play styles
- Loot system to unlock new stuff is cool
- In-game lobby instead of a menu is a nice touch
- The idea of fighting rats with swords is interesting
- Multiplayer is always nice, and works pretty well
(inhales)
Cons (in no particular order):
- Some areas are too dark, while other areas have way too bright ambient light
- Almost exact copy of the L4D formula (complete with copied objectives, items and enemy types)
- Some players are diffucult to distinguish from the rats
- Each character has a different play style, but can only be played by one player at a time
- Poorly optimized (runs far worse than Fallout 4, Hitman, Battlefront)
- Even on high, visuals look bad and objects look washed out and disconnected
- Generic and uninspired materials and textures
- Odd weapon placement on screen
- Some weapon designs make no sense at all (Ex: a screw going into the barrel of a gun?)
- Hitting enemies with melee weapons feels disconnected and unsatisfying
- Special rats that are definitely not clones of L4D special infected have very similar silhouettes and come out of nowhere
- Tank rats that have 6x the damage they probably should have
- Rats constantly swarm you from everywhere, without any clear indication of where they will come from
- Cringey "banter" between player characters that never ends
- Characters choose to talk to each other instead of saying important things like "Health potion" or "Help I'm dying"
- Characters are more like classes, as they have little character beyond their generic archetypes
- Level design is atrocious in areas, with no realistic structural integrity of buildings and no interesting level design (especially the library. The first level was okay though)
- Lighting is flat and adds nothing to the scenes
- Some areas just straight up make no sense and should never have been made
- (when using sword and shield) have to completely release mouse button and wait for current anim to finish before charging up for a big swing, meaning you can't spam sword slashes and then start holding down LMB to do a charge attack because it won't register the mouse being held down while you are still swinging
- You place EXPLOSIVE barrels by left clicking, which also happens to be the button you use to THROW them. You can guess what happens in frantic situations.
I could go on longer, but I think you get the idea.
The game takes L4D2, removes all the good game design, makes it about rats and swords, and ♥♥♥♥♥ out a crappy L4D2 clone.
I'm gonna redownload it and give it another shot, and if my opinions change I'll update the review.
I doubt they will though.

The game is a complete mess and let me explain everything wrong with it. The clowns move way too slow so even when the clown is ready to kill you, you can still equip the handgun, aim with the clunky controls and kill him before he even get's close to you.
The key that opens the door spawns in a random location and is really hard to see. But there's not many places to look so you will find it eventually.
The game is so short, you can finish it in less than a minute, I'm dead serious.
The game is also really buggy. It didn't load on maxed settings and I had to lower the settings and run it window mode and the developer is going around telling people that they're computer can't run the game.
This game has a really cool idea, but the game is a mess and is not worth your time. Just skip this title
I give Clown House a 1/10

Clown House is a short horror game about a person visiting a house full of deranged, knife wielding clowns, who may or may not kill you, depending on their mood. You can shoot them with a pistol if they plan to attack you.
When I say short, you can finish the game in a minute. The point of the game is to find a key to escape the clown house, which is not really hard to find. It is randomly place in the house but the area is so small it doesn’t even matter. Besides from a few jump scares, there’s really nothing to the game. There’s also no end to it. Once you’ve escaped, it loops around to the part where you have to find the key again. It’s like we’re in purgatory or something.
It is free and if you’re bored, you should check it out. Otherwise, there are plenty of other free games worth your time.
On a side note, it’s probably not scary to the average person but I’m deathly afraid of clowns so this game shook me up…just a little bit though.

I am a huge fan of Star Trek but thought I would write a updated review. First off the stories of "buy to win is bull", why because I am playing free to play on hardest setting and so far only two missions gave me some trouble, and not because I couldn't buy my way to victory but because I didn't plan. The game gives you plenty of options from crafting to sending your virtual crew on missions to earn the things you need to buy better gear and ship weapons. the stock items you can buy are not as good as the items you can craft yourself if you took the time to send crew on missions or build with the material you can find on every mission you just have to find them yourself, so most negative reviews are honestly lazy people that want mainstream fun for free, yet don't want a company to make any sort of money or matain servers that are pretty good at staying online. Most bought ships for real money are upgraded version of the standard ships you get for free as you level up, or are for fans like me who may want the Deep Space Nine pack to re live the good old days.
There are 3 factions, Klingon, Romulan and the Federation to play as with story arcs that are pretty well written, and are splint into episodes of a season. It does have  a few flaws when it comes to the standard shoot it out, go to point 1 and 2 sometimes, but it does have you research or solve puzzles, or follow a story well. Voice acting is hit or miss, some mission have alot of voice over, some have you reading dialog but many have good cutscene transition, and the company has come a long way at re vamping locations, doing a entire new crafting system, adding new story content to tie in the main epidoes, and providing a world that is what we expect from Star Trek.
I had a few issues, I always find the voices of NPC's that talk to you very soft, even when I turned down the music and world volume, and I think it may have to do with compression of the audio files but I read the dialog so most of the time it's not a big deal and doesn't happen everywhere. The graphics are ageing sadly but are on par with other MMOs. PVP is ok, and ties in the story of the univerise and it's lore and it does have realtime even. Honestly this hate on buy to win isn't true, mostly you have to learn the game, learn that your sheilds that may may stop klingon weapons, won't work on the next seasons enemies, that your bride officers should have sheild buffs and hull repair, and that you learn how to play.
Yes they need to make money and sometimes I feel hurt being a star trek fan not being able to equip something, but what do you want, they still release new story content, they still matain the servers, it's a trade off, but if you take the time to learn the game, you will find your not road blocked. Take it from someone who only bought the DS9 set because I love the show, that I played most of the game without any ship upgrade. I have since moved onto the PS4 Star Trek Online, but still think the PC version is solid, and offers something to those that wish to live the Star Trek World.

If I could have more money, I'd give it all to Dennaton.
10/10.
The best goddamn game I've ever played.
Story: Dennaton singlehandedly crafted the perfect ending to the duology of the Hotline Miami universe. While people might see it as a cheap ending, it was, in fact, the only one that would do the game justice, aiding the lore into proving what kind of world it is in the HLM universe. The fact that you play as different characters who intertwine with each other and "solidify" the plot from the past without being a flashback of some sort (Jake and Beard) makes the story even stronger.
Music: The perfect mix of Synthwave, Retrowave and Cyberpunk (to an extent). The music artists featured within both Hotline Miami games are amazing ones, to say the least. Mega Drive and Perturbator especially shine in their other work as much as they do in this game with their multiple head-bobbing heart-pumping albums. The devs made a great choice with the music.
Difficulty: Dennaton knew how hard to make this game and by god were they accurate. It gives time for new players to learn the basics and veterans to get into it and the feel of the game, and then it just spikes in difficulty. Not too high of a spike, but high enough to be really challenging when it needs/wants to be. The hard mode just adds onto it and the feeling of accomplishment when you finish the game, Hard Mode or not, is absolutely amazing.
Level design: Long hallways. That's my only complaint. Getting shot and killed off-screen is infuriating, but neccessary in order to make the game even harder than it is without it. It's to make sure the player knows that they're rarely ever safe from enemies until they kill every single last one. Being alert helps you a lot in this game. Trust me, the only way youre getting through Dead Ahead is being alert and strategizing.
Level Editor: The editor is... fun to use, gut-wrenchingly painful to create something actually good such as a campaign. While you can honestly do anything you want with the right tools, it is very much not simplistic and hard to master everything about it. Kinda like the game.
Graphics: Pixel art done right. Even the small things are drawn extremely well. I don't have much else to say about it, so yeah.
Overall: 10/10.

I never went in to this game thinking it would be scary, so I was never let down by that. Having said that, the game is amazing. Graphically, it's beautiful, and the music is quite good. Gameplay is great, and a lot like a souped up RE4, but that's not a bad thing, at least to me. Another complaint I hear is that the story isn't very good, but man oh man, the story is fantastic! It's explained through the game, and by use of collectables found through-out the game. Most of it is explained, except for the things which will be covered in the DLC, but you have to pay attention to all the dialogue if you want to know what's going on. Great control, great music, great graphics, and one of the few games on Steam that I've felt a desire to complete wholly. I would recommend this game to anyone who likes survival horror, RPG style stories, and the RE series. Runner up to my game of the year, 2014.
Edit: The Assignment DLC. Fantastic. I loved how the main focus was stealth, and sneakiness. It really gave the DLC a creepier feel to it. Some of those shadow puzzles were difficult for me as my eyes are awful, but I got past them with time. I didn't have high hopes for this as I wasn't too keen on Kidman, but it was a cool experience to play as her. The Kurayami mode was incredibly frustrating for me, as I stated before my eyes are awful as it is. I died so much on this, but that was to be expected. It was a great challenge, and though I didn't really enjoy Kurayami mode, it was different, and I can appreciate that. Took me about 10 hours to complete all the achievements, and I had a fun time for the most part. I really enjoyed seeing things that were happening at the same time the main game was happening, and also where certain areas of the world came from as they were established as not from the main characters minds. It was definitely worth the time, and, in my opinion, was a fantastic DLC.
Edit: The Consequence DLC. Quite great, though not as good as the first one, imo. The main focus was still stealth, but there were some gun parts thrown in, and I can see why. No where near as many puzzles, though the little collectable hints were a little tricky to find at times. Kurayami mode was even more aggravating this time, but I didn't die nearly as many times as I did on it in the first DLC. Took me about eight hours this time to finish the achievements, but it was pretty fun. There were some great achievements this time too. Well worth getting.
Edit: The Executioner DLC: By far it's the worst yet. It offers a little story, but is basically a boss rush mode that you end up having to grind for coins to upgrade your weapons, and skills. The maps are boring, and unimaginative, and the waves of mobs are boring as well. You'd think playing as the Keeper would be great, but instead it's... yep boring. It takes less than an hour to get through once, a few new things open, about the same time to get through it again. After that... what's the point? Nothing changes, it remains the same, and it's not fun at all. I expected more out of the final DLC, but it's a disappointment, and instead. What a waste.

Hoo boy, this game. Where do I begin? I'm a very big fan of the Deus Ex franchise (as my name no doubt signals), so I was initially very excited when Eidos first teased this game. Unfortunately, the reveal crushed my dreams by unveiling it as a mobile-exclusive title. Ech. Understandably, I was very excited when I heard that the game was being ported to PC and being tweaked to fit a "PC experience." The excitement stopped about five minutes after booting the game. Let's go into detail, shall we?
Pros
+They got the voice actor for Bob Page back again. I love that evil sunnuva♥♥♥♥♥.
Cons
-The game looks absolutely terrible. I know this was originally a mobile game, but the term "PC experience" kinda implies that you're going to upgrade the game from looking like a PS2 game. I'm pretty sure JC Denton's viewmodel hands had more polys than Mr. Saxon's cube fingers. The Human Revolution asthetic helps a bit, though.
-Speaking of which, the animations look like they're out of an N64 game. The characters move jerkily, and their facial animations consist of flapping their lips and half-blinking. Sure, they did the same thing in DE1, but there it didn't look nearly as creepy there because the characters weren't exactly high-detail.
-The gameplay is terrible compared to the other games in the series. You thought Invisible War was dumbed down? IW feels like DE1 compared to this abortion. There is no such thing as running out of ammo, because you can always bring up the pause menu and buy some more. The devs also don't trust you with the right to jump, and will decide when it's appropriate to do so. The tutorial goes on for a good half an hour and forces you to participate, unlike the other games where it's optional.
-The voice acting. Dear god, the voice acting. Deus Ex isn't exactly known for its high-calibur voice actors, but at least in the previous titles the actors put some semblance of effort into their performances. All of the characters in this, however, seem to be wooden and void of any emotion. Ben Saxon, the protagonist, has a voice which managed to get on my nerves almost immediately. The tutorial narrator only speaks in monotone, and drones on for extended periods without a way to shut her up. The enemy NPCs in Panama were so bad that I stopped playing.
-The port job is terrible. Aside from the aformentioned graphical vomit, things such as a field of view slider and rebinding keys are absent. Prefer to have your shoot key bound to RMB because you're a lefty? Too bad! Have a non-QWERTY keyboard? Well, have fun playing the game piano-style!
In closing, it seems like Deus Ex has a "good game, bad game" pattern going on. DE1 was good, IW was bad (comparatively). HR was good, this is an abomination. Hey, at least the next game will be good!

So i already made a review earlier about this game but now that i have nearly 500 hours in the game its time for a better review.
So first of all this game is in BETA verion but that just means that its not a "finished" product. Which means that the Developers are constantly updateing the game with new weapons, maps and cars etc. So thats why its a free to play game in Beta.
Recently it reached more than 7 MILLION players. Thats a  huge number. So you might be thinking "yeah 7 million but mixed reviews!". Yes the game has sadly mixed reviews on steam but thats beacuse the game is a bit grindy. That means that you dont get unlocked every weapon instantly. You need to play the game in order to get better at it and get better stuff. Now please understand that the develpoers cant just give to every new player the best weapons in the game, because it would be to unbalanced. They even have a Tier 0,1,2 systeam which means if you are a new player you are Tier 0 and you play against Tier 0 players so you cant play against the best players. Theen when you gte better you get Tier 1 same thing as in Tier 0 and than Tier 2.
The graphics are really good even if you have a low performace Laptop/PC. Dont expect the graphics of GTA 5 but really good for a free game.
An other thing is that there are 3 factions. The German, US and Soviet factions. A lot of people say that the fations are unbalanced. Which is totally false. If those players would play a bit more with the game, they would realise that the game and the factions are really balanced. ALL the factions have the same number of LMGs, SMGs, Bolt-Action rifles etc. Even the vehicles. Now in the vehicles are a bit of differences in the game. For example the Soviet car does not have a built in LMG but its faster than the US and German Car. So its balanced by the speed. I hope you get my point.
There are 6 types of characters you can play.
-Infantry man (starter character)
-Tanker
-Pilot
-Paratrooper
-Recon (Sniper)
-Generals
The Generals are important for the RTS ( Real Time Strategy) part. Where the really War is being fought. Players there send Pilots infantry mans in to cities to win. Where on the other part there are the normal games which are made by the devs. Its a bit conplicated but you will understandit with time.
Now just to get this out of the way NO its not a pay to win game. Back in the game it was a bit im not gonna lie, but now you can buy EVERYTHING AND I MEAN EVERYTHING with in game credits. There is a bonus called Veteran Membership which costs real life money but thats to help out the developers andd you get a lot of benefits. like 50% more credits than normal players. So its really worth  it andd if you dont mind giving out more for this, go for it. I personaly always buy this option just beacuse its really helpful and worth it.
Now there is two more thing to say. One is that this game has the best anti cheater system in the  FREE to PLAY game history. If you try to cheat, hack it may work for like 5 minutes for you. But you will get almost instantly banned. I only had one experienc with a hacker and after the game that was 10 minutes long he got banned. You will never see a cheeater not like by other free to play games. And this just makes theee game so enjoyable.
The other last thing is that the community in this game is awesome. the twitchers always help othe players. The Devs are always reading the comments, suggetions on the forums. They even do weekly livestream where they show the new stuffs and do QnAs.

From the series I have only played Warlords Battlecry III, but it is a big favorite of mine nevertheless.
As you probably know, Warlords Battlecry III is a Real Time Strategy (RTS) game, just like the Age Of ___ games or Starcraft, Warcraft. What makes it unique is its large amount of races to play with - 16 to be exact - from Elves to Dwarves, Minotaurs, Daemons, different reptiles, etc.
There is a conversion mechanism for buildings - some units can perform a
action which will turn nearby buildings to the player's side. This is how the resources (Gold, Crystal, Metal and Stone) are handled - you have to convert the mines which will produce for you.
A neat feature in Warlords Battlecry III is that the player has their own hero, a superunit who stays with the player between battles and gains experience to level up. There is a huge list of classes to pick for the Hero, such as Merchant, Dragonslayer, Pyromancer, etc.
Heroes can learn spells in many different spell schools - Alchemy, Chaos, Divination, Nature, Poison, Necromancy, and of course the basic ones like Fire or Ice. Additionally, Heroes have an Equipment and Inventory system - with Set items to collect too.
Warlords Battlecry III offers a Campaign Mode to take on with a unique storyline.
The player can take their hero to independent battles in Skirmish Mode and play on either randomly generated or manual maps with up to 5 AIs.
Lastly, there is an Editor in which the player can assemble their own maps.
RTS + RPG, perfectly falls in a good old game category. Definitely recommended.

Where do I even begin with this game. First off ive been playing this game for about 7 years now and every playthrough ive had of it was exellent. There is alot of variety when it comes to builds. There is the obvious Light/Dark or Grey option for the game but there is also Force user builds, Ranged builds, Pure combat focused guardian, etc. I find the combat to be enjoyable (In my opinion) since its tactical and you can really plan attacks and things of that sort. Take DA:0 for example. Its pretty much the same system. You can start with 3 beginning classes: Guardian (Combat focused), Sentinel (Better skill progression), and Consular (Force powers). You then later in the game get different set of prestige classes depending on your allignment. Now, lets get to the writing of the game. This game has one of the best stories I have ever seen. You'll see once you play it for yourself. The reason I prefer this game slightly over the first is just because I prefer the darker, philosophical, grey aspects of the atmosphere and story a bit better (Kotor 1 is also one of my favorite games). Anyways, this game presents the idea that Dark is not necessarily evil and Light isnt nessesary good and you really get to see the Flaws of both sides. For example, you play as the Jedi Exile, who was exiled from the Jedi order for rusing to war to protect innocents. The Jedi were lazy and waited to "evaluate the threat". The dialouge and voice acting in this game is absolutely fantastic (Especially Kreia). For this game, you dont even need to be a fan of Star Wars. A non Star Wars fan would look at this game and just play an RPG. However a Star Wars fan would look at this and play an amazing Star Wars RPG. The reason for this is because the game is set in an era wayyy before the Movies. One flaw however, would be the cut content presented this game. Obsidian (The developers) were rushed to release this game by lucasarts, resulting in them needing to cut out content for the game. Luckily, a group of community modders managed to get into the games files and restore alot of the content that was cut. You can find the mod on the steam workshop. Anyways, hurry up and buy the game! You wont be dissapointed.

Mount and Blade is one of those games that's seemingly been around forever, and practically leaks PC all over the place. It's a very "PC" game, with unique odd-to-navigate menues, tons of dialogue, an esoteric combat system, a plethora of mods, and a very open sandbox. You'll be reading a ton of dialogue to initially understand things, and then clicking through it because it's repetitive and doesn't say much of anything important. You're going to want to have a quick-start guide handy, otherwise you just might accidentally gimp yourself.
Besides all that, Mount & Blade is a great game, as long as you aren't one of those people to get bothered by goofy graphics or lack of goals. You get to carve your own story out in this game, in almost any way you choose. Become a lord of a kingdom, or a travelling mercenary bandit, or even found your own kingdom. It's all up to you. The combat feels initially clunky but is surprisingly deep. The game is a nonstop grind, and starting a new character is a royal pain. You do the same thing over and over and over again in order to make it anywhere... but once you've made it, god damn, this game is fun.
Again, I feel like having some kind of quick-start guide handy will make your initial few hours a lot easier and way more fun. There are some systems in the game that are difficult to understand, but once you have the hang of things... strap in. You're not going anywhere for awhile.

Pirates, Vikings and Knights II is a game with amazing potential. Currently, though incomplete, it can still be played and enjoyed as a solid version of the full game, albeit with limited classes.  However, right now the classes are: Berserker, Huscarl and Gestir on Vikings; Heavy Knight, Archer and Man-at-Arms on Knights; and Skirmisher, Captain and Sharpshooter on Pirates.  So they do have at least 3 per team, and it is more varied than previous versions.  One downside has been the long wait for each new class, but the vast majority of players are grateful for what they get, and rightfully so because it has always been a free mod.  The gameplay was always solid, so for it's time it deserves a lot of credit.  It's unfortunate that it hasn't been greenlighted on Steam.  I'll need to look into that.
I recommend PVKII if you're familiar with games like Oblivion/Skyrim, Chivalry, or any Half-Life 2 games in particular.  Beyond that, any FPS player out there is perfect, as the main perspective is first-person.  The action is very fast paced and accuracy and timing oriented.  There's plenty of interesting custom maps on those servers as well when the core maps become familiar, though the core maps tend to be higher quality than custom.  It's a game to have fun in and adapt to the physics and movement limitations.  You can dodge arrows and feint in battle to dodge and counter their attack.  You can throw a keg and shoot it with your pistol as a Skirmisher and have it explode immediately. (This is dangerous though, you're likely to hit it closer and that may be suicidal. But it's hilarious.)  Every class has it's own style and you can figure out how to best utilize their advantages while adjusting for their disadvantages.  I suggest embracing their disadvantages -- for example, as a Heavy Knight, it's easier to let them come to you.  When you aren't constantly moving while they're moving, they won't see your relative speed, so when you do move to dodge their attack they likely won't be able to adjust in time.  A charged attack from a Heavy Knight does the most damage when used accurately.  Heavy Knights deserve credit because they have the hardest time getting food to restore health, as they run the slowest by far of any class in the game, due to balancing their Attack with Health/Armor and Attack Speed/Movement Speed.
Skirmishers can also die in two hits from a Heavy Knight's Great Sword, or three hits from a Two-handed Axe, and all depending on how Charged and accurate the attack was.  Skirmishers, however, run the fastest. Due to the WASD movement you can move in and out to attack, dodge, or feint (have them swing, you dodge, then counter). A Skirmisher is able to move backwards faster than most classes run forwards.  Thus, if you can time it, you can theoretically avoid every attack.  There tends to be a split second where they are in reach, so you'll want to Charge your attack around a corner, and hearing his footsteps, you move forward and swing towards him.  Otherwise, use Taunt and maybe they'll want to cut you to ribbons.  Then you just allow yourself to get hit and attack them as they can't dodge.  The Heavy Knight blocks slowly, and has a long attack delay, but if you can manage it you should Parry and Counter a Skirmisher because it usually results in a death if they have already engaged in battle.  It's a quick finisher that makes the Heavy Knight more into a Samurai for that moment.  Don't try it too much if they know to just Charge their attack so as not to get Parried, however.  Then you have to absorb their attack to hit them, if they're skilled in weaving their movement and much faster.  A Viking Huscarl and Pirate Captain could even out-maneuver a Heavy Knight.
Above all, you'll want to support your team with Encourage or have some fun over the mic, and try to work together to bring down the enemy teams.  The most important thing in PVK is teamwork.  We all like to mess around and have fun, but when you want to win because the same guy has been winning the last three rounds in a row and is a total d-bag about it, all you gotta do is move in one big group and swing away.  As long as you don't get distracted or separated, you should be akin to a tank with rotating sawblades.  I'm looking at you, Vikings.  Pirates, you gotta run away.  But just long enough to come back and throw eight kegs at the Vikings and Knights who are fighting each other and desperately want to get that kill point from the guy they were just fighting, so they'll let you throw the keg and try to jump away at the last second. But you won't let that happen.  You wait til the wick of the keg is just barely sticking out, one second away from exploding, and you run forward, jump and throw it slightly up so as to fall in the middle of the most fighters in proximity to the keg's explosion, and you in one instant take 4 kills for you and your team.  That, or you and your teammates kegs end up littering the battlefield and clearing everyone out in turn.  Knights, your archers will want to kill a Skirmisher in two hits using one shot from the Crossbow and one shot from their Longbow.  Several archers can nail a Skirmisher if they're accurate and the skirmisher likely has their keg out and moves slower.  Archers, you still do the most damage with your Crossbow and Longbow, so you should try to be like Legolas and shoot people point blank if they get too close.  You can learn to utilize your Shortsword in time, but as it's shorter and weaker than other light weapons, it should be taken into consideration you'll have to work harder to kill with that than as any other class.  Unless the enemy has low health, using this is only for advanced players.  Much like the Sharpshooter's knife or the Captain's hook and fist. Though I would say the Shortsword isn't half bad, either.  It's fun to play Archer with Shortsword because the enemy tends to expect an easy kill.  You can avoid their hits (you'd better) and weaken them, then do a ton of damage with a point-blank Crossbow bolt and usually finish them then.  There's many ways to play, and I could go on.
Most importantly, the gameplay is innovative and has the most control out of any other game.  I look forward to future updates, but I also hope more developers see the potential in this style of gameplay.  The dev team deserves to be picked up and paid to create.

As the developers have stated they made hotline miami 2 to the people that have already finished hotline miami 1. For that reason game is made harder (partially in a bad way) and plot only makes sense if you know the events in the orginal hotline. Basic idea is the same but this game feels enormously different than the predecessor. In this review I try to unlock why.
Masks are better balanced than in hotline miami 1 and almost all of them are useful. Masks also now dramatically alters your playing style as some forbids you to use guns or gives you two characters to control at once for example. There are usually  list of 3-5 masks to choose per act.
Locations are now more varied and you will be slaughtering on a harbor, prison, subway, jungle, etc. Enemies have been also spiced up and some can only be killed by a gun, others only goes down with melee weapons. Game also introduces communist soldiers, columbian cartel, random thug gang, and miami pd to fight with along the mafia suits from hotline miami 1.
Areas are now hugh in size and very open. This is the main problem as enemies can see way more far then you and you are shot constantly offscreen. In hotline miami 1 you could finish every map without ever stopped moving, just butchering everything came on your way. That is the soul of hotline miami and fit the game so damn well. In hotline miami 2 you just can't do it. You have to advance more cautiously, taking cover behind walls from time to time and "lure" enemies to a killzone. Playing this kind of a game is just so much less fun that way.
Story in hotline miami 2 is way too over ambitious and ends up being a mess. There are multiple timelines and a bunch of people you are following through. Dialogue is probably made intentionally poor as these developers surely have a wicked humor but I didn't find the plot interesting even when I figured it all out. There are just way too many meaningless text screens and nobody bought this game for the story.
Game is somewhat slow-paced now. Shotguns take more time to reload, melee finishes takes forever if not wearing a mask specialized for fast executions. Damn even main menu and acts takes more time to start.
I recomend getting hotline miami 1 first as it's simply the best one. If you find that entertaining and left hungry for more, get this one.

The perfect example of why more =/= better in video games.
Where the first game was a tightly designed masterpiece this game is bloated and full of hundreds of little annoyances that really ruin an experience so reliant on repeatedly doing the same thing to win. Poor level design (♥♥♥♥ing windows), enemies shooting from off your screen, inconsistent AI reactions and patrols (normally a great feature in games but not here), randomised AI weapons and occasional glitches really ♥♥♥♥ing annoy you when they get you killed cheaply during an otherwise fine run. It's also much more likely to limit your options if you take the wrong weapon (i.e. not a gun) with you through to the next level's start and in general the game is a lot more limiting in terms of playstyles than the first.
Having larger levels hurts in general since you'll be losing more if you die and really just results in boredom. It also makes hunting down that one remaining enemy before your combo dies a common experience contributing to the 'only one right way to do a level' issue
the general slow feeling of the game. Indeed the first game's addictive and fast, brutal combat is now just a slow trial and error memorisation game where 1/10 tries will be ended by something largely outside of your control like the ai acting incorrectly. I'm all for difficult games but they need to be challenging, not frustrating.
Jumping between characters out of order might have made for unique storytelling but in terms of gameplay it's ♥♥♥♥ing annoying to swap from one set of abilities to another and back again repeatedly. Frankly the game also feels a little long in a bad way with lots of the earlier levels being quite samey. This isn't a huge issue, I suppose, and is probably better than it being too short but the game is still introducing new enemy types and characters with new gameplay styles (13 in total, not counting masks) in the 20th ♥♥♥♥ing level. Hard mode helps a little but isn't an option for your first time and makes the game even more frustrating by ♥♥♥♥ing with the level design and weapons.
On the subject of the story specifically it wasn't terrible by any means (other than the ending...) but it wasn't worth the effort of piecing together the timeline of the various levels. I personally preferred the original game's approach of limited exposition and showing over telling also. Here we just have a ♥♥♥♥ton of characters dumped into the game who are introduced and eventually dropped with no real purpose or overall plot. If we're going to have a story that so often gets in the way of gameplay and pacing it should at least be a ♥♥♥♥ing good one.
In theory there's more replayability here as not only can you try for top scores on each level but also play the game through again on hard mode and have a ♥♥♥♥ton of different playstyles available. In practice I doubt I'll bother playing it through more than once on each mode while I still play the original game through now and again after 100%ing it. Part of this stems from the problems with hard mode. While it's good that the developers didn't just throw more enemies in and call it a day there are cases where levels are nearly uncompleteable with the wrong weapon (and god help you if the RNG gives guards the wrong weapons too).
I'd probably still recommend picking it up cheaply and playing it through at least once and it certainly isn't all bad. There are few games of this style and fewer yet worth playing at all and had this game come before the first one I'd probably be a lot more impressed. The soundtrack is good and the art style is fine though one level at least is annoyingly dark to the degree of hurting gameplay (maybe an intentional choice but difficulty for the sake of difficulty is again a poor decision). The game just needed to be more focussed to be truly classic like the first.

I never went in to this game thinking it would be scary, so I was never let down by that. Having said that, the game is amazing. Graphically, it's beautiful, and the music is quite good. Gameplay is great, and a lot like a souped up RE4, but that's not a bad thing, at least to me. Another complaint I hear is that the story isn't very good, but man oh man, the story is fantastic! It's explained through the game, and by use of collectables found through-out the game. Most of it is explained, except for the things which will be covered in the DLC, but you have to pay attention to all the dialogue if you want to know what's going on. Great control, great music, great graphics, and one of the few games on Steam that I've felt a desire to complete wholly. I would recommend this game to anyone who likes survival horror, RPG style stories, and the RE series. Runner up to my game of the year, 2014.
Edit: The Assignment DLC. Fantastic. I loved how the main focus was stealth, and sneakiness. It really gave the DLC a creepier feel to it. Some of those shadow puzzles were difficult for me as my eyes are awful, but I got past them with time. I didn't have high hopes for this as I wasn't too keen on Kidman, but it was a cool experience to play as her. The Kurayami mode was incredibly frustrating for me, as I stated before my eyes are awful as it is. I died so much on this, but that was to be expected. It was a great challenge, and though I didn't really enjoy Kurayami mode, it was different, and I can appreciate that. Took me about 10 hours to complete all the achievements, and I had a fun time for the most part. I really enjoyed seeing things that were happening at the same time the main game was happening, and also where certain areas of the world came from as they were established as not from the main characters minds. It was definitely worth the time, and, in my opinion, was a fantastic DLC.
Edit: The Consequence DLC. Quite great, though not as good as the first one, imo. The main focus was still stealth, but there were some gun parts thrown in, and I can see why. No where near as many puzzles, though the little collectable hints were a little tricky to find at times. Kurayami mode was even more aggravating this time, but I didn't die nearly as many times as I did on it in the first DLC. Took me about eight hours this time to finish the achievements, but it was pretty fun. There were some great achievements this time too. Well worth getting.
Edit: The Executioner DLC: By far it's the worst yet. It offers a little story, but is basically a boss rush mode that you end up having to grind for coins to upgrade your weapons, and skills. The maps are boring, and unimaginative, and the waves of mobs are boring as well. You'd think playing as the Keeper would be great, but instead it's... yep boring. It takes less than an hour to get through once, a few new things open, about the same time to get through it again. After that... what's the point? Nothing changes, it remains the same, and it's not fun at all. I expected more out of the final DLC, but it's a disappointment, and instead. What a waste.

The Evil Within.
Shinji Mikami, the creator Resident Evil and Vanquish and more,
and now The Evil Within. Does this game live up to his legacy,
or will this be a game soon forgotten?
---ABOUT---
You play as veteran police detective Sebastian Castellanos.
We've been given the task of investigating the scene of a
gruesome mass murder at Beacon Mental Hospital.
You arrive together with Detective Julie Kidman and your
partner Joseph Oda.
You soon figure out that, besides the gruesome mass murder,
not everything is as it should be.
---REVIEW---
Now this game has gotten a lot of love and hate.
This is my opinion, as non-biased as I can get it.
When it comes to the graphics, this game is both horrible,
and beautiful, as this game runs id's Tech 5 engine.
Character textures, enemies, buildings, objects and furnitures,
look really good. In the beginning scene of the game, it's
raining, and you can see how each droplet of rain hit
their uniform and slowly getting soaked. Some of the
terrain and scenery looks stunning.
But as with games running
the id Tech 4-5 engine, they do take a major hit when it
comes to performance, terrain/environmental and structural
textures. The textures simply are washed out, blurry and low-res,
and because of the megatextures, you can see huge slow texture pop-in
when turning around, instantly breaking your immersion in this game,
reminding you all the time that this is just a program.
And as many has been reporting, including myself, games running
id Tech 5 engine has performance issues.
The graphics manages to impress me from time to time, but
the sad part is that the Tech 5 engine, really isn't a graphically
impressive engine, and this game would have done a lot better
if they'd gone for a different engine.
Looking away from the technical aspect of the graphics,
the game is mostly designed well. The enemies has alot of different
texture models, there's a good number of different enemies and
differently themed areas, everything from isolated villages,
urban cities to hospitals, you'll see new stuff and areas frequently,
as the world you play in, is fractured and distorted.
Unfortunately, some of the areas ain't as fun and exciting as others,
the industrial hospital themed areas which are used the most,
are fun to begin with, but after a while you get tired of these places,
as they are all similar, there's no big difference, it'll fell like you're
doing the same places over and over again.
The isolated village areas, one of the first areas you'll visit in this game,
was awesome, they were both creepy and cool, only sad part is
they're hardly ever used after the beginning.
The enemies in this game are ugly as ♥♥♥♥, in a good way.
They seem kinda like Resident Evil zombies mixed with
Silent Hill, actually the entire game feels like a
mix between Resident Evil and Silent Hill, which is a good thing,
as they managed to do it successfully. Some of the bosses
looks really Silent Hill inspired, especially The Keeper, which
you can draw similarities with to Pyramide Head from Silent Hill.
When it comes to gameplay, this game kinda feels like
The Last of Us, where improvised combat often plays
a big role, as you can stealth kill enemies, sneak around,
pick up objects on the ground and use against enemies.
Ammo is limited, so exploiting hand-axes, bottles and
traps to take out enemies to convserve ammo is important,
as (I played this on Survival difficulty) the game don't provide
you much with ammo or health, it's barely enough to save you
from dangerous situations when you have no other way.
Pulling off headshots is critical, as ammo is rare and precious.
This creates a really good tension in this game, where the
key word in this genre of games, survival-horror, comes to play.
This game also has an interesting game mechanic, where you
can burn corpses. Why burn corpses you ask? Because unless
you've pulled off a sneak kill, or blown his head off, you can't
really be sure that it's dead. The only way to be 100% sure
something is dead, is to burn them. This makes up some interesting
situations, as you'd enter a room, see some corpses on the ground,
you're not sure they're dead or not, and you can chain-combo-burn
enemies to conserve ammo, shoot them in the leg, watch them
fall over, run towards them and throw a match, and watch them burn.
But the gameplay ain't perfect, the controlls are slightly clumsy,
and you'll probably accidentally fall of♥♥♥♥♥♥you're trying to stand on.
Your weapons, and your character, are upgradable, and you'll have
different types of weapons to choose from as the game
progresses, which is good, because the enemies becomes
harder later on in the game as they are introduced. Some enemies
wears steel masks, so pulling off headshots might be more a waste of
bullets than what you'd wish for as they often requires 3-4 shots to
break through the mask then blow the head up, so shooting them in the legs,
and burn them, is the more pleasing tactic to use for these enemies.
The story of this game, I found interesting. I was invested into
knowing about what happened, why I am in this world and
who these characters are. The most interesting character
is the Nurse, who resides inside your mental world, as it's
the safe place for you, where you can upgrade and save.
Because the story is really cryptic at the beginning, as it reveals
very little of what's actually going on, you might find
yourself coming up with theories as of what's going on,
which is always fun, and it's interesting to watch this distorted
world get even more weird, and watching your mental safe place
becoming unstable and changing. Unfortunately, the ending lacks
closure, and leaves a bunch of questions unanswered.
As for the value of this game, this game provides good
value for your money. It took me roughly 16 hours to complete
this game, that's with a lot of exploring, after finishing this game
you can either start a New Game +, where you'll have your♥♥♥♥♥♥br>carried over plus some new weapons and upgrade gel,
or you can starts a new game using one of the two new
difficulties unlocked.
---CONCLUSION---
This game does many things correctly, and it's
entertaining and gives a lot of value for your
money, but it falls short at some aspects, mainly
graphics, some gameplay mechanics (control issues),
and lack of closure and explanation of the story.
But I would still warmly recommend this game,
for those who are fans of Silent Hill and Resident Evil,
or survival-games in general.
---Score---
Graphics: 7.0/10
Audio: 7.5/10
Gameplay: 8.5/10
Story: 7.5/10
Value 9.0/10
Score: 7.9/10

The Last Federation is my favorite Arcen game. It's a combination of Drox Operative and SPAZ, except with far more complex and intricate mechanics. It's surprisingly approachable and accessible despite its depth and complexity, due in part to the excellent tutorial. (If only Paradox games had tutorials like this one, introducing concepts in a casual tone at a manageable pace...)
Like most other Arcen games, The Last Federation has myriad gameplay customization options to tweak your experience for the challenge you want. Separating combat and strategic difficulty is especially interesting; the game involves a great deal of combat, but if you don't like it much, turn down the difficulty and you can breeze through encounters to return to strategizing. The combat isn't the game's strongest aspect, but it's definitely an interesting tactical take on 2D space battles. Combat is simultaneous turn-based: you set your flight path, your weapon, and your firing mode, then you watch it take place in real time. It's similar to Frozen Synapse's turn model, except that there's a great deal more to do here. The real-time segments are the perfect length, and you can adjust their playback speed depending on how much you like Star Wars. There's a lot more complexity involved in making combat decisions, but those are the basics. You can customize your loadout (weapons and special abilities) when not in combat, adding strategic depth that requires planning: what kinds of ships will I be fighting? Lots of turrets/defenses? This complexity only grows as the game progresses and more options and possibilities open up to you, but it's never overwhelming.
The real meat of the game is the strategy you employ in creating a universal united Federation. This part of the game (all of it except the combat) takes place in real time with the option to pause at any time. Essentially, you're an independent agent in the middle of a 4X game and you have to influence the civilizations to achieve your goals. Unlike in Drox Operative, a conceptually very similar game, in The Last Federation you have significant power at your disposal. Drox Operative has you doing odd jobs for the warring civilizations, looking out only for yourself and helping or hindering the factions as it suits you. The Last Federation, however, centers diplomacy in the primary goal: you win by uniting all the surviving races. Everything you do is in order to accomplish that goal. How you do it, though, is the interesting part. You can affect nearly everything; from personally working to improve a planet's environment, to advising a race to mine their moons and brokering trade routes with the resulting resource surplus, to sabotaging a planet's infrastructure or aiding a ground invasion, you have great influence over every aspect of the 4X game playing out around you. This only scratches the surface of the intrigue and strategy involved in every playthrough. Carefully manage the balance of power, make sure the right races have the right allies (including yourself, of course), and hope no one gets too resentful of your noble quest for peace... or for supremacy.
I highly recommend The Last Federation to anyone who likes Drox Operative, SPAZ, any space 4X, or complex and replayable strategy games in general.

A Bird Story, To The Moon, and Silver Creek Falls.   What do all of them share in common?
Answer:  They're all RPG Maker titles that focus on a narrative rather than an RPG.
Do I like that?  YES!
Why do I like that?  Because I get tired of battle systems people recycle, making me bored out of my mind as I wonder "How long until I learn more about the story?"
Mysterious disappearances occur in a small town (Yeah...I know), where there are gorey crime scenes that are missing bodies.  It's up to you to find out what happened.  (It'll take you about an hour to finish if you're a slow reader like me.  If you speed run it?  Far less.
PROS:
RPG Maker game that focuses on STORY.
A nice story that grabs your attention without blinding you with battle after battle.
Achievements.  (Though both are missable)
Free.
CONS:
Typos here and there.
Recycled portraits. (Characters look identical to one another save for hairstyles and outfits)
Cliffhanger ending.  (Sorry, gotta buy chapter 2....it's one of those)
Yeah, I think it's clear.   The cons this time are very minor.  Check it out if you have a spare hour.  Of course, it's nothing stellar.
6/10  (Not too shabby)
